structure:Code.common:Description: Value expressed as a percentage of potential GDP.

structure:Code.common:Name: Percent of potential GDP in nominal national currency, percent of GDP
structure:Code.common:Description: Represents potential GDP in nominal national currency, expressed as a percentage of GDP.

structure:Code.common:Name: Percent of quota
structure:Code.common:Description: Refers to the percent of IMF Quota utilized or represented.

structure:Code.common:Name: Percent of the regional groups
structure:Code.common:Description: Metric expressing the share or proportion of a specific variable attributed to different regional groupings of countries.

structure:Code.common:Name: Percent of total
structure:Code.common:Description: The proportion or share that a specific value or category represents within a larger whole.

structure:Code.common:Name: Percent of total allocated foreign exchange reserves
structure:Code.common:Description: The percent of total allocated foreign exchange reserves refers to the proportion of a country's or institution's official foreign currency holdings that are held in a specific currency. This is often used to analyze the currency composition of foreign exchange reserves and assess the diversification of these holdings.

structure:Code.common:Name: Percent of total external debt
structure:Code.common:Description: The total amount of a country's external debt (owed to foreign lenders), expressed as a percentage of its GDP.

structure:Code.common:Name: Percent of total nonfuel
structure:Code.common:Description: The share of a specific item or category within the total amount of that item or category, excluding any components related to fuel or energy.

structure:Code.common:Name: Percent of total outlays
structure:Code.common:Description: The share of a specific expenditure item or category within the total amount of all outlays or expenditures.

structure:Code.common:Name: Percent of world
structure:Code.common:Description: The share of a particular indicator or variable that a specific country or region represents in the global total.

structure:Code.common:Name: Percent of world aggregate, multi-year average
structure:Code.common:Description: Average share of a particular indicator or variable that a specific country or region represents in the global total over multiple years.

structure:Code.common:Name: Percent of world excluding Euro partners, multi-year average
structure:Code.common:Description: Average share of a particular indicator or variable that a specific country or region represents in the global total, excluding Eurozone countries.

structure:Code.common:Name: Percent per annum
structure:Code.common:Description: Expresses an annual rate or percentage, often used in financial contexts.

structure:Code.common:Name: End-of-period (EoP), percent per annum
structure:Code.common:Description: Annual rate of change applied at the end of a period, such as a month or quarter.

structure:Code.common:Name: Period average
structure:Code.common:Description: This refers to the arithmetic mean (average) value of a data series calculated over a specified period, such as a month, quarter, or year. It provides a representative value for the entire period, smoothing out any short-term fluctuations.

structure:Code.common:Name: Period average, calendar basis
structure:Code.common:Description: The average value of a data series over a specific period within a calendar year, such as a month, quarter, or a custom period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Period average, index
structure:Code.common:Description: The period average index refers to the mean value of an index (e.g., price index, exchange rate index) calculated over a specific period of time, such as a month, quarter, or year. This average is calculated by summing the index values for each individual time point within the specified period and then dividing by the number of observations.

structure:Code.common:Name: Period average, index, weighted average of the partner countries' data weighted by the partner countries' shares in reporting country's exports
structure:Code.common:Description: The average value of an index (e.g., price index, exchange rate index) for a group of a country's trading partners over a specific period, where the index values for each partner are weighted by their respective shares in the reporting country's total exports. This gives more weight to the index values of countries that are more important export destinations.

structure:Code.common:Name: Period average, index, weighted average of the partner countries' data weighted by the partner countries' shares in reporting country's imports
structure:Code.common:Description: The average value of an index (e.g., price index, exchange rate index) for a group of a country's trading partners over a specific period, where the index values for each partner are weighted by their respective shares in the reporting country's total imports. This gives more weight to the index values of countries that are more important trading partners.

structure:Code.common:Name: Period average, index, weighted by exports
structure:Code.common:Description: It is the average value of an index over a specific period, where the index itself is constructed by weighting different export categories according to their importance. This gives more weight to the export categories that are more significant in the country's overall export structure.

structure:Code.common:Name: Period average, index, weighted by imports
structure:Code.common:Description: Period average, index weighted by imports is the mean value of an index (e.g., price index, exchange rate index) for a group of a country's trading partners over a specific period, where the index values for each partner are weighted by their respective shares in the reporting country's total imports.

structure:Code.common:Name: Period average, index, Year-over-year (YOY) percent change
structure:Code.common:Description: The percentage change in the average value of an index over two consecutive years. This provides a measure of how the average relative value (compared to the base period) has changed over time.

structure:Code.common:Name: Period average, median, percent change
structure:Code.common:Description: This refers to the percentage change in the median value of a dataset over a specific period, compared to the median value of a reference period or a baseline value. The median is the middle value in a dataset when the values are arranged in ascending or descending order. This measure is less sensitive to outliers than the mean and provides a robust measure of the central tendency of the data.

structure:Code.common:Name: Period average, percent change
structure:Code.common:Description: This refers to the percentage change in the average value of a dataset over a specific period compared to a reference value, which is often the average value of a previous period or a baseline value.

structure:Code.common:Name: Period average, percent change, impact
structure:Code.common:Description: This refers to the percentage change in the average value of a dataset over a specific period compared to a reference value, along with an assessment of the impact or significance of this change. The impact might be evaluated in terms of its economic, social, or environmental consequences.

structure:Code.common:Name: Period average, percent difference from baseline (FSGM scenario)
structure:Code.common:Description: In a Financial Sector General Model (FSGM) scenario, this refers to the percentage difference in a specific variable or outcome between a baseline scenario (often a "business as usual" scenario) and a stress-test scenario (e.g., a severe economic downturn). This is used to assess the impact of different economic conditions or policy changes on the financial sector.

structure:Code.common:Name: Period average, rate
structure:Code.common:Description: The average value of a rate (e.g., interest rate, exchange rate) over a specific period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Percent Change, Period over period, End of Period
structure:Code.common:Description: Percent change between data points at the end of two consecutive periods.

structure:Code.common:Name: Percent Change, Period over period, Period Average
structure:Code.common:Description: Average percentage change of the data series over a defined period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Period-over-preceding period percent change
structure:Code.common:Description: Represents the percentage change between the current period and the one immediately preceding it.

structure:Code.common:Name: Pre-EURO, end-of-period (EoP)
structure:Code.common:Description: The value of a variable at the end of a specific period before the introduction of the Euro as a currency. This is often used for historical data analysis in European countries that adopted the Euro, allowing for comparisons of economic indicators before and after the currency transition.

structure:Code.common:Name: Pre-EURO, period average
structure:Code.common:Description: The average value of a variable over a specific period before the introduction of the Euro as a currency. This is often used for historical data analysis in European countries that adopted the Euro, allowing for comparisons of economic indicators before and after the currency transition.

structure:Code.common:Name: Previous period (PP)
structure:Code.common:Description: Refers to the time period immediately preceding the current period being analyzed. Typically used together with Percent and Percent Change.

structure:Code.common:Name: Proportion of domestic budget funded by domestic taxes
structure:Code.common:Description: This refers to the percentage of a government's budget that is financed through taxes collected within the country. This excludes other sources of government revenue, such as foreign aid, borrowing, or income from state-owned enterprises. A higher proportion indicates greater self-reliance and less dependence on external financing.

structure:Code.common:Name: Proportion of total government spending
structure:Code.common:Description: Share of a specific variable in total government spending.

structure:Code.common:Name: Purchasing power parity (PPP)
structure:Code.common:Description: Rates of currency conversion that equalize purchasing power by eliminating price level differences between countries.

structure:Code.common:Name: Purchasing power parity (PPP) international dollar
structure:Code.common:Description: Rates of currency conversion that equalize purchasing power by eliminating price level differences between countries.

structure:Code.common:Name: Purchasing power parity (PPP) international dollar, percent of regional groups GDP
structure:Code.common:Description: Contribution of a region to a group's GDP, adjusted for purchasing power parity

structure:Code.common:Name: Purchasing power parity (PPP) international dollar, percent of world GDP
structure:Code.common:Description: Share of global GDP attributed to a country, adjusted for purchasing power parity.

structure:Code.common:Name: Per capita, Purchasing power parity (PPP), percent change
structure:Code.common:Description: Rate of change in the average purchasing power per person in a country over a specific period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Per capita, Purchasing power parity (PPP), year-over-year (YOY) percent change
structure:Code.common:Description: Percentage change in average value per capita, adjusted for purchasing power parity, over two consecutive years.

structure:Code.common:Name: Purchasing power parity (PPP) weighted
structure:Code.common:Description: PPP-adjusted metrics to make accurate economic comparisons between countries by considering price levels of a basket of goods and services.

structure:Code.common:Name: Purchasing power parity (PPP), percent change
structure:Code.common:Description: Rate at which the relative purchasing power of two currencies changes over time.

structure:Code.common:Name: Quarter-over-quarter percent change, annualized index
structure:Code.common:Description: Annualized QOQ percent change of a specific index.

structure:Code.common:Name: QOQ percent change, period average index, annualized
structure:Code.common:Description: Annualized QOQ percent change of an index, smoothed over a certain period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Quarter-over-quarter percent change, annualized
structure:Code.common:Description: QOQ percent change projected forward as if it were to continue for a full year.

structure:Code.common:Name: End-of-period (EoP), Quarter-over-quarter percent change
structure:Code.common:Description: Percent change between data points at the end of two consecutive quarters.

structure:Code.common:Name: Period average, annualized, Quarter-over-quarter percent change
structure:Code.common:Description: Annualized QOQ percent change averaged over a defined period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Rare earth carbonate REO 42-45 Dom
structure:Code.common:Description: Specific rare earth carbonate material with a defined range of Rare Earth Oxide (REO) content.

structure:Code.common:Name: Ratio of GDP from preceding period, GDP market exchange rates weighted aggregate
structure:Code.common:Description: Ratio of GDP from the previous period adjusted for market exchange rates, weighted by aggregate.

structure:Code.common:Name: Ratio of GDP from previous period
structure:Code.common:Description: The ratio of GDP from the preceding period is a measure of the percentage change in a country's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) compared to the previous period. This period can be a month, quarter, or year, depending on the frequency of the GDP data.

structure:Code.common:Name: Ratio of GDP from previous period, GDP market exchange rates weighted aggregate
structure:Code.common:Description: Calculation comparing the current combined GDP of countries to their combined GDP from a previous period, weighted by market exchange rates.

structure:Code.common:Name: Ratio of GDP from previous period, percent change
structure:Code.common:Description: The "Ratio of GDP from the previous period, percent change" is more commonly known as the GDP growth rate. It measures the percentage change in a country's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) over a specific period, usually compared to the previous quarter or year.

structure:Code.common:Name: Ratio of monetary base to broad money
structure:Code.common:Description: Measure of how much of a country's broad money supply is supported by the central bank's monetary base.

structure:Code.common:Name: Ratio of monetary base to broad money, percent per annum
structure:Code.common:Description: Annual rate of the ratio of monetary base to broad money, often tracked over time.

structure:Code.common:Name: Ratio of net transfers to own revenue
structure:Code.common:Description: Proportion of a government's net transfers relative to its own revenue.

structure:Code.common:Name: Ratio of net transfers to own spending
structure:Code.common:Description: Ratio comparing a government's net transfers to its total spending.

structure:Code.common:Name: Ratio of own revenue to own spending
structure:Code.common:Description: Ratio comparing a government's own revenue to its total spending.

structure:Code.common:Name: Ratio of own revenues to general government revenues
structure:Code.common:Description: Comparison of specific level government revenue to total revenue of all levels of government.

structure:Code.common:Name: Ratio of own spending to general government spending
structure:Code.common:Description: Comparison of specific level government spending to total spending of all levels of government.

structure:Code.common:Name: Ratio of total reserves minus gold to imports (CIF)
structure:Code.common:Description: Measure of a country's financial reserves (excluding gold) relative to its imports (cost, insurance, freight).

structure:Code.common:Name: Ratio of total reserves minus gold to imports CIF
structure:Code.common:Description: This ratio compares a country's total foreign exchange reserves (excluding gold) to the value of its imports, including the cost of goods, insurance, and freight (CIF).

structure:Code.common:Name: Ratio to total labor force
structure:Code.common:Description: This means that the value being presented is expressed as a proportion or percentage of the total labor force. The labor force includes all people who are either employed or actively seeking employment. This is often used to analyze labor market indicators such as unemployment rates or labor force participation rates.

structure:Code.common:Name: Ratio to total population
structure:Code.common:Description: This means that the value being presented is expressed as a proportion or percentage of the total population. This is often used for demographic or social indicators, such as poverty rates or literacy rates.

structure:Code.common:Name: Ratio to US GDP deflator
structure:Code.common:Description: Metric comparing the GDP Deflator of a country or region to that of the United States.

structure:Code.common:Name: Recent fixed weighted imports to GDP
structure:Code.common:Description: Weights individual commodities in an import index based on their share of the country's GDP, using recent fixed weights.

structure:Code.common:Name: Recent rolling weighted imports to GDP
structure:Code.common:Description: Weights individual commodities in an import index based on their share of the country's GDP, using recent rolling weights.

structure:Code.common:Name: Revisions, difference to last transmission period
structure:Code.common:Description: Changes made to a previously reported data point compared to its value in the last reporting period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Rolling weighted imports to GDP
structure:Code.common:Description: Weights individual commodities in an import index based on their share of the country's GDP, using historical rolling weights.

structure:Code.common:Name: Saving ratio
structure:Code.common:Description: This measures saving relative to income, expressed as a percentage.

structure:Code.common:Name: Index referenced in SDRs
structure:Code.common:Description: An index of the value of the SDR, constructed by indexing the SDR’s value (typically against a reference currency such as the U.S. dollar, or against a fixed base) to a chosen base period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Semi-annual (half-over-half)
structure:Code.common:Description: This refers to a method of calculating interest or growth rates where the rate is applied twice a year, with each application using half of the annual rate. This is often used for bonds or other financial instruments that make semi-annual interest payments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Semi-annual (half-over-half) percent change, annualized
structure:Code.common:Description: The half-over-half percent change is the percentage change in a value from the first half of a year to the second half. The annualized half-over-half percent change projects this change forward as if it were to continue for a full year. This is a way to annualize growth rates that are measured over half-year periods.

structure:Code.common:Name: Services Export Density Index
structure:Code.common:Description: A country's likelihood to export services in the future.

structure:Code.common:Name: Services Export Path Index
structure:Code.common:Description: A service's association to other services.

structure:Code.common:Name: Services Export Revealed Comparative Advantage Index
structure:Code.common:Description: Revealed Comparative Advantage (degree of specialization) for a country to export a specific service sector.

structure:Code.common:Name: Share of exports in country's service export basket
structure:Code.common:Description: Share of exports in a country's service export basket.

structure:Code.common:Name: Share of exports in country's service export basket, 1 digit level
structure:Code.common:Description: Share of exports in a country's service export basket, 1-digit level.

structure:Code.common:Name: Share of exports in country's service export basket, 2 digit level
structure:Code.common:Description: Share of exports in a country's service export basket, 2-digit level.

structure:Code.common:Name: Share of goods exports in total exports, period average
structure:Code.common:Description: Share of goods exports in total exports, averaged over a period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Share of service exports in GDP
structure:Code.common:Description: Percent of total export of services for a country as a share of country GDP. More formally, Total Service Exports (current US$) / GDP (current US$).

structure:Code.common:Name: Share of service exports in total exports
structure:Code.common:Description: Percent of total export basket accounted by Service Exports. More formally, Total Service Exports (current US$) / Total Exports of Goods and Services (current US$).

structure:Code.common:Name: Share of service exports in total exports, period average
structure:Code.common:Description: Average annual percent of Service Exports in Regional Aggregate Total Export Basket.

structure:Code.common:Name: Share of service exports in world service exports
structure:Code.common:Description: Percent of total export basket in world service exports. More formally, Total Service Exports in Country (current US$) / Total Exports of Services Exports in World (current US$).

structure:Code.common:Name: Share of service exports in world service exports, diversity
structure:Code.common:Description: Percent of total export basket in world service exports. More formally, Total Service Exports in Country (current US$) / Total Exports of Services Exports in World (current US$).

structure:Code.common:Name: Shares
structure:Code.common:Description: Indicates a part or portion of something.

structure:Code.common:Name: Short-term debt indexed to the exchange rate
structure:Code.common:Description: Short-term debt indexed to the exchange rate refers to debt instruments with a maturity of less than one year where the principal and/or interest payments are linked to the exchange rate between two currencies.

structure:Code.common:Name: Short-term debt indexed to the exchange rate
structure:Code.common:Description: Short-term debt indexed to the exchange rate for specific measurements.

structure:Code.common:Name: Short-term domestic currency debt indexed to the exchange rate
structure:Code.common:Description: Short-term domestic currency debt indexed to the exchange rate refers to debt issued by a government or corporation in its own currency with a maturity of less than one year, where the principal and/or interest payments are linked to the exchange rate with another currency, typically a major international currency like the US dollar or the euro.

structure:Code.common:Name: Short-term domestic currency debt indexed to the exchange rate
structure:Code.common:Description: Short-term debt indexed to the exchange rate for specific measurements.

structure:Code.common:Name: Standard reference period
structure:Code.common:Description: Benchmark time frame used for comparison in statistical analyses.

structure:Code.common:Name: Terms of trade of goods
structure:Code.common:Description: The ratio of a country's export prices to its import prices for goods.

structure:Code.common:Name: Terms of trade of goods and services
structure:Code.common:Description: The ratio of a country's export prices to its import prices for both goods and services.

structure:Code.common:Name: Terms of trade of goods and services, percent change
structure:Code.common:Description: The percentage change in the terms of trade of goods and services over a specific period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Terms of trade of goods, percent change
structure:Code.common:Description: The percentage change in the terms of trade of goods over a specific period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Thai baht per kilogram
structure:Code.common:Description: Thai baht per kilogram for specific commodity or measurement.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total financial system assets
structure:Code.common:Description: Total financial system assets represent the combined value of all financial assets held within a country's financial system.

structure:Code.common:Name: Valuation of country GDP
structure:Code.common:Description: Method used to express the monetary value of a country's gross domestic product (GDP).

structure:Code.common:Name: Weight
structure:Code.common:Description: Weight refers to a numerical value assigned to each observation in a dataset to adjust its relative importance in calculations.

structure:Code.common:Name: Weighted average
structure:Code.common:Description: An average calculated by assigning weights to values based on their relative importance.

structure:Code.common:Name: Weighted average by non-fuel commodity exports
structure:Code.common:Description: A weighted average based on non-fuel commodity exports for the reporting country.

structure:Code.common:Name: Weighted average by non-fuel commodity imports
structure:Code.common:Description: A weighted average based on non-fuel commodity imports for the reporting country.

structure:Code.common:Name: Weighted average by non-fuel exports, percent change
structure:Code.common:Description: Percent change in the weighted average by non-fuel exports.

structure:Code.common:Name: Weighted average by non-fuel exports, year-over-year change
structure:Code.common:Description: Year-over-year percent change in the weighted average by non-fuel exports.

structure:Code.common:Name: Weighted average by non-fuel imports, percent change
structure:Code.common:Description: Percent change in the weighted average by non-fuel imports.

structure:Code.common:Name: Weighted average by non-fuel imports, year-over-year change
structure:Code.common:Description: Year-over-year percent change in the weighted average by non-fuel imports.

structure:Code.common:Name: Weighted average of exports
structure:Code.common:Description: A weighted average of a specific variable (e.g., inflation rate, GDP growth) for a group of a country's trading partners, where the values for each partner are weighted by their respective shares in the reporting country's total exports.

structure:Code.common:Name: Weighted average of imports
structure:Code.common:Description: A weighted average of a specific variable (e.g., inflation rate, GDP growth) for a group of a country's trading partners, where the values for each partner are weighted by their respective shares in the reporting country's total imports.

structure:Code.common:Name: Weighted average of three components (exports)
structure:Code.common:Description: A weighted average of the unit value for manufactures, oil price, and non-fuel commodity export price, weighted by the composition of exports for the reporting country.

structure:Code.common:Name: Weighted average of three components (imports)
structure:Code.common:Description: A weighted average of the unit value for manufactures, oil price, and non-fuel commodity export price, weighted by the composition of imports for the reporting country.

structure:Code.common:Name: Weighted average of three components, percent change
structure:Code.common:Description: Percent change in the weighted average for the reporting country's imports composition.

structure:Code.common:Name: Weighted average of three components, percent change
structure:Code.common:Description: Percent change in the weighted average for the reporting country's exports composition.

structure:Code.common:Name: Weighted average of three components, year-over-year change
structure:Code.common:Description: Year-over-year percent change in the weighted average for the reporting country's imports composition.

structure:Code.common:Name: Weighted average of three components, year-over-year change
structure:Code.common:Description: Year-over-year percent change in the weighted average for the reporting country's exports composition.

structure:Code.common:Name: Weighted average, over 12 periods
structure:Code.common:Description: A calculation that gives more importance or weight to certain values within a dataset of 12 time periods.

structure:Code.common:Name: Weighted by exports
structure:Code.common:Description: Concept is weighted by exports.

structure:Code.common:Name: Weighted by GDP, period average, index
structure:Code.common:Description: An index calculated as the average of values over a specific period, where each value is weighted by its corresponding GDP. This method gives more importance to periods with higher GDP in the calculation of the average. This type of index is often used to track economic trends over time, where the weights reflect the relative importance of different periods in the overall economic activity.

structure:Code.common:Name: Weighted by imports
structure:Code.common:Description: Concept is weighted by imports.

structure:Code.common:Name: Individual commodities weighted by ratio of imports to total commodity imports
structure:Code.common:Description: Weights commodities in an import index based on their share of the total value of commodity imports.

structure:Code.common:Name: Individual commodities weighted by ratio of imports to GDP
structure:Code.common:Description: Weights individual commodities in an import index based on their share of the country's GDP.

structure:Code.common:Name: Weighted kurtosis
structure:Code.common:Description: A statistical measure that quantifies the "tailenders" of a probability distribution relative to a normal distribution. In weighted kurtosis, each data point is assigned a weight that influences its contribution to the overall calculation, reflecting its relative importance.

structure:Code.common:Name: Weighted percent
structure:Code.common:Description: A percentage calculation where each component or category is assigned a weight that reflects its relative importance or contribution to the total.

structure:Code.common:Name: Weighted quartiles
structure:Code.common:Description: The division of a dataset into four equal groups based on their values, but where each value is assigned a weight. The weighted quartiles (25th, 50th, 75th percentiles) indicate the distribution of the data while taking into account the relative importance of each observation.

structure:Code.common:Name: Weighted quartiles, 1st quartile
structure:Code.common:Description: The weighted 1st quartile (Q1) is the value that divides the lowest 25% of the dataset from the remaining 75%, with the observations in the dataset weighted by the respective deposit-takers' total assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Weighted quartiles, 2nd quartile
structure:Code.common:Description: The weighted 2nd quartile (Q2) or weighted median, is the value that divides the dataset that is sorted in ascending order into two halves, with the observations in the dataset weighted by the respective deposit-takers' total assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Weighted quartiles, 3rd quartile
structure:Code.common:Description: The weighted 3rd quartile (Q3) is The value that divides the highest 25% of the dataset from the remaining 75%, with the observations in the dataset weighted by the respective deposit-takers' total assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Weighted kurtosis
structure:Code.common:Description: A combination of two statistical measures: weighted quartiles (as defined above) and weighted kurtosis. This provides a comprehensive view of both the distribution of the data and its tailenders, considering the relative importance of each data point.

structure:Code.common:Name: Weighted skewness
structure:Code.common:Description: A combination of weighted quartiles and weighted skewness. Weighted skewness measures the asymmetry of a probability distribution, taking into account the weights of individual data points. Together, these measures provide insights into the shape and distribution of data with varying levels of importance assigned to observations.

structure:Code.common:Name: Weighted standard deviation
structure:Code.common:Description: A combination of weighted quartiles and weighted standard deviation. Weighted standard deviation measures the dispersion of a dataset, considering the weights of each data point. This combination offers a comprehensive picture of the data's central tendency, dispersion, and distribution, while accounting for the relative importance of each value.

structure:Code.common:Name: Weighted skewness
structure:Code.common:Description: A statistical measure that quantifies the asymmetry of a probability distribution, taking into account the weights of individual data points. A positive skewness indicates a longer tail on the right side, while a negative skewness indicates a longer tail on the left side.

structure:Code.common:Name: Weighted standard deviation
structure:Code.common:Description: A measure of the dispersion of a dataset, where each data point is assigned a weight that reflects its relative importance. This is a variation of the standard deviation that considers the varying significance of different observations in the dataset.

structure:Code.common:Name: Weighted value
structure:Code.common:Description: The result of multiplying a data point by its corresponding weight.

structure:Code.common:Name: World aggregate
structure:Code.common:Description: The combined or total value of a particular economic indicator or variable across all countries globally. This provides a comprehensive picture of the global economic landscape.

structure:Code.common:Name: Yearly average
structure:Code.common:Description: Average value of a data series over a calendar year.

structure:Code.common:Name: End-of-period (EoP), year-over-year (YOY) per capita percent change
structure:Code.common:Description: The percentage change between the end-of-period value per capita for the current year and the end-of-period value per capita for the previous year.

structure:Code.common:Name: Year-over-year (YOY) percent change
structure:Code.common:Description: The percentage change over two consecutive years.

structure:Code.common:Name: Year-over-year (YOY) percent change weighted by exports
structure:Code.common:Description: Percentage change over two consecutive years, weighted by the export quantities for each period. This provides a measure of how the value has changed over two consecutive years, taking into account the relative importance of different products based on their export volumes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Year-over-year (YOY) percent change weighted by exports, period average
structure:Code.common:Description: The average year-on-year percentage change in a data series, weighted by the export quantities for each period. This provides a measure of how the average value has changed over two consecutive years, taking into account the relative importance of different products based on their export volumes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Year-over-year (YOY) percent change weighted by imports
structure:Code.common:Description: Percentage change over two consecutive years, weighted by the import quantities for each period. This provides a measure of how the value has changed over two consecutive years, taking into account the relative importance of different products based on their import volumes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Year-over-year (YOY) percent change weighted by imports, period average
structure:Code.common:Description: The average year-on-year percentage change in a data series, weighted by the import quantities for each period. This provides a measure of how the average value has changed over time, taking into account the relative importance of different products based on their import volumes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Year-over-year (YOY) percent change, based on market exchange rates
structure:Code.common:Description: Percentage change over two consecutive years, after adjusting the values from one currency to another using market exchange rates. This provides a measure of the change in the variable's value excluding the influence of currency fluctuations.

structure:Code.common:Name: End-of-period (EoP), Year-over-year (YOY) percent change
structure:Code.common:Description: The percent change between the data points at the end of two consecutive years.

structure:Code.common:Name: GDP market exchange rates weighed aggregate, year-over-year (YOY) percent change
structure:Code.common:Description: It refers to the percentage change in the combined GDP of multiple countries compared to the same period in the previous year. Each country's GDP is first converted to a common currency (usually US dollars) using market exchange rates, then weighted based on its economic significance, and finally aggregated. The YOY percentage change reflects the overall growth or contraction of the combined economies, considering both individual GDP changes and fluctuations in exchange rates.

structure:Code.common:Name: Year-over-year (YOY) period average
structure:Code.common:Description: The average change over two consecutive years.

structure:Code.common:Name: Year-over-year (YOY) percent change, period average
structure:Code.common:Description: The percentage change over two consecutive years in the average value of an index for the current period compared to the previous period. This provides a measure of how the average relative value (compared to the base period) has changed over two consecutive periods.

structure:Code.common:Name: Year-over-year (YOY) percent change, period average index
structure:Code.common:Description: The percentage change over two consecutive years in the average value of an index for the current period compared to the previous period. This provides a measure of how the average relative value (compared to the base period) has changed over two consecutive periods.

structure:Code.common:Name: Year-over-year (YOY) percent change, period average, seasonally adjusted (SA)
structure:Code.common:Description: The percentage change over two consecutive years between the seasonally adjusted (SA) average values for the current period and the previous period. This provides a measure of how the average value has changed over two consecutive years, excluding the influence of seasonal patterns.

structure:Code.common:Name: Year-over-year (YOY) percent change, period average, weighted average of the partner countries' data weighted by the partner countries' shares in reporting country's exports
structure:Code.common:Description: The average percentage change over two consecutive years in a specific variable for a group of a country's trading partners, weighted by their respective shares in the reporting country's total exports.

structure:Code.common:Name: Year-over-year (YOY) percent change, period average, weighted average of the partner countries' data weighted by the partner countries' shares in reporting country's imports
structure:Code.common:Description: The average percentage change over two consecutive years in a specific variable for a group of a country's trading partners, weighted by their respective shares in the reporting country's total imports.

structure:Code.common:Name: Year-over-year (YOY) percent change, weighted average of the partner countries' data weighted by the partner countries' shares in reporting country's exports
structure:Code.common:Description: The percentage change over two consecutive years in a weighted average of a specific variable for a group of a country's trading partners, where the weights are based on their respective shares in the reporting country's total exports.

structure:Code.common:Name: Year-over-year (YOY) percent change, weighted average of the partner countries' data weighted by the partner countries' shares in reporting country's imports
structure:Code.common:Description: The percentage change over two consecutive years in a weighted average of a specific variable for a group of a country's trading partners, where the weights are based on their respective shares in the reporting country's total imports.

structure:Code.common:Name: Year-to-date (YTD)
structure:Code.common:Description: The cumulative value of a particular economic indicator or variable from the beginning of the current calendar year up to the present date.

structure:Code.common:Name: Percent of quota per annum

structure:Code.common:Name: Adjusted by relative unit labor costs, Year-over-year (YOY) percent change (advanced economies only)
structure:Code.common:Description: Weighted index reflecting advanced economies, adjusted by relative unit labor costs, Year-over-year (YOY) percent change

structure:Code.common:Name: Adjusted by relative unit labor costs, percent change (advanced economies only)
structure:Code.common:Description: Weighted index reflecting advanced economies trade partners only, adjusted by relative unit labor costs, percent change

structure:Code.common:Name: Weighted by imports, period average
structure:Code.common:Description: This is used to analyze the change in import values over a specific period, where the average import value is calculated by weighting different import categories based on their relative importance. This gives more weight to the changes in import categories that are more significant in the country's overall import structure.

structure:Code.common:Name: Weighted by exports, period average
structure:Code.common:Description: This metric analyzes the change in export values over a specific period. The average export value is calculated by weighting different export categories based on their relative importance. This weighting gives more influence to changes in the more significant export categories within the country's overall export structure.

structure:Code.common:Name: Per capita, Year-over-year (YOY) percent change
structure:Code.common:Description: The percentage change between the end-of-period value per capita for the current year and the end-of-period value per capita for the previous year.

structure:Code.common:Name: Purchasing power parity (PPP) 2017
structure:Code.common:Description: This refers to the Purchasing power parity conversion factors expressed relative to the 2017 ICP benchmark year, used to convert values from national currency units into a common purchasing-power-adjusted unit, thereby equalizing price level differences across economies.

structure:Code.common:Name: GDP aggregation weight
structure:Code.common:Description: A weighting factor based on the relative size of an economy’s gross domestic product, typically expressed as its share of total GDP for a defined group, reference year, and valuation basis, and used to weight component series in the construction of aggregates or weighted averages.

structure:Code.common:Name: In weeks of imports
structure:Code.common:Description: It refers to a metric expressing a country's foreign exchange reserves (typically held by its central bank) relative to the estimated value of its imports. It indicates how many weeks of imports the country could afford if its reserves remained unchanged and its import levels were projected forward. This is a measure of a country's external liquidity and its ability to withstand shocks to its balance of payments.

structure:Code.common:Name: 6-month rolling monthly squared change
structure:Code.common:Description: Measures the volatility of a data series by calculating the squared difference between each month's value and the previous month's value, averaged over a rolling 6-month window. One unit is equivalent to one standard deviation of the standardized variable.

structure:Code.common:Description: This is a country grouping established by the World Bank's classification of countries in fragile and conflict-affected situations. The list consists of (i) countries with high levels of institutional and social fragility and (ii) countries affected by violent conflict, using indicators and thresholds assessed by the World Bank. It is updated annually and available publicly. Under the new IMF strategy for Fragile and Conflicted States (FCS), the Fund has adopted the methodology, thresholds, and criteria of the World Bank's Fragility and Conflict Situations for the IMF Fragile and Conflicted States. This is explained in the FCS Strategy Board paper: The IMF Strategy for Fragile and Conflict-Affected States (March 14, 2022, p. 21-22).

structure:Codelist.common:Name: International accounts item
structure:Codelist.common:Description: A classification of transactions in the balance of payments, such as trade in goods, services, income, and financial flows.

structure:Code.common:Name: Not applicable
structure:Code.common:Description: Not applicable.

structure:Code.common:Name: Acquisition of foreign assets
structure:Code.common:Description: The purchase or obtaining of assets located outside the domestic economy, including investments, real estate, or business entities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Scheduled amortization
structure:Code.common:Description: This refers to the planned repayments of principal on outstanding loans during a specific period

structure:Code.common:Name: Scheduled amortization, before adjustments for exceptional financing
structure:Code.common:Description: This refers to the planned repayments of principal on outstanding loans during a specific period. It excludes any adjustments made for exceptional financing, such as debt rescheduling or forgiveness.

structure:Code.common:Name: Acquisition of other nonreserve assets
structure:Code.common:Description: Purchasing assets that do not qualify as reserve assets, such as non-financial assets or financial assets not held for transaction motives or international liquidity.

structure:Code.common:Name: Balance on invisibles
structure:Code.common:Description: The net balance of transactions that do not result in the transfer of tangible goods, including services, primary income, and secondary income flows.

structure:Code.common:Name: Current account balance
structure:Code.common:Description: The current account balance is the balance of current transactions (transactions in goods and services, earned income and transfer income) between residents and non-residents. The term current account balance is used in the external accounts and is expressed from the perspective of resident units. The term current external balance is used in the national accounts and is expressed from the perspective of the non-resident units, and therefore with the opposite sign.

structure:Code.common:Name: Current account balance, excluding grants
structure:Code.common:Description: The current account balance is the balance of current transactions (transactions in goods and services, earned income and transfer income) between residents and non-residents. The term current account balance is used in the external accounts and is expressed from the perspective of resident units. The term current external balance is used in the national accounts and is expressed from the perspective of the non-resident units, and therefore with the opposite sign. It excludes grants.

structure:Code.common:Name: Classic comparative advantage
structure:Code.common:Description: A country had comparative advantage in specific service exports in 2000-04 and maintains comparative advantage in 2008-13, on average.

structure:Code.common:Name: Capital and financial account balance
structure:Code.common:Description: The combined net balance of the capital account and the financial account, showing the net flow of capital and financial transactions between residents and non-residents.

structure:Code.common:Name: Capital and financial account balance less reserve assets
structure:Code.common:Description: This measures the net flow of capital and financial transactions between a country and the rest of the world, excluding changes in the country's official reserve assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Current and capital account balance
structure:Code.common:Description: The combined balance of the current and capital accounts, reflecting the net flow of goods, services, income, and transfers, as well as capital transactions.

structure:Code.common:Name: Current transfers (receivables less payables)
structure:Code.common:Description: The net balance of current transfers into and out of a country, reflecting the difference between receivable and payable transfers.

structure:Code.common:Name: Current transfers (receivables less payables) (official)
structure:Code.common:Description: Officially recorded net current transfers, emphasizing government or formal transactions.

structure:Code.common:Name: Compensation of employees
structure:Code.common:Description: Total remuneration, in cash or in kind, payable by an enterprise to an employee in return for work done by the latter during the accounting period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Wages and salaries excluding employers' social contributions
structure:Code.common:Description: Remuneration of employees payable in cash and/or in kind, except for social contributions payable by employers.

structure:Code.common:Name: Employers social contributions
structure:Code.common:Description: Social contributions payable by employers to social security funds and other social insurance schemes, to secure social benefits for their employees.

structure:Code.common:Name: Employers actual social contributions
structure:Code.common:Description: Total contributions made by employers for social benefits for their employees, including both pension and non-pension contributions.

structure:Code.common:Name: Employers actual pension contributions
structure:Code.common:Description: Payments made by employers into pension schemes on behalf of their employees for future retirement benefits.

structure:Code.common:Name: Employers actual non-pension contributions
structure:Code.common:Description: Payments made by employers for benefits other than pensions, such as health insurance or unemployment insurance, that are not deferred to a future date.

structure:Code.common:Name: Employers imputed social contributions
structure:Code.common:Description: Contributions for social benefits attributed to employers, including both pension and non-pension, not directly paid out.

structure:Code.common:Name: Employers imputed pension contributions
structure:Code.common:Description: Contributions to pension benefits attributed to employers but not directly paid out, often representing future pension liabilities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Employers imputed non-pension contributions
structure:Code.common:Description: Contributions for non-pension benefits attributed to employers but not directly paid out, such as the value of in-kind benefits.

structure:Code.common:Name: Taxes on production and imports
structure:Code.common:Description: Compulsory, unrequited payments levied by government in respect of production or import of goods and services.

structure:Code.common:Name: Taxes on products

structure:Code.common:Description: Interest before FISIM.

structure:Code.common:Name: Interest: investment income
structure:Code.common:Description: Form of investment income or interest-like income that is receivable by the owners of certain kinds of financial assets, namely: deposits, debt securities, loans, and other accounts receivable, and some similar instruments in the case of Islamic finance, for putting the financial asset at the disposal of another institutional unit. Income on SDR holdings and allocations is also treated as interest and similar returns. By convention, lending fees on securities, gold loans, gold swaps, and crypto assets without a corresponding liability designed to act as a general medium of exchange are classified as interest and similar returns. In the external accounts, trade credit and advances are in a separate category from other accounts receivable/payable and are also included in the list of financial assets that may accrue interest and similar returns.
