structure:Codelist.common:Name: Derivation Type
structure:Codelist.common:Description: This codelist identifies the specific method used to derive a new data element or indicator from source data, such as raw data, IMF staff calculations, IMF staff estimates, or IMF staff projections.

structure:Code.common:Name: Staff estimates using group mean imputation methods
structure:Code.common:Description: Staff estimates using group mean imputation methods.

structure:Code.common:Name: Staff estimates using historical imputation methods
structure:Code.common:Description: Staff estimates using historical imputation methods.

structure:Code.common:Name: Raw data (no derivation)
structure:Code.common:Description: Non-transformed data (also called original data) refers to data in its original form, before any mathematical or statistical operations have been applied to change its values or distribution.

structure:Code.common:Name: IMF Staff calculations (derived value)
structure:Code.common:Description: Data that results from direct calculations or transformations performed on raw data by IMF staff. These calculations are usually straightforward and transparent, with the published numbers easily traceable back to the source data.

structure:Code.common:Name: IMF Staff calculations (derived from counterpart data)
structure:Code.common:Description: Data resulting from direct application of counterpart data by IMF staff to the official information reported by other countries.

structure:Code.common:Name: IMF Staff estimates
structure:Code.common:Description: Data derived through calculations or transformations on available source data, where some necessary information might be missing. In these cases, IMF staff uses estimates to fill in the gaps and produce the published numbers.

structure:Code.common:Name: IMF Staff projections
structure:Code.common:Description: Forecasts of future values for a time series, constructed using various techniques such as statistical modeling, trend analysis, and expert judgment. These projections are based on historical data, current economic conditions, and other relevant factors.

structure:Code.common:Name: Mixed-type data
structure:Code.common:Description: Data that combines both raw and derived data. This could occur when some components of a dataset are directly reported while others are calculated or estimated.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reported official data
structure:Code.common:Description: Official data reported to the IMF by country authorities without any modifications or adjustments made by IMF staff.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reported official data converted to US dollar
structure:Code.common:Description: Official data reported to the IMF by country authorities in a country's domestic currency, which IMF staff then converts to US dollars using appropriate exchange rates.

structure:Code.common:Name: Adjusted using Fund records
structure:Code.common:Description: Official data reported to the IMF by country authorities that has that have been adjusted using internal IMF records.

structure:Code.common:Name: Third party data
structure:Code.common:Description: Third party data.

structure:Codelist.common:Name: Monetary and Financial Instruments
structure:Codelist.common:Description: A classification of financial instruments used in monetary and financial statistics, including currency, deposits, loans, securities, and derivatives.

structure:Code.common:Name: Broad money
structure:Code.common:Description: Broad money is the sum of all liquid financial instruments held by money-holding sectors that are widely accepted in an economy as a medium of exchange, plus those that can be converted into a medium of exchange at short notice at, or close to, their full nominal value (2016 MFSMCG).

structure:Code.common:Name: Stock market index S&P500
structure:Code.common:Description: The S&P 500 is a stock market index that tracks the performance of 500 of the largest publicly traded companies in the United States, serving as a benchmark for the overall U.S. equity market.

structure:Code.common:Name: Benchmark stock market index
structure:Code.common:Description: A benchmark stock market index is a standard measure that tracks the performance of a specific group of stocks, serving as a reference point for evaluating the returns of investment portfolios or the overall market.

structure:Code.common:Name: Benchmark stock market index, US NASDAQ Stock Composite
structure:Code.common:Description: The NASDAQ Composite is a benchmark U.S. stock market index that tracks the performance of over 3,000 companies listed on the NASDAQ Stock Exchange

structure:Code.common:Name: Benchmark stock market index, US Dow Jones 30 Industrial Stocks
structure:Code.common:Description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) is a benchmark U.S. stock market index that tracks the performance of 30 major publicly traded companies across various industries.

structure:Code.common:Name: Stock market index Dow Jones Industrial Average
structure:Code.common:Description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) is a benchmark U.S. stock market index that tracks the performance of 30 major publicly traded companies across various industries.

structure:Code.common:Name: Consumer confidence
structure:Code.common:Description: Consumer confidence is an economic indicator that measures the degree of optimism consumers feel about the overall state of the economy and their personal financial situation.

structure:Code.common:Name: Credit to the private sector
structure:Code.common:Description: Credit to the private sector refers to the total amount of loans and financial resources provided by financial institutions to households and businesses, excluding government entities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Money supply
structure:Code.common:Description: Money supply is the total amount of money available in an economy at a specific time; there are different measures of it, in particular broad money defined above.

structure:Code.common:Name: Money policy evaluation, probability of rate change at/before next FOMC meeting
structure:Code.common:Description: Monetary policy evaluation regarding the probability of a rate change at or before the next FOMC meeting involves assessing economic indicators and market expectations to estimate whether the Federal Reserve will adjust interest rates.

structure:Code.common:Name: Narrow money
structure:Code.common:Description: The most liquid forms of money, including cash and assets that can quickly be converted to cash, such as demand deposits.

structure:Code.common:Name: Use of IMF credit and loans (IMF records)
structure:Code.common:Description: Utilization of credit and loans from the International Monetary Fund, recorded by the IMF.

structure:Code.common:Name: Financial sector support
structure:Code.common:Description: Financial sector support.

structure:Code.common:Name: Use of Fund credit
structure:Code.common:Description: Use of Fund credit.

structure:Code.common:Name: Commodities Research Bureau's futures price, index
structure:Code.common:Description: Commodities Research Bureau's futures price, index.

structure:Code.common:Name: Benchmark stock market index 1
structure:Code.common:Description: Benchmark stock market index 1.

structure:Code.common:Name: Benchmark stock market index 2
structure:Code.common:Description: Benchmark stock market index 2.

structure:Code.common:Name: Income velocity of broad money (GDP in current prices / Broad money)
structure:Code.common:Description: The rate at which broad money circulates in the economy.

structure:Codelist.common:Name: Macroeconomic and financial accounts
structure:Codelist.common:Description: A framework for organizing macroeconomic and financial data into a set of integrated accounts and tables that provide a comprehensive overview of an economy.

structure:Code.common:Name: Capital account
structure:Code.common:Description: The capital account records acquisitions and disposals of non-financial assets as a result of transactions with other units, internal bookkeeping transactions linked to production (such as changes in inventories and depreciation) and the redistribution of wealth by means of capital transfers. In the context of the external accounts, the capital account shows (a) capital transfers receivable and payable between residents and nonresidents and (b) the acquisition and disposal of nonproduced, nonfinancial assets between residents and nonresidents.

structure:Code.common:Name: Capital and financial account
structure:Code.common:Description: The capital account records acquisitions and disposals of non-financial assets as a result of transactions with other units, internal bookkeeping transactions linked to production (such as changes in inventories and depreciation) and the redistribution of wealth by means of capital transfers. In the context of the external accounts, the capital account shows (a) capital transfers receivable and payable between residents and nonresidents and (b) the acquisition and disposal of nonproduced, nonfinancial assets between residents and nonresidents. The financial account records all transactions in financial assets and liabilities. In the external accounts, only transactions between residents and non-residents are included.

structure:Code.common:Name: Current account
structure:Code.common:Description: The current account covers the transactions in goods, services, earned income and transfer income for institutional sectors and between residents and non-residents.

structure:Code.common:Name: Current, capital and financial account
structure:Code.common:Description: The current account covers the transactions in goods, services, earned income and transfer income for institutional sectors and between residents and non-residents. The capital account records acquisitions and disposals of non-financial assets as a result of transactions with other units, internal bookkeeping transactions linked to production (such as changes in inventories and depreciation) and the redistribution of wealth by means of capital transfers. In the context of the external accounts, the capital account shows (a) capital transfers receivable and payable between residents and nonresidents and (b) the acquisition and disposal of nonproduced, nonfinancial assets between residents and nonresidents. The financial account records all transactions in financial assets and liabilities. In the external accounts, only transactions between residents and non-residents are included.

structure:Code.common:Name: Financial account
structure:Code.common:Description: The financial account records all transactions in financial assets and liabilities. In the external accounts, only transactions between residents and non-residents are included.

structure:Code.common:Name: Currency composition of International Investment Position
structure:Code.common:Description: The breakdown of a country's international investment position by the currency in which the assets and liabilities are denominated.

structure:Code.common:Name: Monetary survey
structure:Code.common:Description: An aggregate financial statement that consolidates the accounts of the central bank and other depository corporations, showing the sources and uses of funds.

structure:Code.common:Name: Fund Accounts
structure:Code.common:Description: A system of accounting used by non-profit organizations and governments to track the use of funds restricted for specific purposes.

structure:Code.common:Name: International Investment Position (IIP)
structure:Code.common:Description: Statement drawn up at a particular point in time of the value of financial assets of residents of an economy that are claims on non-residents or are gold bullion held as reserve assets and of the liabilities of residents of an economy to non-residents.

structure:Code.common:Name: Allocated shares
structure:Code.common:Description: Represents shares of ownership or equity that have been formally assigned or distributed to specific individuals or entities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Statement of operations
structure:Code.common:Description: A statement summarizing the revenues, expenses, and results of operations of government over a specific period.

structure:Code.common:Name: International Investment Position (IIP) - Assets
structure:Code.common:Description: Statement drawn up at a particular point in time of the value of financial assets of residents of an economy that are claims on non-residents or are gold bullion held as reserve assets and of the liabilities of residents of an economy to non-residents.

structure:Code.common:Name: International Investment Position (IIP) - Liabilities
structure:Code.common:Description: Statement drawn up at a particular point in time of the value of financial assets of residents of an economy that are claims on non-residents or are gold bullion held as reserve assets and of the liabilities of residents of an economy to non-residents.

structure:Code.common:Name: Statement of other economic flows
structure:Code.common:Description: Captures changes in assets and liabilities that are not due to transactions, such as revaluations, write-offs, and other adjustments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total
structure:Code.common:Description: The sum of all relevant components or categories.

structure:Code.common:Name: Balance Sheet Account
structure:Code.common:Description: The balance sheet account records stocks of nonfinancial assets, financial assets and liabilities.

structure:Code.common:Name: GDP by income approach
structure:Code.common:Description: Total income earned through the production of goods and services in the economy, consisting of remuneration of employees plus gross operating surplus plus gross mixed incomes plus taxes less subsidies on both production and imports

structure:Code.common:Name: GDP by expenditure approach
structure:Code.common:Description: The value of total output less total intermediate consumption plus any taxes less subsidies on products not already included in the value of output.

structure:Code.common:Name: GDP by production approach
structure:Code.common:Description: Total value added (total output less total intermediate goods used to produce the output) from the production of goods and services in an economic territory during an accounting period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Concentration and distribution measures
structure:Code.common:Description: Statistical measures used to assess the concentration of financial assets or economic activities and their distribution across different sectors or entities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Additional Financial Soundness Indicators
structure:Code.common:Description: Supplementary indicators used to assess the stability and soundness of the financial system, beyond the core set of financial soundness indicators.

structure:Code.common:Name: Additional series - Financial Soundness Indicators
structure:Code.common:Description: Additional data series that provide further insights into the financial soundness of institutions or the financial system as a whole.

structure:Code.common:Name: Balance sheets and income statements
structure:Code.common:Description: Financial statements that provide a snapshot of an entity's financial position (balance sheet) and its performance over a period (income statement).

structure:Code.common:Name: Core Financial Soundness Indicators
structure:Code.common:Description: Key indicators used to assess the financial health and stability of financial institutions, such as capital adequacy, asset quality, earnings, and liquidity.

structure:Code.common:Name: Distribution measures
structure:Code.common:Description: Measures used to analyze the distribution of income, wealth, or other economic variables within a population or sector.

structure:Code.common:Name: Encouraged Financial Soundness Indicators
structure:Code.common:Description: Indicators recommended for use in addition to the core financial soundness indicators to provide a more comprehensive assessment of financial stability.

structure:Code.common:Name: Income and expense statement (FSI)
structure:Code.common:Description: A financial statement that shows the revenues, expenses, and profits or losses over a specific period, also known as an income statement or profit and loss statement.

structure:Code.common:Name: Memorandum series: additional series
structure:Code.common:Description: Supplementary data series included in financial or economic reports to provide additional context or insights.

structure:Code.common:Name: Memorandum series: balance sheet-related series
structure:Code.common:Description: Supplementary data series related to balance sheet items, providing additional detail or context.

structure:Code.common:Name: Memorandum series: income statement-related series
structure:Code.common:Description: Supplementary data series related to income statement items, providing additional detail or context.

structure:Code.common:Name: Memorandum series
structure:Code.common:Description: A set of supplementary data series included in financial or economic reports to enhance understanding and analysis.

structure:Code.common:Name: Memorandum series: supervisory-based series
structure:Code.common:Description: Supplementary data series based on information collected by supervisory authorities, often related to regulatory compliance and oversight.

structure:Code.common:Name: Government expenditures by function
structure:Code.common:Description: Government expenditures by function.

structure:Code.common:Name: Statement of sources and uses of cash
structure:Code.common:Description: A summary of the government’s actual cash inflows (receipts) and outflows (payments) over a given period, showing how cash is generated, spent, and how the residual affects the government’s cash balance.

structure:Code.common:Name: Balance Sheet (GFS)
structure:Code.common:Description: A snapshot of the government’s stock of assets and liabilities at a particular point in time, including the resulting net worth (assets minus liabilities).

structure:Code.common:Name: Balance Sheet (FSI)
structure:Code.common:Description: Balance sheet records stocks of nonfinancial assets, financial assets and liabilities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Stocks and flows by counterparty
structure:Code.common:Description: Stocks and Flows of assets and liabilities by counterparty.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net lending (+) / net borrowing (-)
structure:Code.common:Description: Net lending is the difference between changes in net worth due to saving and capital transfers and net acquisitions of non-financial assets (acquisitions less disposals of non-financial assets, less depreciation). If the amount is negative, it represents net borrowing. In the external accounts, it represents the sum of the balances on the current and capital accounts. This is conceptually equal to the net balance of the financial account. If the balance is positive, it is called net lending, implying that in net terms, the economy supplies funds to the rest of the world. If the balance is negative, it is called net borrowing, implying that in net terms, the economy receives funds from the rest of the world.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other investment, Special Drawing Rights (SDRs): allocations, Adjusted using IMF accounting records
structure:Code.common:Description: Other investment represents a residual investment category that includes positions and transactions other than those included in direct investment, portfolio investment, financial derivatives and employee stock options, and reserve assets. SDR allocations are reserve assets created by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and allocated to its member countries to supplement existing reserve assets. Special Drawing Rights (SDRs) are international reserve assets that the IMF allocates to its members as a form of supplementary liquidity. These allocations are based on each member country's IMF quota and are intended to provide additional liquidity and support to the global financial system. This indicator has been adjusted using IMF accounting records received from the IMF Finance Department.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserve assets, Special Drawing Rights (SDRs), Adjusted using IMF accounting records

structure:Code.common:Name: Travel services, Both Business and Personal Travel, Other Services
structure:Code.common:Description: Travel services, Both Business and Personal Travel, Other Services.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other investment, Special Drawing Rights (SDRs)
structure:Code.common:Description: Other investment represents a residual investment category that includes positions and transactions other than those included in direct investment, portfolio investment, financial derivatives and employee stock options, and reserve assets. Reserve assets created by the International Monetary Fund and allocated to its members to supplement existing reserve assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserve assets, Special Drawing Rights (SDRs)
structure:Code.common:Description: External assets that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. Reserve assets created by the International Monetary Fund and allocated to its members to supplement existing reserve assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserve assets, Monetary gold: gold bullion
structure:Code.common:Description: External assets that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. Gold in the form of bars or ingots held as a reserve asset.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserve assets, Monetary gold: of which gold under swap for cash collateral
structure:Code.common:Description: External assets that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. Portion of monetary gold that is held under swap agreements for cash collateral.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserve assets, Unallocated gold accounts
structure:Code.common:Description: External assets that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. Unallocated gold accounts.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserve assets, Financial derivatives
structure:Code.common:Description: External assets that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. Negotiable financial instruments linked to another specific financial instrument, indicator, or commodity, through which specific risks (e.g., interest rate risk, foreign exchange risk, equity and commodity price risk, credit risk) can be traded in their own right in financial markets. Financial instruments whose value is derived from the performance of underlying assets, indexes, or interest rates.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserve assets, Currency and deposits
structure:Code.common:Description: External assets that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. Monetary assets held in the form of currency or in deposit accounts with financial institutions.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserve assets, Debt securities
structure:Code.common:Description: External assets that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. Tradable financial instruments representing a debt, such as bonds and notes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Investment income on other investment income
structure:Code.common:Description: Investment income

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserves and Related items
structure:Code.common:Description: Reserves and Related items.

structure:Code.common:Name: Financial account balance, excluding reserves and related items
structure:Code.common:Description: Financial account balance, excluding reserves and related items.

structure:Code.common:Name: Financial account balance (assets less liabilities), Adjusted using IMF accounting records
structure:Code.common:Description: The financial account balance reflects the difference in transactions in financial assets and liabilities in the accounting period. In the external accounts, only transactions between residents and non-residents are included. This indicator has been adjusted using IMF accounting records received from the IMF Finance Department.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents total
structure:Code.common:Description: The aggregate notional value of all foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents total
structure:Code.common:Description: The aggregate notional value of all foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents total, Other Sectors (BPM6)
structure:Code.common:Description: The aggregate notional value of all foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. Sectors excluding deposit-taking corporations and general government.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents, Central bank
structure:Code.common:Description: The total notional value of foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. The monetary authority of a country responsible for issuing currency and regulating the banking system.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents, Other sectors: Other
structure:Code.common:Description: The total notional value of foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. Miscellaneous or residual sectors not classified elsewhere.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents, General government
structure:Code.common:Description: The total notional value of foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. Central, state, and local governments, including their agencies and departments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents, Central bank
structure:Code.common:Description: The total notional value of foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. The monetary authority of a country responsible for issuing currency and regulating the banking system.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents total, Other Sectors (BPM6)
structure:Code.common:Description: The aggregate notional value of all foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. Sectors excluding deposit-taking corporations and general government.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents, Other financial corporations
structure:Code.common:Description: The total notional value of foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. Financial corporations not classified under other specific financial sub-sectors.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents, General government
structure:Code.common:Description: The total notional value of foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. Central, state, and local governments, including their agencies and departments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents, Other sectors: Other
structure:Code.common:Description: The total notional value of foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. Miscellaneous or residual sectors not classified elsewhere.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents, Other financial corporations
structure:Code.common:Description: The total notional value of foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. Financial corporations not classified under other specific financial sub-sectors.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents, Deposit taking corporations, except the Central Bank
structure:Code.common:Description: The total notional value of foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. Financial corporations accepting deposits, except for the central bank.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents, Deposit taking corporations, except the Central Bank
structure:Code.common:Description: The total notional value of foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. Financial corporations accepting deposits, except for the central bank.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserve assets, Currency and deposits, Claims on monetary authorities
structure:Code.common:Description: External assets that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. Monetary assets held in the form of currency or in deposit accounts with financial institutions, claims on monetary authorities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserve assets, Currency and deposits, Claims on other entities
structure:Code.common:Description: External assets that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. Monetary assets held in the form of currency or in deposit accounts with financial institutions, claims on other entities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserve assets, Reserve position in the IMF
structure:Code.common:Description: External assets that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. Reserve position in the IMF is the sum of a member’s reserve tranche position and any indebtedness of the IMF in the General Resources Account (GRA) that is readily available to the member to meet balance of payments financing needs.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total liabilities, Adjusted using IMF accounting records
structure:Code.common:Description: The total value of all financial obligations owed by an entity to other entities. These obligations represent claims held by others against the entity and may include loans, debt securities, accounts payable, and other forms of debt. This indicator has been adjusted using IMF accounting records received from the IMF Finance Department.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total assets, Adjusted using IMF accounting records
structure:Code.common:Description: Total assets This indicator has been adjusted using IMF accounting records received from the IMF Finance Department.

structure:Code.common:Name: Debt liabilities to nonresidents
structure:Code.common:Description: Liabilities owed to nonresidents in the form of debt.

structure:Code.common:Name: Debt liabilities to nonresidents, Short-term
structure:Code.common:Description: Liabilities owed to nonresidents in the form of debt. Original contract stipulates that payment is due in one year or less or payable on demand (referred to as short-term maturity).

structure:Code.common:Name: Debt liabilities to nonresidents, Other Sectors (BPM6), Short-term
structure:Code.common:Description: Liabilities owed to nonresidents in the form of debt. Sectors excluding deposit-taking corporations and general government. Original contract stipulates that payment is due in one year or less or payable on demand (referred to as short-term maturity).

structure:Code.common:Name: Debt liabilities to nonresidents, Other Sectors (BPM6)
structure:Code.common:Description: Liabilities owed to nonresidents in the form of debt. Sectors excluding deposit-taking corporations and general government.

structure:Code.common:Name: Debt claims on nonresidents, Other Sectors (BPM6)
structure:Code.common:Description: Claims for debt owed by nonresidents. Sectors excluding deposit-taking corporations and general government.

structure:Code.common:Name: Debt claims on nonresidents, Other Sectors (BPM6), Short-term
structure:Code.common:Description: Claims for debt owed by nonresidents. Sectors excluding deposit-taking corporations and general government. Original contract stipulates that payment is due in one year or less or payable on demand (referred to as short-term maturity).

structure:Code.common:Name: Debt claims on nonresidents
structure:Code.common:Description: Claims for debt owed by nonresidents.

structure:Code.common:Name: Debt claims on nonresidents, Short-term
structure:Code.common:Description: Claims for debt owed by nonresidents. Original contract stipulates that payment is due in one year or less or payable on demand (referred to as short-term maturity).

structure:Code.common:Name: Reseve Assets, Not in SDR basket
structure:Code.common:Description: Reserve Assets, not included in the basket of currencies used to value Special Drawing Rights (SDRs).

structure:Code.common:Name: Total
structure:Code.common:Description: The sum of all relevant components or categories.

structure:Codelist.common:Name: Flow or stock entry
structure:Codelist.common:Description: A classification that indicates whether a data point represents a flow (a quantity measured over a period of time) or a stock (a quantity measured at a specific point in time).

structure:Code.common:Name: Not applicable
structure:Code.common:Description: A term used when a particular concept or data item does not apply to the context in question.

structure:Code.common:Name: Balancing items
structure:Code.common:Description: Accounting constructs used to ensure that the accounts balance, representing the difference between total sources and uses.

structure:Code.common:Name: Holding gains in assets and liabilities
structure:Code.common:Description: Categorization of gains in the value of assets and liabilities due to price changes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Holding gains in assets
structure:Code.common:Description: Categorization of gains in the value of assetsdue to price changes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Holding gains in liabilities
structure:Code.common:Description: Categorization of gains in the value of liabilities due to price changes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other changes in the volume of assets and liabilities
structure:Code.common:Description: Categorization of changes in the volume of assets and liabilities due to factors other than transactions and revaluations.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other changes in the volume of assets
structure:Code.common:Description: Categorization of changes in the volume of assets due to factors other than transactions and revaluations.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other changes in the volume of liabilities
structure:Code.common:Description: Categorization of changes in the volume of liabilities due to factors other than transactions and revaluations.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other economic flows (holding gains + other changes in volume) in assets and liabilities
structure:Code.common:Description: Organizing and categorizing all non-transactional changes in the value and volume of assets and liabilities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other economic flows (holding gains + other changes in volume) in assets
structure:Code.common:Description: Organizing and categorizing all non-transactional changes in the value and volume of assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other economic flows (holding gains + other changes in volume) in liabilities
structure:Code.common:Description: Organizing and categorizing all non-transactional changes in the value and volume of liabilities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Expenditures by function of government
structure:Code.common:Description: Categorizing government expenditures based on the purpose or function they serve, such as health, education, or defense.

structure:Code.common:Name: Stocks of assets and liabilities
structure:Code.common:Description: Organizing and categorizing assets and liabilities based on their characteristics and economic functions.

structure:Code.common:Name: Stocks of assets
structure:Code.common:Description: Organizing and categorizing assets based on their characteristics and economic functions.

structure:Code.common:Name: Stocks of liabilities
structure:Code.common:Description: Organizing and categorizing liabilities based on their characteristics and economic functions.

structure:Code.common:Name: Transactions in assets and liabilities
structure:Code.common:Description: Categorizing transactions based on their impact on assets and liabilities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Transactions in assets
structure:Code.common:Description: Categorizing transactions based on their impact on assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Transactions in liabilities
structure:Code.common:Description: Categorizing transactions based on their impact on liabilities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Future flows, contingent
structure:Code.common:Description: Expected future financial flows that depend on the occurrence of specific events or conditions.

structure:Code.common:Name: Stocks and future flows to be reported with standard periodicity and timeliness
structure:Code.common:Description: The requirement to report stock positions and expected future financial flows at regular intervals and within specified timeframes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Future flows, predetermined
structure:Code.common:Description: Expected future financial flows that are certain and based on existing agreements or conditions.

structure:Code.common:Name: Integrated flow and stock positions
structure:Code.common:Description: Combined presentation of economic flows (transactions) and stock positions (assets and liabilities) to provide a comprehensive view of financial status and activity.

structure:Code.common:Name: Changes in positions other than transactions
structure:Code.common:Description: Variations in asset and liability positions due to factors other than transactions, such as revaluations or other changes in volume.

structure:Code.common:Name: Revaluations / nominal holding gains and losses
structure:Code.common:Description: Changes in the value of assets and liabilities due to price changes, reflecting gains or losses in nominal terms.

structure:Code.common:Name: Revaluations due to exchange rate changes
structure:Code.common:Description: Adjustments in the value of assets and liabilities resulting from fluctuations in exchange rates.

structure:Code.common:Name: Revaluations due to other price changes
structure:Code.common:Description: Adjustments in the value of assets and liabilities resulting from changes in market prices other than exchange rates.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other changes in the volume of Assets / liabilities = other changes excluding revaluations
structure:Code.common:Description: Adjustments to the volume of assets and liabilities that are not due to revaluations, such as write-offs or physical changes in assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Closing balance sheet / positions / stocks
structure:Code.common:Description: The financial position of an entity at the end of an accounting period, showing the values of assets, liabilities, and equity.

structure:Code.common:Name: Long positions
structure:Code.common:Description: Assets held by an entity with the expectation of appreciation or income generation.

structure:Code.common:Name: Opening balance sheet / positions / stocks
structure:Code.common:Description: The financial position of an entity at the beginning of an accounting period, showing the values of assets, liabilities, and equity.

structure:Code.common:Name: Changes in balance sheet / positions / stocks
structure:Code.common:Description: Adjustments or variations in the value or composition of assets, liabilities, and equity items on the balance sheet over a period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Main aggregates
structure:Code.common:Description: Key summary indicators or measures that provide an overview of economic activity, such as GDP, total revenue, or total expenditure.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total other economic flows
structure:Code.common:Description: The sum of all changes in the value and volume of assets and liabilities that are not due to transactions, including holding gains and other changes in volume.

structure:Code.common:Name: Positions
structure:Code.common:Description: The financial holdings of assets, liabilities, and equity at a specific point in time.

structure:Code.common:Name: Short positions
structure:Code.common:Description: Assets held by an entity through borrowing and selling, expecting a decrease in value.

structure:Code.common:Name: Stock positions
structure:Code.common:Description: The values of assets, liabilities, and equity held at a specific point in time.

structure:Code.common:Name: Stock positions by counterpart sector
structure:Code.common:Description: The values of assets and liabilities categorized by the sector of the counterpart entity involved in the transaction.

structure:Code.common:Name: Transactions
structure:Code.common:Description: Economic flows that result from interactions between institutional units by mutual agreement, involving an exchange of value.

structure:Code.common:Name: Transactions by counterpart sector
structure:Code.common:Description: The economic transactions categorized by the sector of the counterpart entity involved.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total
structure:Code.common:Description: The sum of all relevant components or categories.

structure:Code.common:Name: Revenue
structure:Code.common:Description: Revenue.

structure:Code.common:Name: Expense
structure:Code.common:Description: Expense.

structure:Code.common:Name: Transactions (cash basis of recording)
structure:Code.common:Description: Transactions (cash basis of recording).

structure:Codelist.common:Name: Prices
structure:Codelist.common:Description: This codelist represents different types of prices or price adjustments, including those that have been adjusted for inflation (real or constant prices) and those that have not (nominal or current prices). It also includes various methods for adjusting prices for inflation, such as using deflators or converting to a constant base period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Constant prices
structure:Code.common:Description: Values that have had the effect of price changes removed, expressed as time series in constant prices (fixed base) or chain-linked volume terms, or as non-time series in previous year's prices

structure:Code.common:Name: Closing price
structure:Code.common:Description: An adjusted deflator index that has been recalibrated to a new base period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Current prices
structure:Code.common:Description: Values expressed without any adjustment for price changes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Price index
structure:Code.common:Description: A measure that examines the weighted average of prices of a basket of consumer goods and services.

structure:Code.common:Name: Breakeven external oil price
structure:Code.common:Description: The oil price at which a country's external balances are neither in surplus nor deficit.

structure:Code.common:Name: Breakeven fiscal oil price
structure:Code.common:Description: The oil price at which a country's fiscal balance is neither in surplus nor deficit.

structure:Code.common:Name: Volume
structure:Code.common:Description: The quantity of goods or services produced or traded, often measured in terms of physical units or monetary value.

structure:Code.common:Name: Value
structure:Code.common:Description: The value of a product reflects its price multipled by its quantity.

structure:Code.common:Name: Not applicable
structure:Code.common:Description: Terms or data that do not apply to the current context or situation.

structure:Code.common:Name: Unit prices
structure:Code.common:Description: The unitary price of an item or commodity.

structure:Code.common:Name: Unit value
structure:Code.common:Description: The unit value (value / quantity) of an item or commodity.

structure:Code.common:Name: Export price
structure:Code.common:Description: The export price of a commodity.

structure:Code.common:Name: Import price
structure:Code.common:Description: The import price of a commodity.

structure:Code.common:Name: Current prices in US Dollar
structure:Code.common:Description: Measured in current prices denominated in US Dollar.

structure:Codelist.common:Name: Currency
structure:Codelist.common:Description: This codelist provides a standardized list of currency codes and names, based on the ISO 4217 standard, representing the various currencies used globally for economic and financial transactions.

structure:Codelist.common:Name: Seasonal Adjustment
structure:Codelist.common:Description: This codelist represents a set of codes identifying the statistical techniques employed to remove seasonal patterns or fluctuations from time series data.

structure:Code.common:Name: Seasonally adjusted (SA)
structure:Code.common:Description: Time series that have been adjusted for seasonal variations, including trading-day (working-day) effects and other regular calendar variations if present.

structure:Code.common:Name: Seasonally adjusted factors
structure:Code.common:Description: The seasonally adjusted component is the result of the extraction of the seasonal component (including the calendar effects component) from a time series. If neither seasonal nor calendar influences are present in the original data, the seasonally adjusted series is given by the original data.

structure:Code.common:Name: Not seasonally adjusted (NSA)
structure:Code.common:Description: Time series that have not been adjusted for seasonal variations, including trading-day (working-day) effects and other regular calendar variations if present.

structure:Code.common:Name: Trend cycle data
structure:Code.common:Description: Trend estimates are derived from seasonally adjusted estimates via an averaging process which attempts to remove the irregular component of the time series. This allows the underlying direction of a time series to be identified.

structure:Code.common:Name: Working day adjusted
structure:Code.common:Description: Working-day adjustment is a part of the calendar adjustment which focusses on the changing number of working days (Monday - Friday) in the various months and their effect on statistical indicators (e.g. industrial production, production in construction) for these months. (source: Eurostat)

structure:Code.common:Name: Not applicable
structure:Code.common:Description: Not applicable

structure:Code.common:Name: Trend
structure:Code.common:Description: Trend estimates are derived from seasonally adjusted estimates via an averaging process which attempts to remove the irregular component of the time series. This allows the underlying direction of a time series to be identified.

structure:Code.common:Name: Trend-cycle data, calendar adjusted
structure:Code.common:Description: Trend-cycle data, calendar adjusted estimates are derived from seasonally adjusced estimates via an averaging process which attempts to remove the irregular components of che time series. This allows The underlying direccion of a time series to be idencified. The data are adjusted for variations in the calendar.

structure:Code.common:Name: Trend-cycle data, not calendar adjusted
structure:Code.common:Description: Trend-cycle data, calendar adjusted estimates are derived from seasonally adjusced estimates via an averaging process which attempts to remove the irregular components of che time series. This allows The underlying direccion of a time series to be idencified. The data are not adjusted for variations in the calendar.

structure:Codelist.common:Name: REPORTING_PERIOD_TYPE
structure:Codelist.common:Description: It is used to identify and distinguish between different types of time periods in economic and financial reporting. The specific start and end dates for a fiscal year (FY) can vary depending on the country, organization, or industry. When reporting data using this codelist, it is essential to specify the exact start and end dates of the fiscal year being referenced.

structure:Code.common:Name: Calendar year
structure:Code.common:Description: A 12-month period starting on January 1st and ending on December 31st.

structure:Code.common:Name: Fiscal year
structure:Code.common:Description: A 12-month period that a company or government uses for accounting purposes. The fiscal year may or may not align with the calendar year. For example, a company's fiscal year could start on July 1st and end on June 30th of the following year.

structure:Code.common:Name: Base year
structure:Code.common:Description: The Base Year is a specific year chosen as a reference point for constructing an index or comparing data over time.

structure:Code.common:Name: Standard reference period (SRP)
structure:Code.common:Description: Standard Reference Period (SRP) is a consistent timeframe used for comparing data over time.

structure:Code.common:Name: To delete
structure:Code.common:Description: To delete

structure:Code.common:Name: Standard reference period (2010=100)
structure:Code.common:Description: Standard Reference Period (SRP) is a consistent timeframe used for comparing data over time. This series is references to 2010=100.

structure:Code.common:Name: Fiscal year starting in February
structure:Code.common:Description: A 12-month period starting in February 1st that a company or government uses for accounting purposes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Fiscal year starting in March
structure:Code.common:Description: A 12-month period starting in March 1st that a company or government uses for accounting purposes.

structure:Code.common:Description: A 12-month period starting in June 1st that a company or government uses for accounting purposes.

structure:Code.common:Description: A 12-month period starting in July 1st that a company or government uses for accounting purposes.

structure:Codelist.common:Name: Accounting Entry
structure:Codelist.common:Description: This codelist identifies whether a transaction represents a use of resources, a source of funds, an asset, a liability, or a change in equity.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total
structure:Code.common:Description: The sum of all relevant components or categories.

structure:Code.common:Name: Not allocated/unspecified
structure:Code.common:Description: Not specified or detailed.

structure:Code.common:Name: Not applicable
structure:Code.common:Description: Not applicable or relevant in the given context.

structure:Code.common:Name: Assets
structure:Code.common:Description: Assets is store of value, over which ownership rights are enforced and from which their owners may derive economic benefits by holding them over a period of time (2016 MFSMCG glossary).

structure:Code.common:Name: Assets, Claims on
structure:Code.common:Description: Assets, Claims on

structure:Code.common:Name: Assets, Claims on, Credit to
structure:Code.common:Description: Assets, Claims on, Credit to

structure:Code.common:Name: Assets, Claims on, Other claims on
structure:Code.common:Description: Assets, Claims on, Other claims on

structure:Code.common:Name: Gross sales of assets (decrease)
structure:Code.common:Description: The total value of asset sales, representing a decrease in asset holdings.

structure:Code.common:Name: Assets (gross)
structure:Code.common:Description: Gross assets refer to the total value of all assets owned or held by an individual, organization, or entity before accounting for any deductions, such as depreciation or liabilities

structure:Code.common:Name: Gross acquisition of assets (increase)
structure:Code.common:Description: The total value of assets acquired, representing an increase in asset holdings.

structure:Code.common:Name: Assets (net)
structure:Code.common:Description: Assets is store of value, over which ownership rights are enforced and from which their owners may derive economic benefits by holding them over a period of time (2016 MFSMCG glossary).

structure:Code.common:Name: Assets - short position
structure:Code.common:Description: Store of value representing a benefit or series of benefits accruing to the economic owner by holding or using the entity over a period of time. It is a means of carrying forward value from one accounting period to another.

structure:Code.common:Name: Assets (short or negative positions)
structure:Code.common:Description: Assets that are either shorted or have negative positions due to borrowing or other financial obligations.

structure:Code.common:Name: Balance (credits minus debits)
structure:Code.common:Description: The difference between the total credits and debits in an account, representing net credit position.

structure:Code.common:Name: Credit (Resources)
structure:Code.common:Description: Credits related to resource inflows, including financial and non-financial resources.

structure:Code.common:Name: Credit (Environment + Economy)
structure:Code.common:Description: Credits accounted for within the context of both environmental and economic transactions.

structure:Code.common:Name: Credit/Revenue
structure:Code.common:Description: Credit entries relate to exports of goods and services, earned income receivable, transfer income receivable and disposals of non-produced non-financial assets (the financial account in the external accounts uses the terms net acquisition of financial assets and net incurrence of liabilities rather than credit and debit).

structure:Code.common:Name: Contingent liabilities
structure:Code.common:Description: Liabilities that may occur depending on the outcome of a future event, as defined in the European System of Accounts (ESA) and Government Finance Statistics (GFS).

structure:Code.common:Name: Claims
structure:Code.common:Description: Financial claims on other entities

structure:Code.common:Name: Credit to
structure:Code.common:Description: Credit to

structure:Code.common:Name: Credit (excluding exceptional financing)
structure:Code.common:Description: Credits that exclude any exceptional financing measures such as bailouts or special financial assistance.

structure:Code.common:Name: Debit (Uses)
structure:Code.common:Description: Debit entries relate to imports of goods and services, earned income payable, transfer income payable and acquisitions of non-produced non-financial assets (the financial account in the external accounts uses the terms net acquisition of financial assets and net incurrence of liabilities rather than credit and debit).

structure:Code.common:Name: Debit (Environment + Economy)
structure:Code.common:Description: Debits accounted for within the context of both environmental and economic transactions.

structure:Code.common:Name: Domestic (adjustment)
structure:Code.common:Description: Adjustments made to domestic accounts to reflect accurate financial positions.

structure:Code.common:Name: Debit/Expenditure
structure:Code.common:Description: Outflows or payments made, representing expenditures.

structure:Code.common:Name: End use
structure:Code.common:Description: The final consumption or utilization of goods and services.

structure:Code.common:Name: End use (Environment + Economy)
structure:Code.common:Description: The final consumption or utilization of goods and services within the context of both environmental and economic considerations.

structure:Code.common:Name: End use, of which emissions relevant
structure:Code.common:Description: End use of goods and services where emissions are a significant factor.

structure:Code.common:Name: Liabilities (domestic)
structure:Code.common:Description: Obligations where one unit (the debtor) is obliged, under specific circumstances, to provide funds or other resources to another unit (the creditor). These include shares and other equity in corporations.

structure:Code.common:Name: Transformation use
structure:Code.common:Description: Use of resources or funds for transformation activities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Transformation use (Environment + Economy)
structure:Code.common:Description: Use of resources or funds for transformation activities within the context of environmental and economic considerations.

structure:Code.common:Name: Economy to environment
structure:Code.common:Description: Financial flows or impacts from economic activities to environmental resources or impacts.

structure:Code.common:Name: Environment to economy
structure:Code.common:Description: Financial flows or impacts from environmental resources or activities to the economy.

structure:Code.common:Name: Financial assets
structure:Code.common:Description: Assets that are in the form of cash, stocks, bonds, or other financial instruments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Financial assets (adjustment)
structure:Code.common:Description: Adjustments made to the value or reporting of financial assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Financial assets (domestic)
structure:Code.common:Description: Financial assets held within the domestic economy.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign (adjustment)
structure:Code.common:Description: Adjustments made to foreign accounts to reflect accurate financial positions.

structure:Code.common:Name: Financial assets (foreign)
structure:Code.common:Description: Financial assets held in foreign entities or markets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Inflows (reserves template)
structure:Code.common:Description: Incoming funds or resources within the context of a reserves template.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net flows (reserves template)
structure:Code.common:Description: Net inflows or outflows within the context of a reserves template.

structure:Code.common:Name: Outflows (reserves template)
structure:Code.common:Description: Outgoing funds or resources within the context of a reserves template.

structure:Code.common:Name: Gross
structure:Code.common:Description: The total value before any deductions.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net income on inward FDI
structure:Code.common:Description: The net income generated from inward foreign direct investment.

structure:Code.common:Name: Inflows
structure:Code.common:Description: The incoming funds or resources.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net income on outward FDI
structure:Code.common:Description: The net income generated from outward foreign direct investment.

structure:Code.common:Name: Liabilities
structure:Code.common:Description: Obligations where one unit (the debtor) is obliged, under specific circumstances, to provide funds or other resources to another unit (the creditor). These include shares and other equity in corporations.

structure:Code.common:Name: Liabilities (adjustment)
structure:Code.common:Description: Obligations where one unit (the debtor) is obliged, under specific circumstances, to provide funds or other resources to another unit (the creditor). These include shares and other equity in corporations.

structure:Code.common:Name: Gross decrease in liabilities
structure:Code.common:Description: The total reduction in liabilities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Liabilities (foreign)
structure:Code.common:Description: Obligations where one unit (the debtor) is obliged, under specific circumstances, to provide funds or other resources to another unit (the creditor). These include shares and other equity in corporations.

structure:Code.common:Name: Liabilities (gross)
structure:Code.common:Description: Gross liabilities refer to the total value of all obligations or debts owed by an individual, organization, or entity before accounting for any adjustments or offsets

structure:Code.common:Name: Gross incurrence of liabilities
structure:Code.common:Description: The total value of liabilities incurred before any deductions.

structure:Code.common:Name: Liabilities to
structure:Code.common:Description: Obligations where one unit (the debtor) is obliged, under specific circumstances, to provide funds or other resources to another unit (the creditor). These include shares and other equity in corporations.

structure:Code.common:Name: Liabilities to, Claims on
structure:Code.common:Description: Liabilities to, Claims on

structure:Code.common:Name: Liabilities: Unofficial
structure:Code.common:Description: Obligations where one unit (the debtor) is obliged, under specific circumstances, to provide funds or other resources to another unit (the creditor). These include shares and other equity in corporations.. Liabilities that are not necessarily recognized by official records or entities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Liabilities (excluding exceptional financing)
structure:Code.common:Description: Obligations where one unit (the debtor) is obliged, under specific circumstances, to provide funds or other resources to another unit (the creditor). These include shares and other equity in corporations.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net (assets minus liabilities)
structure:Code.common:Description: The net value obtained by subtracting total liabilities from total assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net acquisition of financial assets other than cash
structure:Code.common:Description: The net result of acquiring financial assets excluding cash.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net Claims on

structure:Code.common:Name: Net Liabilities (liabilities minus assets)
structure:Code.common:Description: The net value obtained by subtracting total assets from total liabilities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Negative Credit/Revenue
structure:Code.common:Description: A situation where credits or revenues are negative, indicating a deficit or loss.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net (acquisitions less disposals)
structure:Code.common:Description: The net result of total acquisitions minus total disposals.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net (assets less liabilities)

structure:Code.common:Name: Net Foreign Assets, Claims on
structure:Code.common:Description: Net Foreign Assets, Claims on

structure:Code.common:Name: Net Foreign Assets, Liabilities to
structure:Code.common:Description: Net Foreign Assets, Liabilities to

structure:Code.common:Name: Balance on goods, services, and income
structure:Code.common:Description: The net balance of trade in goods, services, and income flows between countries.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net FDI inward
structure:Code.common:Description: The net result of foreign direct investment inflows.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net FDI outward
structure:Code.common:Description: The net result of foreign direct investment outflows.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other Liabilities to
structure:Code.common:Description: Other Liabilities to

structure:Code.common:Name: Provided by
structure:Code.common:Description: Resources or funds provided by an entity.

structure:Code.common:Name: Private liabilities
structure:Code.common:Description: Obligations where one unit (the debtor) is obliged, under specific circumstances, to provide funds or other resources to another unit (the creditor). These include shares and other equity in corporations.. Liabilities with private entities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Provided to
structure:Code.common:Description: Resources or funds provided to an entity.

structure:Code.common:Name: Liabilities: Official
structure:Code.common:Description: Obligations where one unit (the debtor) is obliged, under specific circumstances, to provide funds or other resources to another unit (the creditor). These include shares and other equity in corporations. Liabilities that are not necessarily recognized by official records or entities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net (net acquisition of financial assets less net incurrence of liabilities)
structure:Code.common:Description: The difference between net acquisition of financial assets and the net incurrence of liabilities in an accounting period.

structure:Codelist.common:Name: Functional category
structure:Codelist.common:Description: A classification used to categorize investments based on their purpose or function, such as equity investments, debt investments, or other investments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Allocated foreign exchange reserves
structure:Code.common:Description: Those foreign exchange reserves for which the currency of denomination has been identified and reported in the Currency Composition of Official Foreign Exchange Reserves (COFER).

structure:Code.common:Name: Direct investment
structure:Code.common:Description: Direct investment is a category of cross-border investment associated with an investor (or its affiliated enterprise) in one economy having control or significant degree of influence over the management of an investee enterprise resident in another economy.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserve assets
structure:Code.common:Description: External assets that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). They can include monetary gold, Special Drawing Rights (SDRs), reserve positions in the IMF, and other reserve assets. Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency.

structure:Code.common:Name: Financial derivatives (other than reserves) and employee stock options
structure:Code.common:Description: Financial derivatives are negotiable financial instruments linked to another specific financial instrument, indicator, or commodity, through which specific risks (e.g., interest rate risk, foreign exchange risk, equity and commodity price risk, credit risk) can be traded in their own right in financial markets. Employee stock options are options to buy the equity of a company, offered to employees of the company as a form of remuneration and often at a discount to the market value. If the financial derivative is linked to a reserve asset it is excluded from the value of this indicator.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total foreign exchange reserves
structure:Code.common:Description: Total of Reserve assets as reported in the International Liquidity database (formerly International Financial Statistics)

structure:Code.common:Name: Other investment
structure:Code.common:Description: Other investment represents a residual investment category that includes positions and transactions other than those included in direct investment, portfolio investment, financial derivatives and employee stock options, and reserve assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Portfolio investment
structure:Code.common:Description: Portfolio investment reflects cross-border transactions and positions involving debt or equity securities, other than those included in direct investment or reserve assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Unallocated foreign exchange reserves
structure:Code.common:Description: In the context of the Currency Composition of Official Foreign Exchange Reserves (COFER), Unallocated Foreign Exchange Reserves (FXR) is a residual category consisting of the difference between Total FXR sourced from the IMF's International Liquidity database and the total allocated reserves reported in COFER. It has two components: (i) the total FXR of nonreporting countries; and (ii) the discrepancy (if any) between the Total FXR of COFER-reporting countries and the total Allocated FXR reported in COFER.

structure:Code.common:Name: All functional categories
structure:Code.common:Description: All categories of investment including direct investment, portfolio investment, financial derivatives, employee stock options, reserve assets, and other investments.

structure:Code.common:Name: All functional categories (total) - sum of (direct investment, portfolio investment)
structure:Code.common:Description: The combined total of direct investment and portfolio investment, representing the sum of these two categories.

structure:Code.common:Name: All functional categories (total) excluding direct investment
structure:Code.common:Description: The combined total of all investment categories except for direct investment.

structure:Code.common:Name: All functional categories (total) excluding direct investment and reserve assets
structure:Code.common:Description: The combined total of all investment categories except for direct investment and reserve assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: All functional categories (total) excluding financial derivatives and employee stock options
structure:Code.common:Description: The combined total of all investment categories except for financial derivatives and employee stock options.

structure:Code.common:Name: All functional categories (total) excluding financial derivatives, employee stock options and reserve assets
structure:Code.common:Description: The combined total of all investment categories except for financial derivatives, employee stock options, and reserve assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: All functional categories (total) excluding reserve assets
structure:Code.common:Description: The combined total of all investment categories except for reserve assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Change in reserve assets
structure:Code.common:Description: The difference in the value of reserve assets between two points in time.

structure:Code.common:Name: Direct investment + portfolio investment
structure:Code.common:Description: The sum of direct investment and portfolio investment, indicating the total investment in these two categories.

structure:Code.common:Name: Direct investment and equity security
structure:Code.common:Description: Cross-border investment where the investor has control or significant influence, including ownership of equity securities in the enterprise.

structure:Code.common:Name: Direct investment between fellow enterprises
structure:Code.common:Description: Direct investment between two enterprises that are under control or influence of the same direct investor but where neither of the enterprises controls or influences the other (directly or indirectly).

structure:Code.common:Name: Direct investment between fellow enterprises if ultimate controlling parent is nonresident
structure:Code.common:Description: Direct investment between fellow enterprises if ultimate controlling parent is nonresident

structure:Code.common:Description: Direct investment between fellow enterprises if ultimate controlling parent is unknown
