structure:Code.common:Name: Current transfers within general government
structure:Code.common:Description: Current transfers between different levels of government, such as frequently occur between central and state or local government, and between general government and social security funds.

structure:Code.common:Name: Current grants to/from governments and international organizations
structure:Code.common:Description: Unrequited current transfers between governments and international organizations (e.g., foreign aid).

structure:Code.common:Name: Current international cooperation
structure:Code.common:Description: Current transfers in cash or in kind between the governments of different countries or between governments and international organisations.

structure:Code.common:Name: Miscellaneous current transfers
structure:Code.common:Description: Current transfers, in cash or in kind, other than current taxes on income, wealth, etc.; net social contributions; social benefits; net non-life insurance premiums and claims; current transfers within general government; and current international cooperation. In the external accounts, miscellaneous current transfers include all current transfers, in cash or in kind, other than personal transfers, current taxes on income, wealth, etc.; social contributions; social benefits; net nonlife insurance premiums and claims; and current international cooperation.

structure:Code.common:Name: Current transfers to NPISHs
structure:Code.common:Description: Unrequited transactions between two parties where one party provides a good, service, non-financial or financial asset to the other party, with no expectation of anything of economic value in exchange. Unlike capital transfers, they do not oblige one or both parties to acquire, or dispose of, an asset.

structure:Code.common:Name: Current transfers between resident and non-resident households
structure:Code.common:Description: Transfers of money between households in different countries (e.g., remittances).

structure:Code.common:Name: Other miscellaneous current transfers
structure:Code.common:Description: Fines and penalties, payments (after deduction of service charge and donations) and receipts related to lotteries and gambling, and payments for compensation

structure:Code.common:Name: Fines, penalties, and forfeits
structure:Code.common:Description: Payments made as a result of legal or administrative actions (e.g., traffic fines, court penalties).

structure:Code.common:Name: Other miscellaneous current transfers: other than fines, penalties, and forfeits
structure:Code.common:Description: Other current transfers not elsewhere classified, excluding fines, penalties, and forfeits.

structure:Code.common:Name: Value added tax and GNI - based EU own resources
structure:Code.common:Description: Contributions made by EU member states to the EU budget, based on VAT revenue and Gross National Income (GNI).

structure:Code.common:Name: VAT-based third EU own resource
structure:Code.common:Description: The portion of EU own resources derived from VAT revenue.

structure:Code.common:Name: GNI-based fourth EU own resource
structure:Code.common:Description: The portion of EU own resources derived from GNI.

structure:Code.common:Name: Current transfers of which UK rebate
structure:Code.common:Description: Part of the current transfers related to the EU budget, specifically highlighting the UK rebate (now historically relevant).

structure:Code.common:Name: Miscellaneous non-tax contribution of the government to the institutions of the EU
structure:Code.common:Description: Other contributions made by governments to EU institutions that are not taxes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Miscellaneous non-tax contribution of the government to the institutions of the European Union (EU): of which plastics contribution - EU own resource
structure:Code.common:Description: A specific non-tax contribution related to plastics, forming part of the EU's own resources.

structure:Code.common:Name: Miscellaneous current transfers and VAT and GNI-based own resources [deprecated]
structure:Code.common:Description: A previously used category encompassing various current transfers and EU own resources.

structure:Code.common:Name: Current transfers within general government, current international cooperation and miscellaneous current transfers
structure:Code.common:Description: Transfers between different levels of government, international cooperation transfers, and other miscellaneous current transfers.

structure:Code.common:Name: Current international cooperation, miscellaneous current transfers and VAT and GNI-based EU own resources
structure:Code.common:Description: Combines international cooperation transfers, miscellaneous current transfers, and EU own resources.

structure:Code.common:Name: Current transfers financed by the Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF)
structure:Code.common:Description: Current transfers specifically funded by the EU's Recovery and Resilience Facility.

structure:Code.common:Name: Secondary income: all miscellaneous current transfers
structure:Code.common:Description: A broad category encompassing all miscellaneous current transfers.

structure:Code.common:Name: Adjustment for the change in pension entitlements
structure:Code.common:Description: An adjustment made to account for changes in the value of pension entitlements.

structure:Code.common:Name: Transfer of pension entitlements between schemes
structure:Code.common:Description: The value of pension entitlements transferred between different pension schemes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Change in entitlements due to negotiated changes in scheme structure
structure:Code.common:Description: Changes in pension entitlements resulting from alterations to the rules or structure of pension schemes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net capital transfers
structure:Code.common:Description: Net unrequited transfers, either in cash or in kind, linked to the acquisition, disposal or transfer of an asset (other than cash or inventories); or where a liability is forgiven or assumed; or where the transfers are intended to address accumulated losses incurred over a multi-year period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Capital taxes
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes charged at irregular and infrequent intervals on the values of the assets or net worth owned by institutional units or on the values of assets transferred between institutional units as a result of legacies, gifts inter vivos, or other transfers.

structure:Code.common:Name: Taxes on capital transfers
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes levied on the transfer of capital assets (e.g., inheritance taxes, gift taxes).

structure:Code.common:Name: Capital levies
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes on the values of the assets or net worth owned by institutional units levied at irregular, and very infrequent, intervals of time.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other capital taxes n.e.c.
structure:Code.common:Description: Other capital taxes not elsewhere classified.

structure:Code.common:Name: Investment grants
structure:Code.common:Description: Capital transfers made by governments to other resident or non-resident institutional units to finance all or part of the costs of their acquiring fixed assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other capital transfers
structure:Code.common:Description: Capital transfers other than investment grants, capital taxes, and debt forgiveness.

structure:Code.common:Name: Capital transfers from general government to relevant sectors representing taxes and social contributions assessed but unlikely to be collected
structure:Code.common:Description: Capital transfers representing taxes and social contributions that the government expects not to receive.

structure:Code.common:Name: Taxes on products assessed but unlikely to be collected
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes on products that are assessed but not expected to be collected.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other taxes on production assessed but unlikely to be collected
structure:Code.common:Description: Other taxes on production that are assessed but not expected to be collected.

structure:Code.common:Name: Taxes on income assessed but unlikely to be collected
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes on income that are assessed but not expected to be collected.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other current taxes assessed but unlikely to be collected
structure:Code.common:Description: Other current taxes that are assessed but not expected to be collected.

structure:Code.common:Name: Employers actual social contributions assessed but unlikely to be collected
structure:Code.common:Description: Social contributions from employers that are assessed but not expected to be collected.

structure:Code.common:Name: Households' actual social contributions assessed but unlikely to be collected
structure:Code.common:Description: Social contributions from households that are assessed but not expected to be collected.

structure:Code.common:Name: Employees' actual social contributions assessed but unlikely to be collected
structure:Code.common:Description: Social contributions from employees that are assessed but not expected to be collected.

structure:Code.common:Name: Actual social contributions by non-employed persons assessed but unlikely to be collected
structure:Code.common:Description: Social contributions from non-employed persons that are assessed but not expected to be collected.

structure:Code.common:Name: Actual social contributions by self-employed persons assessed but unlikely to be collected
structure:Code.common:Description: Social contributions from self-employed persons that are assessed but not expected to be collected.

structure:Code.common:Name: Capital taxes assessed but unlikely to be collected
structure:Code.common:Description: Capital taxes that are assessed but not expected to be collected.

structure:Code.common:Name: Nonlife insurance capital claims
structure:Code.common:Description: Capital transfers related to non-life insurance claims, often in cases of large-scale damage.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other capital transfers not elsewhere classified
structure:Code.common:Description: Capital transfers that do not fit into other specific categories.

structure:Code.common:Name: Calls on guarantees
structure:Code.common:Description: Payments made when a guarantee is invoked, transferring a financial obligation.

structure:Code.common:Name: Capital injections recorded as capital transfers
structure:Code.common:Description: It refers to capital injections (funds invested in a business) that are recorded as capital transfers.

structure:Code.common:Name: Capital transfers recorded in the context of asset purchases
structure:Code.common:Description: Capital transfers that occur as part of transactions involving the purchase of assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other capital transfers and investment grants
structure:Code.common:Description: A combination of other capital transfers and grants specifically for investment purposes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Taxes on use of goods and on permission to use goods and perform activities
structure:Code.common:Description: Fees levied for the issuance of a license or permit that are not commensurate with the cost of the control function of government.

structure:Code.common:Name: Motor vehicles taxes [IMF GFSM definition]
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes on the use of motor vehicles or permission to use motor vehicles.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other taxes on use of goods and on permission to use goods or perform activities
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes paid by enterprises in order to obtain a license to carry on a particular kind of business or profession and taxes payable by individuals to perform certain activities .

structure:Code.common:Name: Social security contributions
structure:Code.common:Description: Amounts payable to a social security scheme in order for a designated beneficiary to be entitled to recieve the social benefits covered by the scheme.

structure:Code.common:Name: Social security benefits
structure:Code.common:Description: Current transfers payable by social security funds to households, intended to provide for the needs that arise from certain events or circumstances, for example, sickness, unemployment, retirement, housing, education or family circumstances.

structure:Code.common:Name: Social assistance benefits
structure:Code.common:Description: Social benefits payable in cash by government units or non-profit institutions serving households to households to meet the same needs as social insurance benefits, but without any requirement to participate in a social insurance scheme through the payment of contributions.

structure:Code.common:Name: Transfers not elsewhere classified
structure:Code.common:Description: All transfers other than taxes, grants, social contributions, social benefits, and fines penalties, and forfeits. As a government expense then subsidies are also excluded, but within government revenue subsidies are treated within transfers not elsewhere classified.

structure:Code.common:Name: Gross domestic product (GDP) Oil-based production
structure:Code.common:Description: This refers to the portion of a country's GDP that comes from the extraction, processing, and production of crude oil and related petroleum products.

structure:Code.common:Name: Gross domestic product (GDP) PPP weight
structure:Code.common:Description: This refers to a country's GDP adjusted for purchasing power parity (PPP).

structure:Code.common:Name: Non-oil GDP
structure:Code.common:Description: This represents the portion of a country's GDP generated from all economic activities excluding the oil sector. This includes manufacturing, agriculture, services, tourism, and other industries.

structure:Code.common:Name: Economic appearance of assets
structure:Code.common:Description: Appearance of assets which is neither due to transactions nor due to holding gains and losses (revaluations). Examples relate to the recognition of produced assets, not previously recognised as assets; discoveries of natural resources; changes in the quality of land; the recognition of goodwill in the purchase of a corporation; and the initiation of contracts, leases and licenses.

structure:Code.common:Name: Catastrophic losses
structure:Code.common:Description: Losses which are the result of large scale, discrete and recognizable events that may destroy a significantly large number of assets within any of the asset categories.

structure:Code.common:Name: Uncompensated seizures
structure:Code.common:Description: Governments or other institutional units taking possession of assets of other institutional units without compensation, for reasons other than payment of taxes, fines, etc.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other changes in volume not elsewhere classified
structure:Code.common:Description: Changes in the value of assets or liabilities that are neither due to transactions nor due to holding gains and losses (revaluations). They include, amongst others, economic appearance and disappearance of non-produced assets, catastrophic losses, changes due to cancellation and write-offs of debt, uncompensated seizures, reclassifications, and the changes in financial assets arising from entities changing their economy of residence. In the external accounts, the other changes in the volume of assets and liabilities are restricted to those relating to financial assets and liabilities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Changes in classification
structure:Code.common:Description: Changes in assets and liabilities resulting from changes in sector classification and structure (among which changes in assets and liabilities arising from entities changing their economy of residence), and those resulting from changes in the classification of assets and liabilities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Real holding gains and losses
structure:Code.common:Description: The amount by which the value of assets increases (decreases) beyond the neutral holding gains for the period, in the absence of transactions and other changes in the volume of assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Labour productivity (per hours worked)
structure:Code.common:Description: Measure of output, or value added, per unit of input.

structure:Code.common:Name: Savings to investment ratio
structure:Code.common:Description: This ratio compares the portion of an economy's income that is saved to the portion that is invested.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net lending (+) / net borrowing (-) under EDP
structure:Code.common:Description: Net lending is defined as the difference between changes in net worth due to saving and capital transfers and net acquisitions of non-financial assets (acquisitions less disposals of non-financial assets, less depreciation). If the amount is negative, it represents net borrowing. In the external accounts, it represents the sum of the balances on the current and capital accounts. This is conceptually equal to the net balance of the financial account. If the balance is positive, it is called net lending, implying that in net terms, the economy supplies funds to the rest of the world. If the balance is negative, it is called net borrowing, implying that in net terms, the economy receives funds from the rest of the world.

structure:Code.common:Name: Output
structure:Code.common:Description: Goods and services produced by (part of) an enterprise, excluding the value of any goods and services used in an activity for which the establishment does not assume the risk of using the products in production, and excluding the value of goods and services consumed by the same establishment except for goods and services used for capital formation (fixed capital or changes in inventories) or own final consumption.

structure:Code.common:Name: Market output
structure:Code.common:Description: Output intended for sale at economically significant prices.

structure:Code.common:Name: Financial Intermediation Services Indirectly Measured (FISIM)
structure:Code.common:Description: Financial intermediation services which are implicitly charged in the form of either the difference between a reference rate and the interest rate actually paid to depositors, or the difference between the interest rate charged to borrowers and a reference rate.

structure:Code.common:Name: Non-market output
structure:Code.common:Description: Goods and individual or collective services produced by government, the central bank and non-profit institutions serving households that are supplied free, or at prices that are not economically significant, to other institutional units or the community as a whole.

structure:Code.common:Name: Output gap
structure:Code.common:Description: The output gap is the difference between the actual level of output in an economy and its potential level of output.

structure:Code.common:Name: Intermediate consumption
structure:Code.common:Description: Goods and services consumed as inputs by a process of production, excluding fixed assets whose consumption is recorded as depreciation.

structure:Code.common:Name: Final consumption expenditure
structure:Code.common:Description: The amount of expenditure on consumption goods and services, whether individual or collective. Final consumption expenditure can be measured for households, general government, the central bank and non-profit institutions serving households (NPISHs).

structure:Code.common:Name: CO2 emissions embodied in Final Domestic Demand
structure:Code.common:Description: Amount of CO2 emissions from fuel combustion embodied in domestic final demand. Environment, Climate Change, Mitigation, Trade-Related indicators.

structure:Code.common:Name: Collective consumption expenditure
structure:Code.common:Description: Expenditure on services provided simultaneously to all members of the community or to all members of a particular section of the community. Collective final consumption expenditure is only measured for general government, the central bank and non-profit institutions serving households (NPISHs).

structure:Code.common:Name: Actual final consumption
structure:Code.common:Description: Goods or services that are acquired by resident institutional units for the direct satisfaction of human needs or wants, whether individual or collective. Actual final consumption can be measured for households, general government, the central bank and non-profit institutions serving households.

structure:Code.common:Name: Actual individual consumption
structure:Code.common:Description: Goods or services that are acquired by resident institutional units for the direct satisfaction of the needs or wants of individual households. Actual individual consumption is only measured for households.

structure:Code.common:Name: Actual collective consumption
structure:Code.common:Description: Services provided simultaneously to all members of the community or to all members of a particular section of the community. Actual collective consumption is only measured for general government, the central bank and non-profit institutions serving households.

structure:Code.common:Name: Gross capital formation
structure:Code.common:Description: Acquisitions less disposals of produced assets for purposes of fixed capital formation, inventories or valuables.

structure:Code.common:Name: Acquisitions less disposals of fixed assets: machinery and equipment
structure:Code.common:Description: Net investment in non-residential machinery and equipment (e.g. vehicles, computers).

structure:Code.common:Name: Gross fixed capital formation
structure:Code.common:Description: Acquisitions less disposals of fixed assets during the accounting period, including certain specified expenditures on services that add to the value of non-produced assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net fixed capital formation
structure:Code.common:Description: Gross fixed capital formation, after deduction of depreciation.

structure:Code.common:Name: Changes in inventories
structure:Code.common:Description: Value of entries into inventories less the value of withdrawals and less the value of any recurrent losses of goods held in inventories during the accounting period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net capital formation
structure:Code.common:Description: Gross capital formation, after deduction of depreciation.

structure:Code.common:Name: Exports of goods
structure:Code.common:Description: Change in the economic ownership of goods from residents of the compiling economy to non-residents, irrespective of physical movement of goods across national borders.

structure:Code.common:Name: Merchanting
structure:Code.common:Description: Purchase of goods by a resident (of the compiling economy) from a nonresident combined with the subsequent resale of the same goods to another nonresident without the goods being physically moved in and out the compiling economy.

structure:Code.common:Name: Goods sent abroad after processing (inward processing, i.e. your country processes)
structure:Code.common:Description: Adjustment required to reconcile the treatment of pensions as current transfers (social contributions and social benefits) with the treatment of pension entitlements as financial assets. After the adjustment, the saving (SNA) and current account balance (BPM) are the same as what they would have been if social contributions and benefits related to pensions are considered as pure financial transactions, and not recorded as current transfers.

structure:Code.common:Name: Exports of services
structure:Code.common:Description: Services provided by residents of the compiling economy to non-residents.

structure:Code.common:Name: Re-exports
structure:Code.common:Description: Goods produced in other economies, and previously imported, that are exported with no substantial transformation from the state in which they were previously imported.

structure:Code.common:Name: CO2 emissions embodied in Gross Exports
structure:Code.common:Description: Amount of CO2 emissions from fuel combustion embodied in exports. Environment, Climate Change, Mitigation, Trade-Related indicators.

structure:Code.common:Name: Imports of goods
structure:Code.common:Description: Change in the economic ownership of goods from non-residents to residents of the compiling economy, irrespective of physical movement of goods across national borders.

structure:Code.common:Name: Imports of services
structure:Code.common:Description: Services provided by non-residents to residents of the compiling economy.

structure:Code.common:Name: CO2 emissions embodied in Gross Imports
structure:Code.common:Description: Amount of CO2 emissions from fuel combustion embodied in imports. Environment, Climate Change, Mitigation, Trade-Related indicators.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total population
structure:Code.common:Description: All persons who are resident in the economic territory at a given point in time.

structure:Code.common:Name: CO2 emissions embodied in Production
structure:Code.common:Description: Amount of CO2 emissions from fuel combustion embodied in production. Environment, Climate Change, Mitigation, Trade-Related indicators.

structure:Code.common:Name: Employees
structure:Code.common:Description: Persons who, by agreement, work for a resident institutional unit and receive remuneration for their labour.

structure:Code.common:Name: Self employed
structure:Code.common:Description: Individuals working for their own account.

structure:Code.common:Name: Transactions
structure:Code.common:Description: Economic flows that are an interaction between institutional units by mutual agreement or through the operation of the law, or actions within an institutional unit that are analytically useful to treat like transactions because the unit is operating in two different capacities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total final use
structure:Code.common:Description: The total spending on final goods and services in the economy.

structure:Code.common:Name: Terms of trade
structure:Code.common:Description: Ratio of the price of exports to the price of imports.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total resources production account
structure:Code.common:Description: The total resources available to the economy from domestic production.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total resources generation of income account
structure:Code.common:Description: Resources available for the generation of income.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total resources allocation of primary income account
structure:Code.common:Description: Resources available for the allocation of primary income.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total resources secondary distribution of income account
structure:Code.common:Description: Resources available for secondary income distribution.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total resources use of disposable income account
structure:Code.common:Description: Resources available for the use of disposable income.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total change in liabilities and net worth: change in net worth due to saving and capital transfers account
structure:Code.common:Description: Changes in liabilities and net worth due to saving and capital transfers.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total change in liabilities and net worth: acquisitions of nonfinancial assets accounts
structure:Code.common:Description: Changes in liabilities and net worth due to the acquisition of non-financial assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total supply
structure:Code.common:Description: The total amount of goods and services available in the economy (domestic production plus imports).

structure:Code.common:Name: Total use
structure:Code.common:Description: The total use of goods and services in the economy (intermediate consumption plus final use).

structure:Code.common:Name: Total uses production account
structure:Code.common:Description: The uses of goods and services in the production process.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total uses generation of income account
structure:Code.common:Description: The uses of resources in the generation of income.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total uses allocation of primary income account
structure:Code.common:Description: The uses of resources in the allocation of primary income.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total uses secondary distribution of income account
structure:Code.common:Description: The uses of resources in secondary income distribution.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total uses use of disposable income account
structure:Code.common:Description: The uses of disposable income.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total change in assets: change in net worth due to saving and capital, transfers account
structure:Code.common:Description: Changes in assets and net worth due to saving and capital transfers.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total change in assets: acquisitions of non-financial assets accounts
structure:Code.common:Description: Changes in assets due to the acquisition of non-financial assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total intermediate consumption/final use
structure:Code.common:Description: The combined value of intermediate consumption and final use.

structure:Code.common:Name: Domestic use
structure:Code.common:Description: Legal tender in the economy which is issued by the monetary authority for that economy. That is, either that of an individual economy or, in a currency union, that of the common currency area to which the economy belongs.

structure:Code.common:Name: Unit labour cost (based on hours worked)
structure:Code.common:Description: The cost of labor per unit of output, measured using hours worked.

structure:Code.common:Name: Unit labour cost (based on persons)
structure:Code.common:Description: The cost of labor per unit of output, measured using the number of persons employed.

structure:Code.common:Name: Unemployed persons
structure:Code.common:Description: Persons who are the sole or joint owners of the unincorporated enterprises in which they work, excluding those unincorporated enterprises that are classified as quasi-corporations.

structure:Code.common:Name: Unit profits
structure:Code.common:Description: Profits per unit of output.

structure:Code.common:Name: Statistical discrepancy (expenditure approach)
structure:Code.common:Description: The difference between GDP calculated using the expenditure approach and the headline measure of GDP (either by the production approach or an average of the three approaches).

structure:Code.common:Name: Statistical discrepancies in stock flow adjustment
structure:Code.common:Description: Discrepancies arising in the reconciliation of changes in stocks and flows.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other statistical discrepancies (+/-) in stock flow adjustment
structure:Code.common:Description: Other discrepancies in stock flow adjustment not classified elsewhere.

structure:Code.common:Name: Transaction imbalance
structure:Code.common:Description: Discrepancies arising from the recording of transactions.

structure:Code.common:Name: Budget imbalance
structure:Code.common:Description: The difference between government revenue and expenditure.

structure:Code.common:Name: Gross domestic income
structure:Code.common:Description: Total income earned through the production of goods and services in the economy, consisting of remuneration of employees plus gross operating surplus plus gross mixed incomes plus taxes less subsidies on both production and imports.

structure:Code.common:Name: Gross domestic product (GDP) production approach
structure:Code.common:Description: The value of total output less total intermediate consumption plus any taxes less subsidies on products not already included in the value of output.

structure:Code.common:Name: Gross domestic product (GDP) in US Dollars
structure:Code.common:Description: Gross domestic product reflects the total income earned through the production of goods and services in an economic territory during an accounting period. It can be measured in three different ways: using either the expenditure approach, the income approach, or the production approach. This value has been converted into US Dollars.

structure:Code.common:Name: Gross domestic product in purchasing power parity (PPP)
structure:Code.common:Description: Gross domestic product in purchasing power parity (PPP).

structure:Code.common:Name: Potential gross domestic product (fiscal year)
structure:Code.common:Description: The level of GDP that an economy could produce in a fiscal year at full capacity utilization without generating inflationary pressures.

structure:Codelist.common:Name: GFS Stocks, Transactions, Other Flows
structure:Codelist.common:Description: A classification of data items used in the Government Finance Statistics (GFS) framework, distinguishing between stocks (levels at a point in time), transactions (changes over a period), and other flows.

structure:Code.common:Name: Not applicable
structure:Code.common:Description: A term used to indicate that a specific item or category does not apply in the given context.

structure:Code.common:Name: Amortization of total public debt
structure:Code.common:Description: The process of gradually paying off the total public debt through scheduled payments over time. This includes both principal repayments and interest payments on government debt.

structure:Code.common:Name: Budget balance
structure:Code.common:Description: The difference between a government's total revenue and total expenditure over a specific period. A positive balance indicates a surplus, while a negative balance indicates a deficit.

structure:Code.common:Name: Cyclically adjusted balance
structure:Code.common:Description: The cyclically adjusted balance is a measure of a government's budget balance that takes into account the effects of the economic cycle. It adjusts the actual budget balance for the impact of cyclical fluctuations in economic activity, such as changes in output, employment, and tax revenues, to provide a clearer picture of the underlying fiscal position. This adjustment helps policymakers assess the structural or underlying fiscal position of the government, independent of temporary fluctuations caused by the economic cycle. A positive cyclically adjusted balance indicates a structural surplus, while a negative cyclically adjusted balance indicates a structural deficit.

structure:Code.common:Name: Cyclically adjusted primary balance
structure:Code.common:Description: The cyclically adjusted primary balance is similar to the cyclically adjusted balance but focuses specifically on the primary balance, which excludes interest payments on government debt. It adjusts the primary balance for the effects of the economic cycle to provide a measure of the structural fiscal position of the government, independent of cyclical fluctuations. Like the cyclically adjusted balance, a positive cyclically adjusted primary balance indicates a structural surplus, while a negative cyclically adjusted primary balance indicates a structural deficit.

structure:Code.common:Name: Consumption of fixed capital (CFC): major improvements, nonproduced assets
structure:Code.common:Description: The decline in value of major improvements to nonproduced assets, such as land reclamation or infrastructure development, over time.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net cash inflow from operating activities
structure:Code.common:Description: The net amount of cash generated from the government's regular operational activities, including tax collections and fees, minus operational expenses.

structure:Code.common:Name: Cash inflow from operating activities
structure:Code.common:Description: The cash generated by a government's regular operational activities, including tax collections, fees, and other income.

structure:Code.common:Name: Corporate income tax (CIT)
structure:Code.common:Description: A?corporate tax, also called?corporation tax?or?company tax, is a type of direct tax?levied on the income or capital of?corporations?and other similar legal entities. The tax is usually imposed at the national level, but it may also be imposed at state or local levels in some countries. Corporate taxes may be referred to as income tax or capital tax, depending on the nature of the tax.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total changes in net worth, stock-flow discrepancy
structure:Code.common:Description: The difference between total changes in net worth and the stock-flow discrepancy, indicating potential errors or inconsistencies.

structure:Code.common:Name: Cash receipts from operating activities
structure:Code.common:Description: The total cash received from a government's regular operational activities, including all forms of income and revenue.

structure:Code.common:Name: Capital spending
structure:Code.common:Description: Expenditures by the government on acquiring, constructing, or improving physical assets such as infrastructure, buildings, and equipment.

structure:Code.common:Name: Cash surplus/deficit
structure:Code.common:Description: The difference between a government's cash inflows and outflows over a specific period. A surplus indicates more inflows than outflows, while a deficit indicates more outflows than inflows.

structure:Code.common:Name: Cash surplus/deficit (adjustment)
structure:Code.common:Description: Adjustments made to the reported cash surplus or deficit to account for corrections, reallocations, or other changes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Deficit
structure:Code.common:Description: The amount by which a government's total expenditures exceed its total revenues in a specific period, leading to a shortfall that must be financed through borrowing.

structure:Code.common:Name: Debt service charges
structure:Code.common:Description: The total amount of interest payments and repayments of principal on government debt that are due within a specific period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Statistical discrepency
structure:Code.common:Description: The difference between statistical data collected from different sources or methods, indicating potential errors or inconsistencies.

structure:Code.common:Name: Fiscal end day
structure:Code.common:Description: The final day of the government's fiscal period, marking the end of the fiscal year or quarter.

structure:Code.common:Name: Fiscal impulse
structure:Code.common:Description: A measure of the change in the fiscal stance of the government, indicating the impact of fiscal policy on economic activity.

structure:Code.common:Name: Revenue
structure:Code.common:Description: Revenue refers to the total inflow of resources, typically in the form of taxes, fees, charges, grants, and other income, received by a government entity during a specific period. It represents the funds generated by the government through its various activities and sources, including taxation, sales of goods or services, investment income, and transfers from other entities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Revenue from extractive industries
structure:Code.common:Description: Government revenue generated from the extraction of natural resources, such as minerals, oil, and gas.

structure:Code.common:Name: Taxes
structure:Code.common:Description: Compulsory financial charges levied by the government on individuals, businesses, and transactions to fund public services and programs.

structure:Code.common:Name: Unallocated tax revenue
structure:Code.common:Description: Tax revenue that cannot be allocated to specific categories and is classified as miscellaneous.

structure:Code.common:Name: Taxes on income, profits, and capital gains
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes levied on the income, profits, and capital gains of individuals and businesses.

structure:Code.common:Name: Taxes on income, profits, and capital gains from extractive industries
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes levied on the income, profits, and capital gains generated by extractive industries, such as mining, oil, and gas.

structure:Code.common:Name: Unallocated taxes on income, profits, and capital gains
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes on income, profits, and capital gains that cannot be allocated to specific categories and are classified as miscellaneous.

structure:Code.common:Name: Taxes on income, profits, and capital gains, payable by individuals
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes levied on the income, profits, and capital gains of individuals.

structure:Code.common:Name: Taxes on income, profits, and capital gains, payable by corporations and other enterprises
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes levied on the income, profits, and capital gains of corporations and other business enterprises.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other taxes on income, profits, and capital gains
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes levied on income, profits, and capital gains that do not fit into specific categories.

structure:Code.common:Name: Taxes on payroll and workforce
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes levied on payroll and workforce expenses, such as social security contributions and payroll taxes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Taxes on property
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes levied on the ownership, use, or transfer of property, including real estate and personal property.

structure:Code.common:Name: Recurrent taxes on immovable property
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes levied on immovable property, such as land and buildings, on a regular basis.

structure:Code.common:Name: Recurrent taxes on net wealth
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes levied on the net wealth of individuals or entities on a regular basis.

structure:Code.common:Name: Tax, property, estate, inheritance, and gift taxes
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes levied on property ownership, estates, inheritances, and gifts.

structure:Code.common:Name: Capital levies
structure:Code.common:Description: One-time charges or taxes imposed by the government on capital assets or wealth to raise revenue for specific purposes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other recurrent taxes on property
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes levied on property on a regular basis that do not fit into specific property tax categories.

structure:Code.common:Name: Taxes on goods and services
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes levied on the sale or consumption of goods and services.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other taxes on goods and services
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes on goods and services not classified elsewhere in general taxes on goods and services or excises.

structure:Code.common:Name: General taxes on goods and services
structure:Code.common:Description: A category of taxes that includes all taxes levied on the sale or consumption of goods and services.

structure:Code.common:Name: Value added tax, goods and services
structure:Code.common:Description: A consumption tax levied on the value added at each stage of production and distribution

structure:Code.common:Name: Sales taxes
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes levied on the sale of goods and services, typically collected at the point of sale.

structure:Code.common:Name: Turnover and other general taxes on goods and services
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes levied on the total revenue generated by the sale of goods and services, including turnover taxes and general sales taxes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Taxes on financial and capital transactions
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes levied on financial and capital transactions, such as stock trades and real estate sales.

structure:Code.common:Name: Excises
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes imposed on specific goods and services, such as alcohol, tobacco, and fuel, typically included in the price of the product.

structure:Code.common:Name: Profits of fiscal monopolies
structure:Code.common:Description: Profits generated by government-owned monopolies involved in fiscal activities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Specific services tax: goods and services
structure:Code.common:Description: A tax levied on specific goods and services, such as telecommunications or tourism.

structure:Code.common:Name: Use of goods tax, goods and services
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes levied on the use of goods and services.

structure:Code.common:Name: Motor vehicles taxes
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes imposed on the ownership, registration, or use of motor vehicles.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other taxes on use of goods and on permission to use goods or perform activities
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes levied on the use of goods and services and on permissions to use goods or perform activities that do not fit into specific categories.

structure:Code.common:Name: Business and professional licenses
structure:Code.common:Description: Permits issued by government authorities that allow individuals or businesses to engage in specific professional activities or operate certain types of businesses.

structure:Code.common:Name: Pollution taxes
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes levied on activities that cause environmental pollution, intended to reduce harmful emissions and encourage cleaner practices.

structure:Code.common:Name: Radio and television licenses
structure:Code.common:Description: Fees charged by the government for issuing licenses to operate radio and television stations.

structure:Code.common:Name: Licenses and permits for households
structure:Code.common:Description: Fees charged by the government for issuing licenses and permits to households, allowing them to engage in specific activities or use certain goods.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other taxes on use of goods and on permission to use goods or perform activities not elsewhere classified
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes levied on the use of goods and services and on permissions to use goods or perform activities that do not fit into any specific tax category.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other taxes on goods and services
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes levied on the sale or consumption of goods and services that do not fit into specific categories.

structure:Code.common:Name: Taxes on international trade and transactions
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes levied on international trade and transactions, including customs duties and import/export taxes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Customs and other import duties
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes and fees imposed by the government on imported goods and services.

structure:Code.common:Name: Taxes on exports
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes levied on goods and services exported from the country.

structure:Code.common:Name: Profits of export or import monopolies
structure:Code.common:Description: Profits generated by government-owned export or import monopolies.

structure:Code.common:Name: Exchange profits
structure:Code.common:Description: Profits generated from the exchange of goods and services, including gains from favorable exchange rates.

structure:Code.common:Name: Exchange taxes
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes levied on the exchange of goods and services, including customs duties and other import/export taxes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other taxes on international trade and transactions
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes levied on international trade and transactions that do not fit into specific categories.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other taxes
structure:Code.common:Description: A category of taxes that includes all taxes levied by the government that do not fit into specific tax categories.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other taxes payable solely by business
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes that are exclusively levied on businesses.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other taxes payable by other than business or unidentifiable
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes collected from entities other than businesses or from sources that cannot be identified.

structure:Code.common:Name: Tax (adjustment)
structure:Code.common:Description: Adjustments made to the recorded tax revenue to account for corrections, reallocations, or other changes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other taxes
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes not classified elsewhere in taxes on income, profits, and capital gains, taxes on property, taxes on goods and services, or taxes on international trade and transactions.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other tax
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes collected by the government that do not fit into specific categories and are classified as miscellaneous.

structure:Code.common:Name: Tax revenue [WEO]
structure:Code.common:Description: Tax revenue data sourced from the World Economic Outlook (WEO) reports.

structure:Code.common:Name: Social contributions
structure:Code.common:Description: Compulsory payments made to social insurance schemes by employees, employers, and the self-employed to fund future social benefits.

structure:Code.common:Name: Social security contributions
structure:Code.common:Description: Compulsory payments made to social security schemes by employees, employers, and the self-employed.

structure:Code.common:Name: Social security contributions: employee contributions
structure:Code.common:Description: Contributions made by employees to social security schemes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Social security contributions: employer contributions
structure:Code.common:Description: Contributions made by employers to social security schemes on behalf of their employees.

structure:Code.common:Name: Social security contributions: self-employed or nonemployed contributions
structure:Code.common:Description: Contributions made by self-employed individuals or those not employed to social security schemes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Social security contributions: unallocable contributions
structure:Code.common:Description: Contributions to social security schemes that cannot be allocated to specific categories.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other social contributions
structure:Code.common:Description: Contributions to social security schemes and other social benefits that do not fit into specific categories.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other social contributions: employee contributions
structure:Code.common:Description: Contributions made by employees to social security schemes and other social benefits.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other social contributions: employer contributions
structure:Code.common:Description: Contributions made by employers to social security schemes and other social benefits on behalf of their employees.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other social contributions: imputed contributions
structure:Code.common:Description: Contributions that are assumed to have been made to social security schemes and other social benefits, even if no actual transaction took place.

structure:Code.common:Name: Social contributions (adjustment)
structure:Code.common:Description: Adjustments made to the recorded social contributions to account for corrections, reallocations, or other changes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Grants receivable
structure:Code.common:Description: Transfers that the government expects to receive from various entities for various purposes, including operational support and capital projects.

structure:Code.common:Name: Grants adjustment
structure:Code.common:Description: Adjustments made to recorded grants to account for corrections, reallocations, or other changes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Current grants receivable
structure:Code.common:Description: Transfers that the government expects to receive from other entities for current purposes, such as operational support or social benefits.

structure:Code.common:Name: Grants receivable from foreign governments: current grants
structure:Code.common:Description: Current grants that the government expects to receive from foreign governments for operational support or social programs.

structure:Code.common:Name: Capital grants receivable
structure:Code.common:Description: Transfers that the government expects to receive from other entities for capital purposes, such as infrastructure development or major equipment purchases.

structure:Code.common:Name: Grants receivable from foreign governments: capital grants
structure:Code.common:Description: Capital grants that the government expects to receive from foreign governments for infrastructure development or major equipment purchases.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other revenue
structure:Code.common:Description: Revenue collected by the government from various sources that do not fit into specific categories.

structure:Code.common:Name: Property income
structure:Code.common:Description: Income generated from government-owned property, including rent, leases, and sales.

structure:Code.common:Name: Interest (before FISIM allocation), receivable
structure:Code.common:Description: Interest income that the government is entitled to receive before the allocation of Financial Intermediation Services Indirectly Measured (FISIM).

structure:Code.common:Name: Dividends receivable
structure:Code.common:Description: Payments that the government expects to receive from its investments in state-owned enterprises or other equity holdings.

structure:Code.common:Name: Withdrawals from income of quasi-corporations, receivable
structure:Code.common:Description: Payments that the government expects to receive from quasi-corporations from their income, typically representing the government's share of profits or other earnings.

structure:Code.common:Name: Property income from investment income disbursements
structure:Code.common:Description: Income generated from investments in property assets, including dividends, interest, and rent.

structure:Code.common:Name: Insurance income receivable
structure:Code.common:Description: Income that the government expects to receive from insurance policies, such as premium payments or claims reimbursements.

structure:Code.common:Name: Rent, receivable
structure:Code.common:Description: Rent payments that the government expects to receive for the use of its property or land.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reinvested earnings on foreign direct investment
structure:Code.common:Description: Earnings from foreign direct investments that are reinvested in the same foreign enterprises.

structure:Code.common:Name: Sales of goods and services
structure:Code.common:Description: Revenue generated from the sale of goods and services by the government.

structure:Code.common:Name: Sales by market establishments
structure:Code.common:Description: Revenue generated from the sale of goods and services by government or nonprofit establishments operating in the market.

structure:Code.common:Name: Administrative fees
structure:Code.common:Description: Charges levied by government entities or organizations for the provision of administrative services. These fees cover the costs associated with processing applications, permits, and other administrative activities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Incidental sales by nonmarket establishments
structure:Code.common:Description: Sales of goods and services by government or nonprofit establishments that primarily do not operate in the market but occasionally sell products as a by-product of their main activities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Imputed sales of goods and services
structure:Code.common:Description: Sales that are assumed to have occurred, even if no actual transaction took place, based on

structure:Code.common:Name: Fines, penalties, and forfeits
structure:Code.common:Description: Revenue collected by the government from fines, penalties, and forfeits imposed for legal or regulatory violations.

structure:Code.common:Name: Transfers, receivable not elsewhere classified
structure:Code.common:Description: Transfer payments expected to be received that do not fit into specific categories and are classified as miscellaneous.

structure:Code.common:Name: Current transfers not elsewhere classified
structure:Code.common:Description: Transfers that do not fit into specific categories and are classified as miscellaneous current transfers.

structure:Code.common:Name: Current tansfers not elsewhere classified, Subsidies
structure:Code.common:Description: Financial assistance provided by the government to support specific sectors, activities, or entities, not classified under other categories.

structure:Code.common:Name: Current transfers not elsewhere classified: other
structure:Code.common:Description: Other financial transfers that do not fit into specific categories.

structure:Code.common:Name: Capital transfers not elsewhere classified
structure:Code.common:Description: Transfers of capital that do not fit into specific categories and are classified as miscellaneous capital transfers.

structure:Code.common:Name: Premiums, fees, and claims related to nonlife insurance and standardized guarantee schemes, receivable
structure:Code.common:Description: Amounts that the government expects to receive from nonlife insurance policies and standardized guarantee schemes, including premiums, fees, and claims.

structure:Code.common:Name: Premiums, fees, and current claims, receivable
structure:Code.common:Description: Amounts that the government expects to receive for premiums, fees, and current claims related to nonlife insurance policies and standardized guarantee schemes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Premiums receivable
structure:Code.common:Description: The amount of insurance premiums that the government expects to receive from policyholders.

structure:Code.common:Name: Fees for standardized guarantee schemes, receivable
structure:Code.common:Description: Fees that the government expects to receive from entities participating in standardized guarantee schemes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Current claims receivable
structure:Code.common:Description: Amounts that the government expects to receive from other entities for current transactions, such as taxes, fees, or transfers.

structure:Code.common:Name: Capital claims receivable
structure:Code.common:Description: Amounts that the government expects to receive from other entities for capital transactions, such as sales of nonfinancial assets or repayments of loans.

structure:Code.common:Name: Miscellaneous and unidentified revenue
structure:Code.common:Description: Revenue that cannot be classified under specific categories due to its irregular or unidentified nature.

structure:Code.common:Name: Revenue (adjustment)
structure:Code.common:Description: Adjustments made to the recorded revenue to account for corrections, reallocations, or other changes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Commodity related revenues
structure:Code.common:Description: Income generated from the production and sale of commodities such as oil, gas, minerals, and agricultural products.

structure:Code.common:Name: Grants in cash receivable
structure:Code.common:Description: Cash grants that the government expects to receive from other entities, such as local governments or international organizations.

structure:Code.common:Name: Grants in kind receivable
structure:Code.common:Description: Non-cash grants that the government expects to receive from other entities, such as goods or services provided by local governments or international organizations.

structure:Code.common:Name: Primary revenue
structure:Code.common:Description: The government's total revenue excluding any interest income.

structure:Code.common:Name: Tax revenue
structure:Code.common:Description: Revenue generated from taxes levied by the government on individuals, businesses, and transactions.

structure:Code.common:Name: Revenue, excluding grants
structure:Code.common:Description: Revenue refers to the total inflow of resources, typically in the form of taxes, fees, charges, grants, and other income, received by a government entity during a specific period. It represents the funds generated by the government through its various activities and sources, including taxation, sales of goods or services, investment income, and transfers from other entities. This indicator excludes grants receivable. Grants are transfers receivable (payable) by government units, from (to) other resident or non-resident government units or international organisations, that do not meet the definition of a tax, subsidy, or social contribution.

structure:Code.common:Name: Non-oil revenue
structure:Code.common:Description: Government revenue generated from sources other than oil production and related activities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Expense
structure:Code.common:Description: The total outflow of resources, including payments, purchases, and transfers, made by a government entity during a specific period to fulfill its various functions and obligations.

structure:Code.common:Name: Compensation of employees
structure:Code.common:Description: The total remuneration, including wages, salaries, and benefits, paid to employees by the government for their work.

structure:Code.common:Name: Wages and salaries
structure:Code.common:Description: The total remuneration paid to employees by the government, including regular pay, bonuses, and other compensation.

structure:Code.common:Name: Wages and salaries in cash [GFS]
structure:Code.common:Description: Cash payments made by the government to employees as part of their wages and salaries, recorded in the Government Finance Statistics (GFS).

structure:Code.common:Name: Wages and salaries in kind [GFS]
structure:Code.common:Description: Non-cash benefits provided by the government to employees as part of their wages and salaries, such as housing or transportation, recorded in the Government Finance Statistics (GFS).

structure:Code.common:Name: Employers' social contributions
structure:Code.common:Description: Payments made by employers to social security schemes or other social insurance programs on behalf of their employees.

structure:Code.common:Name: Actual employers' social contributions [GFS]
structure:Code.common:Description: Payments made by employers to social security schemes, recorded in the Government Finance Statistics (GFS). These contributions are intended to provide future social benefits for employees.

structure:Code.common:Name: Imputed employers' social contributions [GFS]
structure:Code.common:Description: Social contributions that are assumed to have been made by employers on behalf of their employees, recorded in the Government Finance Statistics (GFS).

structure:Code.common:Name: Use of goods and services
structure:Code.common:Description: The consumption of goods and services by the government for its operational activities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Consumption of fixed capital (CFC)
structure:Code.common:Description: The systematic allocation of the cost of fixed assets over their useful lives, reflecting the reduction in their value over time.

structure:Code.common:Name: Interest payable
structure:Code.common:Description: The amount of interest that the government is obligated to pay on its borrowed funds.

structure:Code.common:Name: Subsidies payable
structure:Code.common:Description: Amounts that the government owes as subsidies to various sectors, activities, or entities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Grants payable
structure:Code.common:Description: Transfers that the government provides to other entities for various purposes, including operational support and capital projects.

structure:Code.common:Name: Current grants payable
structure:Code.common:Description: Transfers that the government provides to other entities for current purposes, such as operational support or social benefits.

structure:Code.common:Name: Grants payable to foreign governments: current grants
structure:Code.common:Description: Current grants that the government provides to foreign governments for operational support or social programs.

structure:Code.common:Name: Grants payable to international organizations: current grants
structure:Code.common:Description: Current grants that the government provides to international organizations for operational support or social programs.

structure:Code.common:Name: Grants payable to foreign governments
structure:Code.common:Description: Transfers that the government provides to foreign governments for various purposes, including development assistance and disaster relief.

structure:Code.common:Name: Grants receivable from foreign governments
structure:Code.common:Description: Transfers that the government expects to receive from foreign governments for various purposes, including development assistance and disaster relief.

structure:Code.common:Name: Capital grants payable
structure:Code.common:Description: Transfers that the government provides to other entities for capital purposes, such as infrastructure development or major equipment purchases.

structure:Code.common:Name: Grants payable to foreign governments: capital grants
structure:Code.common:Description: Capital grants that the government provides to foreign governments for infrastructure development or major equipment purchases.

structure:Code.common:Name: Grants payable to international organizations: capital grants
structure:Code.common:Description: Capital grants that the government provides to international organizations for infrastructure development or major equipment purchases.

structure:Code.common:Name: Social benefits
structure:Code.common:Description: Financial or in-kind benefits provided by the government to individuals or households to support their well-being, including social assistance, pensions, and unemployment benefits.

structure:Code.common:Name: Social security benefits
structure:Code.common:Description: Benefits provided by social security schemes, including pensions, unemployment benefits, and disability payments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Social security benefits in cash
structure:Code.common:Description: Cash payments provided by social security schemes to beneficiaries.

structure:Code.common:Name: Social security benefits in kind
structure:Code.common:Description: Non-cash benefits provided by social security schemes, such as healthcare or housing assistance.

structure:Code.common:Name: Social benefits other than social transfers in kind (nonmarket production)
structure:Code.common:Description: Benefits provided by the government through nonmarket production, excluding social transfers in kind.

structure:Code.common:Name: Social benefits other than social transfers in kind
structure:Code.common:Description: Benefits provided by the government that do not fit into the category of social transfers in kind, such as direct financial assistance.

structure:Code.common:Name: Social assistance benefits
structure:Code.common:Description: Government-provided financial assistance to individuals or households in need, aimed at improving their economic well-being.

structure:Code.common:Name: Social assistance benefits in cash [GFS]
structure:Code.common:Description: Cash payments provided by the government to individuals or households as social assistance benefits, recorded in the Government Finance Statistics (GFS).

structure:Code.common:Name: Social assistance benefits in kind [GFS]
structure:Code.common:Description: Non-cash benefits provided by the government to individuals or households, such as food, housing, or medical services, recorded in the Government Finance Statistics (GFS).

structure:Code.common:Name: Employer social benefits
structure:Code.common:Description: Benefits provided by employers to their employees, including health insurance, retirement benefits, and other welfare benefits.

structure:Code.common:Name: Employer social benefits in cash [GFS]
structure:Code.common:Description: Cash payments made by employers to employees as part of social benefits, recorded in the Government Finance Statistics (GFS).

structure:Code.common:Name: Employer social benefits in kind [GFS]
structure:Code.common:Description: Non-cash benefits provided by employers to employees, such as health care or housing, recorded in the Government Finance Statistics (GFS).

structure:Code.common:Name: Other expense
structure:Code.common:Description: Expenses incurred by the government that do not fit into specific categories and are classified as miscellaneous expenses.

structure:Code.common:Name: Property expense other than interest
structure:Code.common:Description: Property-related expenses that do not include interest payments, such as maintenance, insurance, and taxes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Dividends payable
structure:Code.common:Description: Payments that the government owes to shareholders of state-owned enterprises as a distribution of profits.

structure:Code.common:Name: Withdrawals from income of quasi-corporations, payable
structure:Code.common:Description: Payments that quasi-corporations are required to make to the government from their income, typically representing the government's share of profits or other earnings.

structure:Code.common:Name: Property expense for investment income disbursements
structure:Code.common:Description: Expenses related to the disbursement of investment income from property assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Rent payable
structure:Code.common:Description: Rent payments that the government owes for the use of property or land.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reinvested earnings on foreign direct investment, payable
structure:Code.common:Description: Earnings from foreign direct investments that are reinvested in the same foreign enterprises, representing amounts owed to foreign investors.

structure:Code.common:Name: Miscellaneous non-interest property expense
structure:Code.common:Description: Property-related expenses that do not involve interest payments, such as repairs and operational costs.

structure:Code.common:Name: Miscellaneous current property expense other than interest
structure:Code.common:Description: Expenses related to property that do not include interest payments, such as maintenance, insurance, and taxes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Miscellaneous non-interest property expense: capital
structure:Code.common:Description: Capital expenses related to property that do not involve interest, such as major repairs and improvements.

structure:Code.common:Name: Transfers payable not elsewhere classified
structure:Code.common:Description: Transfer payments that do not fit into specific categories and are classified as miscellaneous.

structure:Code.common:Name: Current transfers n.e.c.: other current expense
structure:Code.common:Description: Financial transfers that do not fit into specific categories and are classified as other current expenses.

structure:Code.common:Name: Capital transfers not elsewhere classified: other capital expense
structure:Code.common:Description: Transfers of capital that do not fit into specific categories and are classified as other capital expenses. These transfers may include various types of capital transactions.

structure:Code.common:Name: Premiums, fees, and claims related to nonlife insurance and standardized guarantee schemes
structure:Code.common:Description: Payments related to nonlife insurance policies and standardized guarantee schemes, including premiums, fees, and claims.

structure:Code.common:Name: Premiums, fees, and current claims, payable
structure:Code.common:Description: Amounts that the government owes for premiums, fees, and current claims related to nonlife insurance policies and standardized guarantee schemes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Premiums, payable (premiums, fees, and claims related to nonlife insurance and standardized guarantee schemes)
structure:Code.common:Description: Amounts that the government owes for premiums related to nonlife insurance policies and standardized guarantee schemes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Fees for standardized guarantee schemes, payable
structure:Code.common:Description: Fees that the government owes for participation in standardized guarantee schemes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Capital claims payable (premiums, fees, and claims related to nonlife insurance and standardized guarantee schemes)
structure:Code.common:Description: Amounts owed by the government for premiums, fees, and claims related to nonlife insurance policies and standardized guarantee schemes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Premiums, fees, and claims related to nonlife insurance and standardized guarantee schemes, capital claims
structure:Code.common:Description: Capital claims related to nonlife insurance policies and standardized guarantee schemes, including premiums and fees.

structure:Code.common:Name: Premiums, fees, and claims related to nonlife insurance and standardized guarantee schemes: current claims payable
structure:Code.common:Description: Current claims related to nonlife insurance policies and standardized guarantee schemes, including premiums and fees.

structure:Code.common:Name: Expense not elsewhere classified
structure:Code.common:Description: Expenses that do not fit into specific categories and are classified as miscellaneous expenses.

structure:Code.common:Name: Expense (adjustment)
structure:Code.common:Description: Adjustments made to recorded expenses to account for corrections, reallocations, or other changes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Expense excluding consumption of fixed capital
structure:Code.common:Description: The total outflow of resources for operating expenses, excluding the depreciation of fixed assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Expense and investment in nonfinancial assets
structure:Code.common:Description: The total outflow of resources for operating expenses and the acquisition of nonfinancial assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Expenditure
structure:Code.common:Description: Expenditure refers to the total outflow of resources, including payments, purchases, and transfers, made by a government entity during a specific period to fulfill its various functions and obligations. It encompasses spending on goods and services, wages and salaries, social benefits, debt servicing, infrastructure investments, and other government programs and activities. Expenditure represents the utilization of government funds to provide public services, maintain infrastructure, implement policies, and meet financial obligations. Monitoring expenditure patterns and allocations provides insight into government priorities, policy objectives, and fiscal sustainability.

structure:Code.common:Name: Social benefits in cash
structure:Code.common:Description: Cash payments provided by the government to individuals or households as social benefits.

structure:Code.common:Name: Social benefits in kind
structure:Code.common:Description: Non-cash benefits provided by the government to individuals or households as social benefits.

structure:Code.common:Name: Social transfers in kind (purchased market production)
structure:Code.common:Description: Non-cash benefits provided by the government through the purchase of goods and services from the market, distributed to beneficiaries.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total expenditure and net lending / net borrowing
structure:Code.common:Description: Expenditure refers to the total outflow of resources, including payments, purchases, and transfers, made by a government entity during a specific period to fulfill its various functions and obligations. It encompasses spending on goods and services, wages and salaries, social benefits, debt servicing, infrastructure investments, and other government programs and activities. Expenditure represents the utilization of government funds to provide public services, maintain infrastructure, implement policies, and meet financial obligations. Monitoring expenditure patterns and allocations provides insight into government priorities, policy objectives, and fiscal sustainability. Net lending is defined as the difference between changes in net worth due to saving and capital transfers and net acquisitions of non-financial assets (acquisitions less disposals of non-financial assets, less depreciation). If the amount is negative, it represents net borrowing. In the external accounts, it represents the sum of the balances on the current and capital accounts. This is conceptually equal to the net balance of the financial account. If the balance is positive, it is called net lending, implying that in net terms, the economy supplies funds to the rest of the world. If the balance is negative, it is called net borrowing, implying that in net terms, the economy receives funds from the rest of the world.

structure:Code.common:Name: Primary expenditure (expenditure less interest payable)
structure:Code.common:Description: The government's total expenditure excluding interest payments on debt.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net transactions in assets and liabilities
structure:Code.common:Description: The difference between the acquisition and disposal of assets and the incurrence and repayment of liabilities by the government.

structure:Code.common:Name: Investment in nonfinancial assets (acquisitions less disposals)
structure:Code.common:Description: Expenditures by the government on acquiring, constructing, or improving physical assets such as infrastructure, buildings, and equipment.

structure:Code.common:Name: Acquisitions of nonfinancial assets: domestic
structure:Code.common:Description: The purchase or acquisition of nonfinancial assets within the domestic economy. These assets include physical assets like infrastructure, buildings, machinery, and land.

structure:Code.common:Name: Acquisitions of nonfinancial assets
structure:Code.common:Description: Assets other than financial assets, where financial assets repressent financial claims, and gold bullion held by monetary authorities as a reserve asset.

structure:Code.common:Name: Acquisitions of nonfinancial assets: excluding cash
structure:Code.common:Description: The purchase or acquisition of nonfinancial assets excluding cash transactions. This includes physical assets and other non-monetary items.

structure:Code.common:Name: Disposals of nonfinancial assets
structure:Code.common:Description: The process of selling, transferring, or otherwise disposing of nonfinancial assets, such as land, buildings, and equipment.

structure:Code.common:Name: Consumption of fixed capital
structure:Code.common:Description: The decline in the value of fixed assets over time due to wear and tear, obsolescence, or other factors. This concept is similar to depreciation in business accounting.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net acquisition of financial assets
structure:Code.common:Description: The difference between the acquisition and disposal of financial assets by the government, representing the net increase in financial assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net acquisition of financial assets, policy lending
structure:Code.common:Description: The net increase in the government's financial assets resulting from policy-driven lending activities, such as loans to support economic development.

structure:Code.common:Name: Acquisitions of nonfinancial assets: foreign
structure:Code.common:Description: The purchase or acquisition of nonfinancial assets located in foreign economies. These can include properties, businesses, and other physical assets outside the domestic economy.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net acquisition of financial assets (adjustment)
structure:Code.common:Description: Adjustments made to the recorded net acquisition of financial assets to account for corrections, reallocations, or other changes.
