structure:Code.common:Name: Net acquisition of financial assets other than cash
structure:Code.common:Description: The net increase in the government's financial assets excluding cash, such as investments in securities or loans.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net acquisition of financial assets other than cash: domestic
structure:Code.common:Description: The net increase in the government's financial assets within the domestic economy, excluding cash.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net acquisition of financial assets other than cash: foreign
structure:Code.common:Description: The net increase in the government's financial assets in foreign economies, excluding cash.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net incurrence of liabilities
structure:Code.common:Description: The net increase in the government's liabilities to domestic creditors, representing new borrowing from domestic sources minus repayments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net incurrence of liabilities: domestic
structure:Code.common:Description: The net increase in the government's liabilities within the domestic economy, representing new borrowing minus repayments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net incurrence of liabilities: foreign
structure:Code.common:Description: The net increase in the government's liabilities in foreign economies, representing new borrowing minus repayments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net incurrence of liabilities (adjustment)
structure:Code.common:Description: Adjustments made to the recorded net incurrence of liabilities to account for corrections, reallocations, or other changes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net incurrence of foreign liabilities (adjustment)
structure:Code.common:Description: Adjustments made to the recorded net incurrence of foreign liabilities to account for corrections, reallocations, or other changes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Change in net debt due to transactions
structure:Code.common:Description: The change in the government's net debt resulting from economic transactions, including borrowing, repayments, and other financial activities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net incurrence of liabilities: domestic debtors
structure:Code.common:Description: The net increase in the government's liabilities to domestic debtors, representing new borrowing from domestic sources minus repayments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net incurrence of liabilities: external creditors
structure:Code.common:Description: The net increase in the government's liabilities to foreign creditors, representing new borrowing from foreign sources minus repayments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net incurrence of liabilities: external debtors
structure:Code.common:Description: The net increase in the government's liabilities to foreign debtors, representing new borrowing from foreign sources minus repayments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Own-account capital formation
structure:Code.common:Description: The process of creating capital assets by the government for its own use rather than purchasing them.

structure:Code.common:Name: Own-account capital formation: compensation of employees
structure:Code.common:Description: The cost of employee compensation involved in the creation of capital assets for the government's own use.

structure:Code.common:Name: Own-account capital formation: use of goods and services
structure:Code.common:Description: The cost of goods and services consumed in the creation of capital assets for the government's own use.

structure:Code.common:Name: Own-account capital formation: consumption of fixed capital
structure:Code.common:Description: The depreciation of fixed assets involved in the creation of capital assets for the government's own use.

structure:Code.common:Name: Own-account capital formation: other taxes on producation minus other subsidies on production
structure:Code.common:Description: The net amount of other taxes on production minus subsidies on production involved in the creation of capital assets for the government's own use.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net transactions in financial assets and liabilities
structure:Code.common:Description: The difference between the acquisition and disposal of financial assets and the incurrence and repayment of financial liabilities by the government.

structure:Code.common:Name: Change in net worth due to holding gains and losses
structure:Code.common:Description: The change in the government's net worth resulting from changes in the value of its assets and liabilities due to market fluctuations or other factors.

structure:Code.common:Name: Holding gains and losses in nonfinancial assets
structure:Code.common:Description: Changes in the value of nonfinancial assets due to market fluctuations or other factors.

structure:Code.common:Name: Holding gains and losses in financial assets
structure:Code.common:Description: Changes in the value of financial assets due to market fluctuations or other factors.

structure:Code.common:Name: Holding gains and losses in liabilities
structure:Code.common:Description: Changes in the value of liabilities due to market fluctuations or other factors.

structure:Code.common:Name: Change in net debt due to holding gains and losses
structure:Code.common:Description: The change in the government's net debt resulting from changes in the value of its debt instruments due to market fluctuations or other factors.

structure:Code.common:Name: Change in net financial worth due to holding gains and losses
structure:Code.common:Description: The change in the government's net financial worth resulting from changes in the value of its financial assets and liabilities due to market fluctuations or other factors.

structure:Code.common:Name: Change in net worth due to volume changes
structure:Code.common:Description: The change in the government's net worth due to changes in the volume of assets and liabilities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other volume changes in nonfinancial assets
structure:Code.common:Description: Changes in the value of nonfinancial assets due to factors other than transactions, such as revaluations or other volume changes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other volume changes in financial assets
structure:Code.common:Description: Changes in the value of financial assets due to factors other than transactions, such as revaluations or other volume changes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other volume changes in liabilities
structure:Code.common:Description: Changes in the value of liabilities due to factors other than transactions, such as revaluations or other volume changes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Change in net debt due to volume changes
structure:Code.common:Description: The change in the government's net debt due to changes in the volume of debt instruments, such as issuance or redemption of bonds.

structure:Code.common:Name: Change in net financial worth due to volume changes
structure:Code.common:Description: The change in the government's net financial worth due to changes in the volume of financial assets and liabilities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net worth
structure:Code.common:Description: The difference between the government's total assets and total liabilities, representing its net financial position.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net worth lagged by one period
structure:Code.common:Description: The government's net worth from the previous accounting period, used for comparative analysis.

structure:Code.common:Name: Closing stock position of nonfinancial assets
structure:Code.common:Description: The value of the government's nonfinancial assets at the end of a specific period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Closing stock position of financial assets
structure:Code.common:Description: The value of the government's financial assets at the end of a specific period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Closing stock position of financial assets: domestic
structure:Code.common:Description: The value of the government's financial assets held within the domestic economy at the end of a specific period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Closing stock position of financial assets: foreign
structure:Code.common:Description: The value of the government's financial assets held in foreign economies at the end of a specific period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Closing stock position of liabilities
structure:Code.common:Description: The value of the government's liabilities at the end of a specific period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Closing stock position of liabilities: domestic
structure:Code.common:Description: The value of the government's liabilities held within the domestic economy at the end of a specific period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Closing stock position of liabilities: foreign
structure:Code.common:Description: The value of the government's liabilities held in foreign economies at the end of a specific period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Closing stock position of contingent liabilities
structure:Code.common:Description: The value of contingent liabilities that the government holds at the end of a specific period. Contingent liabilities are potential obligations that may arise based on the outcome of future events.

structure:Code.common:Name: Gross debt
structure:Code.common:Description: Gross debt is the sum of all liabilities that are debt instruments. Debt instruments are financial instruments that require the payment of principal and/or interest at some point(s) in the future. Debt instruments consist of SDRs, currency and deposits, debt securities, loans, insurance technical reserves, pension and related entitlements, provision for calls under standardized guarantees, and other accounts receivable/payable.

structure:Code.common:Name: Gross debt denominated in domestic currency
structure:Code.common:Description: The total amount of government debt denominated in the domestic currency.

structure:Code.common:Name: Gross debt denominated in foreign currency
structure:Code.common:Description: The total amount of government debt denominated in foreign currencies.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net debt
structure:Code.common:Description: Net debt is the sum of all liabilities less financial assets that are debt instruments. Debt instruments are financial instruments that require the payment of principal and/or interest at some point(s) in the future. Debt instruments consist of SDRs, currency and deposits, debt securities, loans, insurance technical reserves, pension and related entitlements, provision for calls under standardized guarantees, and other accounts receivable/payable.

structure:Code.common:Name: Closing stock position of liabilities net of currency and deposits assets
structure:Code.common:Description: The value of the government's liabilities minus its assets held in the form of currency and deposits at the end of a specific period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Closing net financial worth
structure:Code.common:Description: The government's net financial worth at the end of a specific period, calculated as the difference between its financial assets and liabilities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Implicit transfers resulting from loan liabilities at concessional interest rates
structure:Code.common:Description: Financial transfers that result from loans provided at below-market interest rates, representing a form of subsidy.

structure:Code.common:Name: Change in net worth due to other economic flows
structure:Code.common:Description: The change in the government's net worth due to factors other than transactions, such as revaluations or other changes in volume.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other economic flows in nonfinancial assets
structure:Code.common:Description: Changes in the value of nonfinancial

structure:Code.common:Name: Other economic flows in financial assets
structure:Code.common:Description: Changes in the value of financial assets due to economic flows other than transactions, such as revaluations or other volume changes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other economic flows in liabilities
structure:Code.common:Description: Changes in the value of liabilities due to economic flows other than transactions, such as revaluations or other volume changes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Change in net debt due to other economic flows
structure:Code.common:Description: The change in the government's net debt due to factors other than transactions, such as revaluations or other changes in volume.

structure:Code.common:Name: Change in net financial worth due to other economic flows
structure:Code.common:Description: The change in the government's net financial worth due to factors other than transactions, such as revaluations or other changes in volume.

structure:Code.common:Name: Purchases of nonfinancial assets
structure:Code.common:Description: Expenditures by the government on acquiring physical assets such as infrastructure, buildings, and equipment.

structure:Code.common:Name: Gross financing requirement
structure:Code.common:Description: The total amount of financing needed to cover the government's budget deficit and refinance maturing debt. In general this reflects the general government fiscal deficit (excluding grants) and general government external and domestic amortization

structure:Code.common:Name: Government balance per national definition
structure:Code.common:Description: The government's fiscal balance as defined by national accounting standards, reflecting the difference between total revenue and total expenditure.

structure:Code.common:Name: Gross operating balance
structure:Code.common:Description: The difference between total revenue and total operating expenses, excluding capital expenditures and interest payments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Cash inflow from financing activities
structure:Code.common:Description: The cash received from financing activities such as borrowing, issuing bonds, or receiving grants.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net lending (+) / net borrowing (-)
structure:Code.common:Description: Net lending is defined as the difference between changes in net worth due to saving and capital transfers and net acquisitions of non-financial assets (acquisitions less disposals of non-financial assets, less depreciation). If the amount is negative, it represents net borrowing. In the external accounts, it represents the sum of the balances on the current and capital accounts. This is conceptually equal to the net balance of the financial account. If the balance is positive, it is called net lending, implying that in net terms, the economy supplies funds to the rest of the world. If the balance is negative, it is called net borrowing, implying that in net terms, the economy receives funds from the rest of the world.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net lending (+) / net borrowing (-) (adjustment)
structure:Code.common:Description: Adjustments made to the recorded net lending or borrowing to account for corrections, reallocations, or other changes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net lending (+) / net borrowing (-) excluding social security schemes
structure:Code.common:Description: The government's net lending or borrowing excluding the transactions and balances related to social security schemes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net operating balance
structure:Code.common:Description: The difference between the government's total revenue and total operating expenses, excluding capital expenditures and interest payments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net operating balance (adjustment)
structure:Code.common:Description: Adjustments made to the recorded net operating balance to account for corrections, reallocations, or other changes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Primary net lending (+) / net borrowing (-)
structure:Code.common:Description: Primary net lending/borrowing refers to the difference between a government's total revenue (excluding borrowing) and its total expenditures (excluding debt repayments and interest payments). It represents the government's fiscal position, indicating whether it is running a surplus (positive value) or a deficit (negative value) before considering the impact of debt servicing costs.

structure:Code.common:Name: Primary net cash inflow from operating activities
structure:Code.common:Description: The net amount of cash generated from the government's operating activities excluding interest payments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Intermediate consumption
structure:Code.common:Description: The value of goods and services consumed as inputs in the production process, excluding fixed assets. This consumption is subtracted from the total output to calculate value added.

structure:Code.common:Name: Indirect tax
structure:Code.common:Description: An?indirect tax?(such as sales tax, per unit tax, value-added tax (VAT), or goods and services tax (GST), excise, consumption tax, tariff) is a?tax?that is levied upon goods and services before they reach the customer who ultimately pays the indirect tax as a part of market price of the good or service purchased.

structure:Code.common:Name: Memo item: expenditure
structure:Code.common:Description: An additional item in financial accounts that records expenditure not included in the main accounting categories, used for supplementary information.

structure:Code.common:Name: Market output
structure:Code.common:Description: The total value of goods and services produced for sale at market prices.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net acquisition of nonfinancial assets
structure:Code.common:Description: The difference between the acquisition and disposal of nonfinancial assets by the government, representing the net increase in physical assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net acquisition of nonfinancial assets (adjustment)
structure:Code.common:Description: Adjustments made to the recorded net acquisition of nonfinancial assets to account for corrections, reallocations, or other changes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net change in the stock of cash
structure:Code.common:Description: The difference between the opening and closing balances of cash held by the government over a specific period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net change in the stock of financial assets/liabilities
structure:Code.common:Description: The difference between the opening and closing balances of financial assets and liabilities held by the government over a specific period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net cash inflow from financing activities
structure:Code.common:Description: The net amount of cash received from financing activities, including borrowing and issuing bonds, minus repayments and interest payments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net financial worth
structure:Code.common:Description: The difference between the government's total financial assets and total liabilities, representing its net financial position.

structure:Code.common:Name: Stock-flow discrepancy, net financial worth
structure:Code.common:Description: The difference between changes in stocks (assets and liabilities) and flows (transactions) that affect the net financial worth of the government.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net nonlife insurance premiums
structure:Code.common:Description: The total amount of premiums received from nonlife insurance policies, minus claims and administrative costs.

structure:Code.common:Name: Non-tax revenues
structure:Code.common:Description: Government revenue generated from sources other than taxes, such as fees, fines, and income from state-owned enterprises.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other non-tax revenues
structure:Code.common:Description: Revenue not classified elsewhere in taxes, social contributions, grants receivable, or non-tax revenue from extractive industries.

structure:Code.common:Name: Non-tax revenue from extractive industries
structure:Code.common:Description: Revenue generated from non-tax sources in the extractive industries, such as royalties, fees, and sales of extracted resources.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other non-tax revenue
structure:Code.common:Description: Revenue not classified elsewhere in taxes, social contributions, grants receivable, or non-tax revenue from extractive industries.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net privatization proceeds
structure:Code.common:Description: The net amount of revenue received from the sale of government-owned assets or enterprises, after deducting the costs associated with the privatization process.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other changes in the volume of assets
structure:Code.common:Description: Changes in the value of assets due to factors other than transactions, such as revaluations or other volume changes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Overall fiscal balance
structure:Code.common:Description: The difference between the government's total revenue and total expenditure, indicating whether it is running a surplus or deficit.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other revenue: interest income
structure:Code.common:Description: Interest income earned by the government from various sources, excluding taxes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other taxes on production less other subsidies on production
structure:Code.common:Description: The net amount of taxes on production minus subsidies on production that do not fit into specific categories.

structure:Code.common:Name: Overall balance
structure:Code.common:Description: The overall balance represents the difference between a government's total revenue and its total expenditure over a specific period, typically a fiscal year. It reflects the net financial position of the government, indicating whether it is running a surplus (positive overall balance) or a deficit (negative overall balance). The overall balance takes into account all sources of revenue, including taxes, fees, and grants, as well as all types of expenditure, such as salaries, public services, and debt servicing costs. Monitoring the overall balance is crucial for assessing the government's fiscal health, its ability to meet its financial obligations, and the sustainability of its budgetary policies

structure:Code.common:Name: Overall balance excluding oil revenue
structure:Code.common:Description: The overall balance represents the difference between a government's total revenue and its total expenditure over a specific period, typically a fiscal year. It reflects the net financial position of the government, indicating whether it is running a surplus (positive overall balance) or a deficit (negative overall balance). The overall balance takes into account all sources of revenue, including taxes, fees, and grants, as well as all types of expenditure, such as salaries, public services, and debt servicing costs. Monitoring the overall balance is crucial for assessing the government's fiscal health, its ability to meet its financial obligations, and the sustainability of its budgetary policies. This indicator excludes government revenues and expenditures from oil production related activities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Overall balance excluding privatization
structure:Code.common:Description: The government's overall fiscal balance excluding revenues from the sale of government-owned assets or enterprises.

structure:Code.common:Name: Overall primary balance
structure:Code.common:Description: The difference between the government's total revenue and total expenditure excluding interest payments, indicating its fiscal position before debt servicing costs.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other voluntary transfers: current transfers
structure:Code.common:Description: Current transfers that do not fit into specific categories and are classified as miscellaneous.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other voluntary transfers
structure:Code.common:Description: Financial transfers that do not fit into specific categories and are classified as miscellaneous.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other voluntary transfers: capital transfers
structure:Code.common:Description: Capital transfers that do not fit into specific categories and are classified as miscellaneous.

structure:Code.common:Name: Output for own final use
structure:Code.common:Description: Goods and services produced by the government for its own use rather than for sale or distribution.

structure:Code.common:Name: Output, except other nonmarket output
structure:Code.common:Description: Goods and services produced by the government for sale or distribution, excluding those produced for its own use.

structure:Code.common:Name: Personal income tax (PIT)
structure:Code.common:Description: Personal income tax is a tax levied on the income earned by individuals. It is imposed by government authorities at the federal, state, and local levels and is typically calculated based on a progressive tax rate structure, where higher levels of income are taxed at higher rates. Personal income tax serves as a significant source of revenue for governments, funding public services, social welfare programs, infrastructure projects, and other government expenditures.

structure:Code.common:Name: Policy lending
structure:Code.common:Description: Loans provided by the government to support specific policy objectives, such as economic development or social welfare.

structure:Code.common:Name: Payments for other non-market output
structure:Code.common:Description: Payments made for goods and services produced by non-market establishments that do not operate primarily in the market.

structure:Code.common:Name: Public sector net cash requirement
structure:Code.common:Description: The total amount of cash needed by the public sector to meet its financial obligations.

structure:Code.common:Name: Privatization proceeds
structure:Code.common:Description: Revenue received from the sale of government-owned assets or enterprises.

structure:Code.common:Name: Revenue decentralization
structure:Code.common:Description: The process of transferring revenue-generating powers from central to local governments to enhance local financial autonomy.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reporting scale
structure:Code.common:Description: The scale or level at which financial data is reported, such as national, regional, or local levels.

structure:Code.common:Name: Type of general sales tax
structure:Code.common:Description: VAT if the country has one, empty otherwise. VAT variable also indicated the implementation date for countires that implemented in 1980 or after.

structure:Code.common:Name: Structural balance
structure:Code.common:Description: The government's budget balance adjusted for the economic cycle, representing the underlying fiscal position.

structure:Code.common:Name: Structural primary balance
structure:Code.common:Description: The primary budget balance adjusted for the economic cycle, excluding interest payments on debt.

structure:Code.common:Name: Expenditure decentralization
structure:Code.common:Description: The process of transferring authority and responsibility for public spending from central to local governments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Social security contribution
structure:Code.common:Description: Social security contributions are?compulsory payments paid to general government that confer entitlement to receive a (contingent) future social benefit.

structure:Code.common:Name: Tax revenue decentralization
structure:Code.common:Description: The process of transferring tax revenue-generating powers from central to local governments to enhance local financial autonomy.

structure:Code.common:Name: General sales taxes collected on imports
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes collected on imported goods and services at the point of entry into the country.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total changes in net worth
structure:Code.common:Description: The overall change in the government's net worth over a specific period, including changes in assets and liabilities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total outlays
structure:Code.common:Description: The total amount of government expenditures, including operating expenses, capital expenditures, and transfer payments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Transfer dependency method 1
structure:Code.common:Description: A method used to calculate the dependency of a government entity on transfer payments from other entities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Transfer dependency method 2
structure:Code.common:Description: An alternative method used to calculate the dependency of a government entity on transfer payments from other entities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Value-added tax (VAT)
structure:Code.common:Description: A Value-Added Tax (VAT) is?a consumption tax assessed on the value added in each production stage of a good or service. Every business along the value chain receives a tax credit for the VAT already paid. The end consumer does not, making it a tax on final consumption.

structure:Code.common:Name: Vertical fiscal imbalance
structure:Code.common:Description: A situation where there is a mismatch between the revenue-raising powers and expenditure responsibilities of different levels of government, often requiring transfers from higher to lower levels of government to address the imbalance.

structure:Code.common:Name: Fiscal revenue
structure:Code.common:Description: The total amount of funds collected by a government from various sources, including taxes, fees, charges, grants, and other income.

structure:Code.common:Name: Employers' social contributions: actual
structure:Code.common:Description: This refers to the mandatory payments made by employers to social security programs and other social insurance schemes on behalf of their employees.

structure:Code.common:Name: Employers' social contributions: imputed
structure:Code.common:Description: In some cases, governments provide social benefits directly to employees or self-employed individuals without requiring employers to make explicit contributions. In these situations, an imputed value is assigned to represent the cost of these benefits if they were financed through employer contributions.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other revenue: adjustment
structure:Code.common:Description: This is a broad category that encompasses various adjustments and miscellaneous sources of government revenue that don't fit neatly into other classifications.

structure:Code.common:Name: Taxes on immovable property
structure:Code.common:Description: These are taxes levied on real estate or landed property.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net lending (+) / net borrowing (-) excluding grants
structure:Code.common:Description: This indicator measures the difference between a government's total revenue and its total expenditure, excluding grants from other governments or international organizations.

structure:Code.common:Name: Overall fiscal balance, excluding grants
structure:Code.common:Description: The difference between total revenue, excluding grants, and total expenditure over a specific period. This balance indicates the overall fiscal position of the government, excluding the impact of grants.

structure:Code.common:Name: Cyclically adjusted balance (with exception for countries with adjustments beyond the cycle)
structure:Code.common:Description: This is a measure of a government's budget balance that attempts to isolate the effects of the business cycle. It estimates what the budget balance would be if the economy were operating at its potential output (i.e., no inflationary or recessionary gaps).

structure:Code.common:Name: Cyclically adjusted primary balance (with exception for countries with adjustments beyond the cycle)
structure:Code.common:Description: This is similar to the cyclically adjusted balance but excludes net interest payments on government debt. The primary balance focuses on government revenue and expenditure related to its core operations, excluding the cost of servicing past debt.

structure:Code.common:Name: Social security contributions, unallocable contributions
structure:Code.common:Description: This refers to social security contributions that cannot be directly assigned or allocated to specific individuals or programs.

structure:Code.common:Name: Oil revenue
structure:Code.common:Description: The income a country generates from the extraction, production, and sale of crude oil and related petroleum products. This can include revenue from exports, taxes on oil companies, and royalties.

structure:Code.common:Name: Revenue, including grants
structure:Code.common:Description: It refers to the total income a government receives from all sources, including both its own revenue-generating activities and grants from external sources.

structure:Code.common:Name: Overall primary balance excluding grants
structure:Code.common:Description: This measures the difference between a government's primary revenue (excluding grants) and its primary expenditure.

structure:Code.common:Name: Overall primary balance, excluding grants, excluding oil
structure:Code.common:Description: This is a more specific measure that further refines the primary balance by removing both oil-related revenues and oil-related expenditures.

structure:Code.common:Name: Fiscal balance calculated (oil revenue minus non-oil current account balance), central government
structure:Code.common:Description: This is a specific calculation of the central government's fiscal balance that takes into account oil revenue and the non-oil current account balance.

structure:Code.common:Name: Overall fiscal balance, excluding oil-related revenues
structure:Code.common:Description: The difference between a government's total revenue (excluding oil revenue) and its total expenditure.

structure:Code.common:Name: Operating expenditure
structure:Code.common:Description: Recurring expenses incurred by the government for its day-to-day operations. This includes salaries, wages, pensions, subsidies, and other administrative costs.

structure:Code.common:Name: Capital expenditures, oil related
structure:Code.common:Description: Investments in long-term assets related to the oil sector, such as infrastructure for oil extraction, pipelines, and refineries.

structure:Code.common:Name: Subsidies and transfers
structure:Code.common:Description: Government payments to individuals or businesses for various purposes, such as social welfare programs, agricultural support, or industry subsidies.

structure:Code.common:Name: Overall primary balance, excluding oil
structure:Code.common:Description: Similar to the overall primary balance but excludes both oil revenue and oil-related expenditures.

structure:Code.common:Name: Oil revenue from exports
structure:Code.common:Description: The portion of oil revenue specifically generated from exporting crude oil and petroleum products to other countries.

structure:Code.common:Name: Fiscal revenue, oil related
structure:Code.common:Description: All government revenue directly related to the oil sector, including taxes, royalties, and other oil-related income.

structure:Code.common:Name: National defense expenditures
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on the military, including salaries, equipment, and operations.

structure:Code.common:Name: Gross financing sources
structure:Code.common:Description: This is a broad term referring to all the ways a government obtains funds to finance its activities. It includes revenue, borrowing, and other inflows.

structure:Code.common:Name: Gross financing sources (general government)
structure:Code.common:Description: This is more specific, focusing on the financing sources of the "general government" sector. The general government usually includes the central government, state and local governments, and social security funds. It excludes public corporations and other government-controlled entities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Holding gains and losses
structure:Code.common:Description: These are changes in the value of a government's assets or liabilities that are not due to transactions.

structure:Code.common:Name: Expense, consumption of fixed capital
structure:Code.common:Description: This refers to the decline in the value of fixed assets (like buildings, machinery, and infrastructure) over time due to wear and tear, obsolescence, or age. It's essentially the depreciation of these assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net/Gross investment in nonfinancial assets
structure:Code.common:Description: This refers to the acquisition of new nonfinancial assets (like buildings, roads, and equipment) by the government, minus the disposal of existing assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Environmental taxes
structure:Code.common:Description: A tax whose tax base is a physical unit (or a proxy of it) of something that has a proven, specific, negative impact on the environment. These are subdivided into four types of taxes: taxes on energy (including fuel for transport); taxes on transport (excluding fuel for transport), taxes on pollution and taxes on resources.

structure:Code.common:Name: Environmental taxes, Taxes on energy (including fuel for transport)
structure:Code.common:Description: A tax whose tax base is a physical unit (or a proxy of it) of something that has a proven, specific, negative impact on the environment. These are subdivided into four types of taxes: taxes on energy (including fuel for transport); taxes on transport (excluding fuel for transport), taxes on pollution and taxes on resources.

structure:Code.common:Name: Environmental taxes, Taxes on pollution
structure:Code.common:Description: A tax whose tax base is a physical unit (or a proxy of it) of something that has a proven, specific, negative impact on the environment. These are subdivided into four types of taxes: taxes on energy (including fuel for transport); taxes on transport (excluding fuel for transport), taxes on pollution and taxes on resources.

structure:Code.common:Name: Environmental taxes, Taxes on resources
structure:Code.common:Description: A tax whose tax base is a physical unit (or a proxy of it) of something that has a proven, specific, negative impact on the environment. These are subdivided into four types of taxes: taxes on energy (including fuel for transport); taxes on transport (excluding fuel for transport), taxes on pollution and taxes on resources.

structure:Code.common:Name: Environmental taxes, Taxes on transport (excluding fuel for transport)
structure:Code.common:Description: A tax whose tax base is a physical unit (or a proxy of it) of something that has a proven, specific, negative impact on the environment. These are subdivided into four types of taxes: taxes on energy (including fuel for transport); taxes on transport (excluding fuel for transport), taxes on pollution and taxes on resources.

structure:Code.common:Name: Revenue and grants
structure:Code.common:Description: The sum of total revenue received by the government and grants receivable from various entities, including both current and capital grants.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total revenue and grants (G)
structure:Code.common:Description: A specific category or sub-component of total revenue and grants, potentially related to a particular type of grant, a specific source of funding, or a defined geographic area.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total government expenditure (XP)
structure:Code.common:Description: This refers to all spending by the government on goods, services, and transfer payments (like social benefits).

structure:Code.common:Name: Net lending (+) / net borrowing (-) (XC)
structure:Code.common:Description: This is a core measure of the fiscal balance. It shows the difference between a government's total revenue and its total expenditure.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total expenditure including net lending / net borrowing
structure:Code.common:Description: The total outflow of resources by the government over a specific period, including spending on goods and services, transfers, and net lending or net borrowing activities. Net lending refers to loans provided by the government, while net borrowing represents loans received.

structure:Code.common:Name: Gross debt (XWDG)
structure:Code.common:Description: This is the total amount of outstanding debt owed by the government.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net debt (XWDN)
structure:Code.common:Description: This is a more refined measure of government debt. It subtracts any financial assets held by the government from its gross debt.

structure:Code.common:Name: Overall primary balance excluding grants (NLBXG)
structure:Code.common:Description: The primary balance of the government (revenue minus expenditure, excluding interest payments), further excluding grants received.

structure:Code.common:Name: Primary fiscal balance, excluding oil related transactions
structure:Code.common:Description: The primary balance of the government (revenue minus expenditure, excluding interest payments), excluding revenue and expenditure directly related to oil extraction, production, and sales.

structure:Code.common:Name: Fiscal impulse (EUR)
structure:Code.common:Description: A measure of the change in the fiscal stance of the government, indicating the impact of fiscal policy on economic activity.

structure:Code.common:Name: Transfers payable
structure:Code.common:Description: Transfers, payable including pensions, social security, unemployment insurances, other transfers n.e.c.

structure:Code.common:Name: Financing of additional infrastructure / public spending if not already incorporated in cyclically adjusted primary balance
structure:Code.common:Description: Financing of additional infrastructure/public spending if not already incorporated in cyclically adjusted primary balance

structure:Code.common:Name: Recommended cyclically adjusted primary balance
structure:Code.common:Description: This is a measure used to assess a government's fiscal position

structure:Code.common:Name: Capital taxes
structure:Code.common:Description: These are taxes on things people own, like property (real estate), stocks, bonds, and other investments. They can also include taxes on wealth transfers, such as inheritance taxes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Labor taxes
structure:Code.common:Description: These are taxes on people's income from working.

structure:Code.common:Name: Current and projected infrastructure / public investment
structure:Code.common:Description: Current and projected infrastructure/public investment.

structure:Code.common:Name: Recommended infrastructure / public investment
structure:Code.common:Description: Recommended infrastructure/public investment.

structure:Code.common:Name: Expenditure decentralization (ratio of own spending to general government spending)
structure:Code.common:Description: A measure of expenditure decentralization, calculated as the ratio of sub-national government spending to general government spending over a specific period. This ratio indicates the distribution of spending authority between different levels of government.

structure:Code.common:Name: Fiscal balance, excluding oil related transactions
structure:Code.common:Description: The overall fiscal balance of the government (total revenue minus total expenditure), excluding revenue and expenditure directly related to oil extraction, production, and sales.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other public financing sources, GG gross financing sources
structure:Code.common:Description: Public financing sources other than traditional debt or revenue, such as asset sales, privatization proceeds, or other non-debt financing instruments, contributing to the general government's gross financing needs.

structure:Code.common:Name: Domestic debt gross issuance, GG gross financing sources
structure:Code.common:Description: The total value of new debt instruments issued by the government within its own country, contributing to general government gross financing sources.

structure:Code.common:Name: External debt gross issuance, GG gross financing sources
structure:Code.common:Description: The total value of new debt instruments issued by the government in foreign markets or to foreign lenders, contributing to general government gross financing sources.

structure:Code.common:Name: External market debt issuance, GG gross financing sources
structure:Code.common:Description: The total value of new debt instruments issued by the government specifically in international capital markets, a subset of external debt issuance, contributing to general government gross financing sources.

structure:Code.common:Name: Domestic amortization, GG gross financing needs
structure:Code.common:Description: The repayment of principal on outstanding domestic debt obligations by the government, contributing to general government gross financing needs.

structure:Code.common:Name: External amortization, GG gross financing needs
structure:Code.common:Description: The repayment of principal on outstanding external debt obligations by the government, contributing to general government gross financing needs.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net investment in nonfinancial assets, Acquisitions (++)
structure:Code.common:Description: The net investment (acquisitions minus disposals) by the government in nonfinancial assets, such as infrastructure, buildings, and equipment, indicating a higher level or intensity of acquisition activity.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net investment in nonfinancial assets, Acquisitions (+)
structure:Code.common:Description: The net investment (acquisitions minus disposals) by the government in nonfinancial assets, such as infrastructure, buildings, and equipment, indicating a moderate level of acquisition activity.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total
structure:Code.common:Description: The sum of all relevant components or categories.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net acquisition of financial assets, Policy lending
structure:Code.common:Description: Loans provided by the government to support specific policy objectives, such as economic development or social welfare.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net acquisition of financial assets: foreign
structure:Code.common:Description: The difference between the acquisition and disposal of foreign financial assets by the government, representing the net increase in financial assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Domestic excluding cash
structure:Code.common:Description: Domestic excluding cash.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net investement in nonfinanical assets, Consumption of fixed capital (--)
structure:Code.common:Description: Net investment in nonfinancial assets, Consumption of fixed capital (--).

structure:Code.common:Name: Gross debt at market value
structure:Code.common:Description: Gross debt is the sum of all liabilities that are debt instruments. Debt instruments are financial instruments that require the payment of principal and/or interest at some point(s) in the future. Debt instruments consist of SDRs, currency and deposits, debt securities, loans, insurance technical reserves, pension and related entitlements, provision for calls under standardized guarantees, and other accounts receivable/payable. Debt is valued at markt value.

structure:Code.common:Name: Adjustment (GFS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Adjustment (GFS).

structure:Code.common:Name: Stock-flow discrepancy, Change in net worth vs change in stocks
structure:Code.common:Description: Stock-flow discrepancy, Change in net worth vs change in stocks.

structure:Code.common:Name: Stock-flow discrepancy
structure:Code.common:Description: Stock-flow discrepancy.

structure:Code.common:Name: Buildings other than dwellings (acquisitions less disposals)
structure:Code.common:Description: Buildings other than dwellings (acquisitions less disposals).

structure:Code.common:Name: Machinery and equipment (acquisitions less disposals)
structure:Code.common:Description: Machinery and equipment (acquisitions less disposals).

structure:Code.common:Name: Weapons systems (acquisitions less disposals)
structure:Code.common:Description: Weapons systems (acquisitions less disposals).

structure:Code.common:Name: Inventories by type of inventory (acquisitions less disposals)
structure:Code.common:Description: Inventories by type of inventory (acquisitions less disposals).

structure:Code.common:Name: Buildings and structures
structure:Code.common:Description: Buildings and structures.

structure:Code.common:Name: Buildings and structures (acquisitions less disposals)
structure:Code.common:Description: Buildings and structures (acquisitions less disposals).

structure:Code.common:Name: Social security benefits: Unemployment benefits
structure:Code.common:Description: Social security benefits: Unemployment benefits.

structure:Code.common:Name: Social security benefits: Family benefits
structure:Code.common:Description: Social security benefits: Family benefits.

structure:Code.common:Name: Social security benefits: Care benefits
structure:Code.common:Description: Social security benefits: Care benefits.

structure:Code.common:Name: Social security benefits: In-work benefits
structure:Code.common:Description: Social security benefits: In-work benefits.

structure:Codelist.common:Name: COFOG
structure:Codelist.common:Description: This codelist represents the Classification of the Functions of Government (COFOG) 1999, a standardized system for classifying government expenditures by their purpose.

structure:Code.common:Name: Economic affairs n.e.c. (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Economic affairs expenditures that do not fit into other specific categories.

structure:Code.common:Name: R&D General economic, commercial and labour affairs (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on research and development related to general economic issues, commerce, and labor markets.

structure:Code.common:Name: R&D Agriculture, forestry, fishing and hunting (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on research and development related to agriculture, forestry, fishing, and hunting.

structure:Code.common:Name: R&D Fuel and energy (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on research and development related to energy production, distribution, and efficiency.

structure:Code.common:Name: R&D Mining, manufacturing and construction (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on research and development related to the mining, manufacturing, and construction industries.

structure:Code.common:Name: R&D Transport (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on research and development related to transportation technologies and infrastructure.

structure:Code.common:Name: R&D Communication (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on research and development related to communication technologies and infrastructure.

structure:Code.common:Name: R&D Other industries (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on research and development related to industries not categorized elsewhere.

structure:Code.common:Name: Distributive trades, storage and warehousing (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government support for wholesale and retail trade, logistics, and warehousing, including infrastructure development and regulation.

structure:Code.common:Name: Hotels and restaurants (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government support for the hospitality industry, including hotels, restaurants, and tourism.

structure:Code.common:Name: Tourism (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government support for the tourism industry, including marketing campaigns, infrastructure development, and tourism promotion.

structure:Code.common:Name: Multi-purpose development projects (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on large-scale development projects that have multiple objectives, such as economic development, social welfare, and environmental protection.

structure:Code.common:Name: Communication (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Expenses related to telecommunications infrastructure, regulation, and services.

structure:Code.common:Name: Road transport (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on road infrastructure, including highways, streets, and bridges.

structure:Code.common:Name: Water transport (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on water transportation infrastructure, including ports, waterways, and support for shipping.

structure:Code.common:Name: Railway transport (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on railway infrastructure, including tracks, trains, and stations.

structure:Code.common:Name: Air transport (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on air transportation infrastructure, including airports, air traffic control, and subsidies for airlines.

structure:Code.common:Name: Pipeline and other transport (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on pipeline transport and other modes of transportation not categorized elsewhere, such as cable cars and ferries.

structure:Code.common:Name: Mining of mineral resources other than mineral fuels (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on the mining of minerals other than fossil fuels, such as metals and industrial minerals.

structure:Code.common:Name: Manufacturing (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government support for the manufacturing sector, including subsidies, tax incentives, and infrastructure development.

structure:Code.common:Name: Construction (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on public construction projects, such as roads, bridges, buildings, and other infrastructure.

structure:Code.common:Name: Coal and other solid mineral fuels (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending related to the coal industry and the extraction and utilization of other solid mineral fuels.

structure:Code.common:Name: Petroleum and natural gas (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending related to the petroleum and natural gas industry, including exploration, production, and distribution.

structure:Code.common:Name: Nuclear fuel (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending related to nuclear fuel, including production, processing, and waste management.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other fuels (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on fuels not categorized elsewhere, such as biomass, geothermal, and other alternative energy sources.

structure:Code.common:Name: Electricity (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on electricity infrastructure, including power generation, transmission, and distribution, as well as subsidies and regulations related to the electricity sector.

structure:Code.common:Name: Non-electric energy (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on energy sources other than electricity, such as petroleum, natural gas, and renewable energy.

structure:Code.common:Name: Agriculture (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Expenditures on support for agricultural production, including subsidies, research, and development, and other programs to promote farming and food production.

structure:Code.common:Name: Forestry (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on forestry management, including forest conservation, reforestation, and support for the timber industry.

structure:Code.common:Name: Fishing and hunting (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on the management and regulation of fishing and hunting activities, including conservation efforts and support for the fishing and hunting industries.

structure:Code.common:Name: General economic and commercial affairs (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on policies and programs to promote economic growth and trade, such as trade agreements, export promotion, and investment incentives.

structure:Code.common:Name: General labour affairs (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on labor market policies and programs, such as job training, unemployment benefits, and labor law enforcement.

structure:Code.common:Name: Protection of biodiversity and landscape (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Spending on conservation of natural habitats, species protection, and landscape preservation.

structure:Code.common:Name: Pollution abatement (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government efforts to reduce pollution through regulation, incentives, and cleanup programs.

structure:Code.common:Name: Waste water management (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Expenses related to the treatment and management of wastewater.

structure:Code.common:Name: Waste management (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on waste collection, treatment, and disposal.

structure:Code.common:Name: R&D Environmental protection (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Research and development focused on environmental protection and sustainability.

structure:Code.common:Name: Environmental protection n.e.c. (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Environmental protection expenditures not categorized elsewhere.

structure:Code.common:Name: Housing and community amenities n.e.c. (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Expenditures on housing and community amenities that are not categorized into more specific sub-categories within this function.

structure:Code.common:Name: R&D Housing and community amenities (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Research and development expenses aimed at improving housing and community amenities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Street lighting (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Expenses related to maintaining street lighting systems.

structure:Code.common:Name: Water supply (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Expenditures on providing clean water to households and businesses, including infrastructure and treatment facilities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Community development (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on improving local communities, including infrastructure, social services, and economic development.

structure:Code.common:Name: Housing development (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government investment in affordable housing initiatives and housing programs.

structure:Code.common:Name: Health n.e.c. (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Health-related expenditures not categorized elsewhere.

structure:Code.common:Name: R&D Health (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Research and development focused on improving healthcare and medical treatments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Public health services (IS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Expenditures on public health programs, such as disease prevention, health education, and sanitation.

structure:Code.common:Name: General hospital services (IS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on general hospitals, including operating costs, staff salaries, and medical supplies.

structure:Code.common:Name: Specialized hospital services (IS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on specialized hospitals, such as psychiatric hospitals, children's hospitals, and cancer centers.

structure:Code.common:Name: Medical and maternity centre services (IS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on medical and maternity centers, including clinics, birthing centers, and other outpatient facilities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Nursing and convalescent home services (IS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on nursing homes and convalescent care facilities.

structure:Code.common:Name: General medical services (IS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on general medical services, such as doctor's visits, primary care, and preventive medicine.

structure:Code.common:Name: Specialized medical services (IS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on specialized medical services, such as cardiology, oncology, and neurology.

structure:Code.common:Name: Dental services (IS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on dental care services, including dental clinics, subsidies for dental treatment, and dental health programs.

structure:Code.common:Name: Paramedical services (IS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on paramedical services, such as ambulance services, physiotherapy, and occupational therapy.

structure:Code.common:Name: Pharmaceutical products (IS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on pharmaceuticals, including subsidies for prescription drugs and support for pharmaceutical research and development.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other medical products (IS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on medical products not categorized elsewhere, such as diagnostic tools, medical textiles, and laboratory supplies.

structure:Code.common:Name: Therapeutic appliances and equipment (IS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on therapeutic appliances and equipment, such as wheelchairs, prosthetics, and medical braces.

structure:Code.common:Name: Recreation, culture and religion n.e.c. (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Recreational, cultural, and religious expenditures not categorized elsewhere.

structure:Code.common:Name: R&D Recreation, culture and religion (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Research and development aimed at improving recreational, cultural, and religious activities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Religious and other community services (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Spending on religious institutions and community organizations that provide social services.

structure:Code.common:Name: Broadcasting and publishing services (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government support for public broadcasting, media, and publishing industries.

structure:Code.common:Name: Cultural services (IS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Expenditures on cultural institutions (museums, theaters), arts programs, and heritage preservation.

structure:Code.common:Name: Recreational and sporting services (IS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on recreational facilities, parks, sports programs, and other leisure activities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Education n.e.c. (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Education-related expenditures not categorized elsewhere.

structure:Code.common:Name: R&D Education (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Research and development focused on improving educational outcomes and methods.

structure:Code.common:Name: Subsidiary services to education (IS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Expenditures on support services for education, such as transportation, meals, and school supplies.

structure:Code.common:Name: Education not definable by level (IS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Educational expenses that cannot be categorized by a specific level.

structure:Code.common:Name: First stage of tertiary education (IS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on the first stage of tertiary education, which typically includes bachelor's degrees and equivalent programs.

structure:Code.common:Name: Second stage of tertiary education (IS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on the second stage of tertiary education, which typically includes master's degrees, doctoral degrees, and equivalent programs.

structure:Code.common:Name: Post-secondary non-tertiary education (IS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government funding for vocational training and other non-university post-secondary education.

structure:Code.common:Name: Lower-secondary education (IS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on lower-secondary education, which typically includes grades 7-9 or equivalent.

structure:Code.common:Name: Upper-secondary education (IS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on upper-secondary education, which typically includes grades 10-12 or equivalent.

structure:Code.common:Name: Pre-primary education (IS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending specifically on pre-primary education, such as preschool and kindergarten.

structure:Code.common:Name: Primary education (IS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending specifically on primary education, which typically includes grades 1-6 or equivalent.

structure:Code.common:Name: Social protection n.e.c. (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Social protection expenditures not categorized elsewhere.

structure:Code.common:Name: R&D Social protection (CS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Research and development aimed at improving social protection programs and policies.

structure:Code.common:Name: Social exclusion n.e.c. (IS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Expenditures on programs to address social exclusion and poverty not categorized elsewhere.

structure:Code.common:Name: Housing (IS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Spending on housing assistance programs for low-income individuals and families.

structure:Code.common:Name: Unemployment (IS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government expenditures on unemployment benefits and job training programs.

structure:Code.common:Name: Family and children (IS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Spending on family support programs, child care, and other services for children and families.

structure:Code.common:Name: Survivors (IS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government payments to surviving family members of deceased workers.

structure:Code.common:Name: Old age (IS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Expenditures on pensions and other social security programs for the elderly.

structure:Code.common:Name: Sickness (IS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on programs that provide financial support to individuals who are sick or temporarily disabled, such as sick leave benefits and disability insurance.

structure:Code.common:Name: Disability (IS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on programs and services for people with disabilities, including income support, rehabilitation, and accessibility services.

structure:Code.common:Name: Sickness and disability
structure:Code.common:Description: Government spending on programs that provide financial support to individuals with illnesses or disabilities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Old age
structure:Code.common:Description: Expenditures on pensions and other social security programs for the elderly.

structure:Code.common:Name: Survivors
structure:Code.common:Description: Government payments to surviving family members of deceased workers.

structure:Code.common:Name: Cost, insurance, and freight Northwest Europe

It indicates that the seller is responsible for the costs, insurance, and freight of delivering the product to a port in Northwest Europe assumes responsibility for the goods once they are loaded onto the ship at the port of origin. NEW likely refers to a specific geographic region or port, but without further context, it's difficult to be certain.
