structure:Codelist.common:Name: Statistical Measures
structure:Codelist.common:Description: This codelist describe characteristics of a group of data. They summarize the distribution, central tendency, or spread of multiple values.

structure:Code.common:Name: Maximum value
structure:Code.common:Description: In a dataset or set of numbers, the maximum value refers to the largest or highest value present.

structure:Code.common:Name: Mean
structure:Code.common:Description: The mean is a measure of central tendency, calculated by summing all values in a dataset and dividing by the number of values.

structure:Code.common:Name: Minimum value
structure:Code.common:Description: The minimum value is the smallest or lowest value within a dataset. It represents the lower limit of the data range.

structure:Code.common:Name: Standard deviation
structure:Code.common:Description: A statistical measure that quantifies the amount of variation or dispersion of a set of values from their average (mean).

structure:Code.common:Name: Individual forecast
structure:Code.common:Description: An estimated future value or outcome of a random variable for a specific individual observation expressed as a conditional expectation or probability.

structure:Code.common:Name: Median
structure:Code.common:Description: The median is the middle value in a data set when the values are arranged in ascending or descending order.

structure:Code.common:Name: Lag 1 (Opening)
structure:Code.common:Description: A value for a variable that refers to a one-period delay of that variable relative to its current value.

structure:Code.common:Name: 60-day moving average
structure:Code.common:Description: A statistical measure that smooths time-series data by calculating the average of a variable over the most recent 60 days, updating the average each day.

structure:Code.common:Name: 60-month moving average
structure:Code.common:Description: An average of a variable over the most recent 60 months, updating the average each month to track long-term trends.

structure:Code.common:Name: Rate
structure:Code.common:Description: A measure that expresses the frequency of occurrence of an event or phenomenon in relation to another quantity.

structure:Code.common:Name: Rate, 60-day moving average
structure:Code.common:Description: The average of rates (e.g., stock prices, sales figures) over the past 60 days, updating the rate each day.

structure:Code.common:Name: Rate, 60-month moving average
structure:Code.common:Description: The average of rates (e.g., stock prices, sales figures) over the past 60 months, updating the rate each month.

structure:Code.common:Name: 95 percent interval - lower bound
structure:Code.common:Description: The lower bound of a 95 percent confidence interval, representing the lower limit within which a parameter is likely to fall.

structure:Code.common:Name: 95 percent interval - upper bound
structure:Code.common:Description: The upper bound of a 95 percent confidence interval, representing the upper limit within which a parameter is likely to fall.

structure:Code.common:Name: Z-Score
structure:Code.common:Description: A statistical measure that determines how many standard deviations a value is from the mean of a dataset

structure:Code.common:Name: Sustainability Logit Metric
structure:Code.common:Description: A metric that uses a logistic transformation to assess the sustainability of a particular system or behavior.

structure:Code.common:Name: Null value
structure:Code.common:Description: A variable that has no assigned value (either no data is available, not applicable or is unknown for a given field)

structure:Code.common:Name: Aggregate Z-score
structure:Code.common:Description: A combined Z-score, aggregating multiple Z-scores to evaluate overall performance or comparison.

structure:Code.common:Name: Sustainability Logit Z-score
structure:Code.common:Description: A Z-score derived from the Sustainability Logit Metric to assess sustainability on a comparable, unit-free scale.

structure:Code.common:Name: Scaling factor
structure:Code.common:Description: A constant number used to multiply or divide values in order to change their scale, magnitude, or units while preserving their relative relationships.

structure:Code.common:Name: Signal
structure:Code.common:Description: An early indicator of change or risk that refers to the magnitude of an effect

structure:Code.common:Name: Rank
structure:Code.common:Description: Ranking determines the position of a value within a set of values when they're arranged in order (either largest to smallest or smallest to largest).

structure:Code.common:Name: Scores
structure:Code.common:Description: Scores provided to a categorial variable indicates ranking relative to a benchmark or a distribution.

structure:Code.common:Name: Sum
structure:Code.common:Description: The total obtained by adding together all values in a dataset or set of numbers, either over a given period or across a group of observations.

structure:Codelist.common:Name: Observation Status
structure:Codelist.common:Description: This codelist indicates the status of an observation within a dataset, such as whether it is a provisional value, an estimated value, a final figure, or a value where a time series break occurs. (Source: SDMX)

structure:Code.common:Name: Normal value
structure:Code.common:Description: To be used as default value if no value is provided or when no special coded qualification is assumed. Usually, it can be assumed that the source agency assigns sufficient confidence to the provided observation and/or the value is not expected to be dramatically revised.

structure:Code.common:Name: Time series break
structure:Code.common:Description: Observations are characterised as such when different content exists or a different methodology has been applied to this observation as compared with the preceding one (the one given for the previous period).

structure:Code.common:Name: Definition differs
structure:Code.common:Description: Used to indicate slight deviations from the established methodology (footnote-type information); these divergences do not imply a break in time series.

structure:Code.common:Name: Estimated value
structure:Code.common:Description: Observation obtained through an estimation methodology (e.g. to produce back-casts) or based on the use of a limited amount of data or ad hoc sampling and through additional calculations (e.g. to produce a value at an early stage of the production stage while not all data are available). It may also be used in case of experimental data (e.g. in the context of a pilot ahead of a full scale production process) or in case of data of (anticipated/assessed) low quality. If needed, additional information can be provided through free text using the COMMENT_OBS attribute at the observation level or at a higher level. This code is to be used when the estimation is done by a sender agency. When the imputation is carried out by a receiver agency in order to replace or fill gaps in reported data series, the flag to use is I "Value imputed by a receiving agency".

structure:Code.common:Name: Forecast value
structure:Code.common:Description: Value deemed to assess the magnitude which a quantity will assume at some future point of time (as distinct from "estimated value" which attempts to assess the magnitude of an already existent quantity).

structure:Code.common:Name: Experimental value
structure:Code.common:Description: Data collected on the basis of definitions or (alternative) collection methods under development. Data not of guaranteed quality as normally expected from provider.

structure:Code.common:Name: Data included in another category
structure:Code.common:Description: This code is used when data for a given category are missing and are included in another category, sub-total or total. Generally where code "K" is used there should be a corresponding code "W - Includes data from another category" assigned to the over-covered category. Implementers and data reporters should use the COMMENT_OBS observation-level attribute to specify under which category the data are included.

structure:Code.common:Name: Includes data from another category
structure:Code.common:Description: This code is used when data include another category, or go beyond the scope of the data collection and are therefore over-covered. Generally, where code "W" is used there should be a corresponding code "K - Data included in another category" assigned to the category which is under-covered. Implementers and data reporters should use the COMMENT_OBS observation-level attribute to specify which additional data are included.

structure:Code.common:Name: Missing value
structure:Code.common:Description: This code is to be used when no breakdown is made between the reasons why data are missing. Data can be missing due to many reasons: data cannot exist, data exist but are not collected (e.g. because they are below a certain threshold or subject to a derogation clause), data are unreliable, etc.

structure:Code.common:Name: Missing value; data cannot exist
structure:Code.common:Description: Used to denote empty cells resulting from the impossibility to collect a statistical value (e.g. a particular education level or type of institution may be not applicable to a given country's education system).

structure:Code.common:Name: Provisional value
structure:Code.common:Description: An observation is characterised as "provisional" when the source agency - while it bases its calculations on its standard production methodology - considers that the data, almost certainly, are expected to be revised.

structure:Code.common:Name: Strike and other special events
structure:Code.common:Description: Special circumstances (e.g. strike) affecting the observation or causing a missing value.

structure:Code.common:Name: Missing value; data exist but were not collected
structure:Code.common:Description: Used, for example, when some data are not reported/disseminated because they are below a certain threshold.

structure:Code.common:Name: Missing value; holiday or weekend
structure:Code.common:Description: Used in some daily data flows.

structure:Code.common:Name: Missing value; suppressed
structure:Code.common:Description: Used, for example, when data are suppressed due to statistical confidentiality considerations.

structure:Code.common:Name: Derogation
structure:Code.common:Description: Clause in an agreement (e.g. legal act, gentlemen's agreement) stating that some provisions in the agreement are not to be implemented by designated parties; these derogations may affect the observation or cause a missing value. In general, derogations are limited in time.

structure:Code.common:Name: Not significant
structure:Code.common:Description: Used to indicate a value which is not a "real" zero (e.g. a result of 0.0004 rounded to zero).

structure:Code.common:Name: Low reliability
structure:Code.common:Description: This indicates existing observations, but for which the user should also be aware of the low quality assigned.

structure:Code.common:Name: Unvalidated value
structure:Code.common:Description: Observation as received from the respondent without further evaluation of data quality.

structure:Code.common:Name: Derived value
structure:Code.common:Description: A value that is calculated or estimated, rather than directly observed or measured.

structure:Code.common:Name: Value imputed
structure:Code.common:Description: A value that is estimated or assigned when it cannot be directly measured or observed. Observation imputed by a receiving agency to replace or fill gaps in reported data series. This code is intended to cover all cases where a receiving agency publishes data about a sending agency that do not come from an official source in the sender agency's reporting framework. When the estimation is done by the sender agency, the flag to use is E "Estimated value".

structure:Code.common:Name: Derived from counterpart country data
structure:Code.common:Description: Data that is estimated or calculated based on information obtained from counterpart countries.

structure:Code.common:Name: Unknown
structure:Code.common:Description: This code is used when the observation status (rather than the value) is not available.

structure:Code.common:Name: Observation status unavailable from external organisation
structure:Code.common:Description: This code is used when the observation is from an external organization and the observation status (rather than the value) is not available. The observation may be from an external organization that does not use any system of flags when sharing data. Implementers should use attributes at the observation-level or at a higher-level such as: COMMENT_OBS, DATA_SOURCE or NATURE, to provide information on the source or nature.

structure:Code.common:Name: Excludes one or more subcategories
structure:Code.common:Description: This code is used when data exclude one or several subcategories that it should normally include, resulting in under-coverage of the category. This situation typically arises when the category is an aggregate and code ‘K’ or ‘O’ applies to one (or several) of its subcategories.

Maturity of Financial Instrument
structure:Codelist.common:Description: A classification of financial instruments based on their remaining time to maturity or expiration.

structure:Code.common:Name: Short-term
structure:Code.common:Description: The original contract specifies a maturity of one year or less, or repayment on demand (short-term maturity).

structure:Code.common:Name: Short-term, remaining maturity basis
structure:Code.common:Description: Short term on a remaining maturity basis. Indicates residual maturity of one year or less at reference date.

structure:Code.common:Name: Long-term
structure:Code.common:Description: The original contract specifies a maturity of more than one year, or has no stated maturity (long-term maturity).

structure:Code.common:Name: Bid yield to maturity
structure:Code.common:Description: The bid yield is the yield to maturity corresponding to the current bid price (the price at which a bond can be purchased). YTM is calculated implicitly from the current market price, the remaining term to maturity, and the amount and frequency of coupon payments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Yield to maturity
structure:Code.common:Description: A bond’s yield to maturity (YTM) is the internal rate of return (IRR) that equates the present value of all future cash flows from the bond, including coupon payments and principal, to its current market price

structure:Code.common:Name: All original maturities
structure:Code.common:Description: Financial instruments with their initial maturity at issuance.

structure:Code.common:Name: All original maturities with long-term residual maturity over 1 year
structure:Code.common:Description: Financial instruments initially issued for any term, with more than one year remaining until maturity.

structure:Code.common:Name: All original maturities with short-term residual maturity up to 1 year
structure:Code.common:Description: Instruments initially issued for any term, with up to one year remaining until maturity.

structure:Code.common:Name: Long-term original maturity over 1 year with long-term residual maturity over 1 year
structure:Code.common:Description: Instruments initially issued for more than one year, with more than one year remaining until maturity.

structure:Code.common:Name: Long-term by original maturity with payment due in one year or less
structure:Code.common:Description: Instruments initially issued for more than one year, with one year or less remaining until maturity.

structure:Code.common:Name: Not allocated/unspecified
structure:Code.common:Description: Financial instruments or data that have not been categorized or specified.

structure:Code.common:Name: Not applicable
structure:Code.common:Description: Not applicable

structure:Code.common:Name: Total residual maturity
structure:Code.common:Description: Remaining (residual) maturity aggregated across all instruments in the category.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other long-term
structure:Code.common:Description: Other long-term

structure:Code.common:Name: Other short-term
structure:Code.common:Description: Other short-term

structure:Code.common:Name: Over 3 months and up to 1 Year
structure:Code.common:Description: Under the original contract, payment falls due in more than three months and within one year.

structure:Code.common:Name: Up to 1 year
structure:Code.common:Description: Under the original contract, payment falls due within one year.

structure:Code.common:Name: Agreed maturity
structure:Code.common:Description: Maturity agreed between the parties to the transaction.

structure:Code.common:Name: Up to 1 month
structure:Code.common:Description: Under the original contract, payment falls due within one month.

structure:Code.common:Name: More than 3 months and up to 1 year
structure:Code.common:Description: Under the original contract, payment falls due in more than three months and within one year.

structure:Code.common:Name: More than 1 and up to 3 months
structure:Code.common:Description: Under the original contract, payment falls due in more than one month and within three months.

structure:Code.common:Name: Falling due within 1 year
structure:Code.common:Description: Under the original contract, payment falls due within one year.

structure:Code.common:Name: Residual maturity more than 1 year
structure:Code.common:Description: Remaining or residual maturity (payment due) specified on the original contract is more than 1 year.

structure:Code.common:Name: Over 5 years
structure:Code.common:Description: Indicates a financial instrument with an original or remaining maturity exceeding 5 years.

structure:Code.common:Name: Short to medium term
structure:Code.common:Description: Refers to instruments with a maturity period that spans from short-term to medium-term duration.

structure:Code.common:Name: Short-term by original maturity
structure:Code.common:Description: The original contract specifies a maturity of one year or less, or repayment on demand (short-term maturity).

structure:Code.common:Name: Overnight
structure:Code.common:Description: Instruments with a maturity of one day, repayable on the next business day.

structure:Code.common:Name: Up to 2 years
structure:Code.common:Description: Long-term instruments with maturity of up to two years.

structure:Code.common:Name: 1 Year
structure:Code.common:Description: Short-term instruments with maturity of up to one year.

structure:Code.common:Name: 1 Month
structure:Code.common:Description: Short-term instruments with maturity of up to one month.

structure:Code.common:Name: 6 Months
structure:Code.common:Description: Short-term instruments with maturity of up to six months.

structure:Code.common:Name: 3 Months
structure:Code.common:Description: Short-term instruments with maturity of up to three months.

structure:Codelist.common:Name: Trade flow
structure:Codelist.common:Description: Data related to the movement of goods and services between countries, including exports and imports.

structure:Code.common:Name: Goods
structure:Code.common:Description: Physical, tangible products that are traded internationally.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total imports
structure:Code.common:Description: Total imports reflects the change in the economic ownership of products from non-residents to residents of the compiling economy, irrespective of physical movement of goods across national borders.

structure:Code.common:Name: Imports
structure:Code.common:Description: Imports of goods are recorded at the time when they enter the economic territory of a country.

structure:Code.common:Name: Imports of manufactures
structure:Code.common:Description: The total value of manufactured goods sold by foreign sellers to domestic purchasers

structure:Code.common:Name: Imports of non-oil related products
structure:Code.common:Description: The total value of non-oil-related products bought by a country from foreign sellers.

structure:Code.common:Name: Imports of oil related products
structure:Code.common:Description: The total value of oil-related products bought by a country from foreign sellers.

structure:Code.common:Name: Re-imports
structure:Code.common:Description: Re-imports are domestic goods imported in the same state as previously exported, without any substantial transformation occurring on the goods while they were outside the territory.

structure:Code.common:Name: Import of goods for inward processing
structure:Code.common:Description: Import of goods for the purpose of processing and re-exporting them.

structure:Code.common:Name: Import of goods after outward processing
structure:Code.common:Description: Import of goods that were sent abroad for processing and then imported back.

structure:Code.common:Name: Intra-firm imports
structure:Code.common:Description: Imports of goods or services between different branches of the same multinational company.

structure:Code.common:Name: Imports of goods
structure:Code.common:Description: Imports of goods are recorded at the time when they enter the economic territory of a country.

structure:Code.common:Name: Imports of goods (customs basis)
structure:Code.common:Description: The total value of goods bought by a country from foreign sellers, measured at the customs border.

structure:Code.common:Name: Imports of goods and services
structure:Code.common:Description: Imports of goods and services reflect the change in the economic ownership of goods from non-residents to residents of the compiling economy, irrespective of physical movement of goods across national borders. Imports of services reflect services provided by non-residents to residents

structure:Code.common:Name: Imports of services
structure:Code.common:Description: The total value of services bought by a country from foreign sellers.

structure:Code.common:Name: Trade balance goods
structure:Code.common:Description: The difference between the value of a country's exports and imports of goods and services.

structure:Code.common:Name: Oil trade balance
structure:Code.common:Description: The difference between the value of a country's exports and imports of oil and oil-related products.

structure:Code.common:Name: Three component-based goods trade imports
structure:Code.common:Description: Three component-based goods trade imports

structure:Code.common:Name: Three component-based goods trade exports
structure:Code.common:Description: Three component-based goods trade exports

structure:Code.common:Name: Total exports
structure:Code.common:Description: Total exports reflects the change in the economic ownership of products from residents of the compiling economy to non-residents, irrespective of physical movement of goods across national borders.

structure:Code.common:Name: Exports
structure:Code.common:Description: Exports of goods are recorded at the time when they leave the economic territory of a country.

structure:Code.common:Name: Exports of manufactures
structure:Code.common:Description: The total value of manufactured goods sold by a country to foreign buyers.

structure:Code.common:Name: Exports and imports
structure:Code.common:Description: The total value of goods and services exported and imported by a country.

structure:Code.common:Name: Exports of non-oil related products
structure:Code.common:Description: The total value of non-oil-related products sold by a country to foreign buyers.

structure:Code.common:Name: Exports of oil related products
structure:Code.common:Description: The total value of oil-related products sold by a country to foreign buyers.

structure:Code.common:Name: Re-exports
structure:Code.common:Description: Re-exports are goods produced in other economies, and previously imported, that are exported with no substantial transformation from the state in which they were previously imported.

structure:Code.common:Name: Re-exports (customs basis)
structure:Code.common:Description: Re-exports are goods produced in other economies, and previously imported, that are exported with no substantial transformation from the state in which they were previously imported, measured on a customs basis.

structure:Code.common:Name: Export of goods after inward processing
structure:Code.common:Description: Export of goods that have been imported, processed, and then exported.

structure:Code.common:Name: Export of goods for outward processing
structure:Code.common:Description: Export of goods sent abroad for processing and then returned or further traded.

structure:Code.common:Name: Intra-firm exports
structure:Code.common:Description: Exports of goods or services between different branches of the same multinational company.

structure:Code.common:Name: Crude oil exports
structure:Code.common:Description: The total value of crude oil sold by a country to foreign buyers.

structure:Code.common:Name: Exports of goods
structure:Code.common:Description: Exports of goods are recorded at the time when they leave the economic territory of a country.

structure:Code.common:Name: Exports of goods (customs basis)
structure:Code.common:Description: The total value of goods sold by a country to foreign buyers, measured at the customs border.

structure:Code.common:Name: Exports of goods and services
structure:Code.common:Description: Exports of goods and services reflect the export of goods reflect changes in the economic ownership of goods from residents of the compiling economy to non-residents, irrespective of physical movement of goods across national borders. Exports of services provided by residents to non-residents.

structure:Code.common:Name: Exports and imports of goods
structure:Code.common:Description: The combined total value of all goods exported and imported by a country.

structure:Code.common:Name: Exports and imports of goods and services
structure:Code.common:Description: The combined total value of all goods and services exported and imported by a country.

structure:Code.common:Name: Exports of services
structure:Code.common:Description: The total value of services sold by a country to foreign buyers.

structure:Code.common:Name: Imports of environmental goods
structure:Code.common:Description: Imports of environmental goods comprise all environmental goods entering the national territory. A relatively high share of environmental goods imports indicates that an economy purchases a significant share of environmental goods from other economies. Exports of environmental goods comprise all environmental goods leaving the national territory. A relatively high share of environmental goods exports indicates that an economy produces and sells a significant share of environmental goods to other economies. An economy’s environmental goods trade balance is the difference between its exports and imports of environmental goods.

structure:Code.common:Name: Quality of imported goods
structure:Code.common:Description: Quality of imported goods

structure:Code.common:Name: Imports of low carbon technology products
structure:Code.common:Description: Low carbon technology products produce less pollution than their traditional energy counterparts, and will play a vital role in the transition to a low carbon economy. Low carbon technologies include mechanics like wind turbines, solar panels, biomass systems and carbon capture equipment. Imports of low carbon technology products comprise all low carbon technology products entering the national territory.

structure:Code.common:Name: Trade balance in environmental goods
structure:Code.common:Description: Environmental goods include both goods connected to environmental protection—such as goods related to pollution management and resource management—and adapted goods—which are goods that have been specifically modified to be more “environmentally friendly” or “cleaner.” Imports of environmental goods comprise all environmental goods entering the national territory.

structure:Code.common:Name: Trade balance in low carbon technology products
structure:Code.common:Description: Low carbon technology products produce less pollution than their traditional energy counterparts, and will play a vital role in the transition to a low carbon economy. Low carbon technologies include mechanics like wind turbines, solar panels, biomass systems and carbon capture equipment. Imports of low carbon technology products comprise all low carbon technology products entering the national territory.

structure:Code.common:Name: Exports of industrial inputs
structure:Code.common:Description: Exports of industrial inputs

structure:Code.common:Name: Exports of refined petroleum products
structure:Code.common:Description: Exports of refined petroleum products

structure:Code.common:Name: Exports of environmental goods
structure:Code.common:Description: Environmental goods include both goods connected to environmental protection—such as goods related to pollution management and resource management—and adapted goods—which are goods that have been specifically modified to be more “environmentally friendly” or “cleaner.”

structure:Code.common:Name: Quality of exported goods
structure:Code.common:Description: Quality of exported goods

structure:Code.common:Name: Quality of exported goods index
structure:Code.common:Description: Quality of exported goods index

structure:Code.common:Name: Exports of low carbon technology products
structure:Code.common:Description: Low carbon technology products produce less pollution than their traditional energy counterparts, and will play a vital role in the transition to a low carbon economy. Low carbon technologies include mechanics like wind turbines, solar panels, biomass systems and carbon capture equipment. Imports of low carbon technology products comprise all low carbon technology products entering the national territory.

structure:Code.common:Name: Trade in environmental goods
structure:Code.common:Description: Environmental goods include both goods connected to environmental protection—such as goods related to pollution management and resource management—and adapted goods—which are goods that have been specifically modified to be more “environmentally friendly” or “cleaner.” Imports of environmental goods comprise all environmental goods entering the national territory.

structure:Code.common:Name: Trade in low carbon technology products
structure:Code.common:Description: Low carbon technology products produce less pollution than their traditional energy counterparts, and will play a vital role in the transition to a low carbon economy. Low carbon technologies include mechanics like wind turbines, solar panels, biomass systems and carbon capture equipment. Imports of low carbon technology products comprise all low carbon technology products entering the national territory. A relatively high share of low carbon technology products imports indicates that an economy purchases a significant share of low carbon technology products from other economies. Exports of low carbon technology products comprise all low carbon technology products leaving the national territory. A relatively high share of low carbon technology products exports indicates that an economy produces and sells a significant share of low carbon technology products to other economies. An economy’s trade balance in low carbon technology products is the difference between its exports and imports of low carbon technology products.

structure:Code.common:Name: Natural gas exports
structure:Code.common:Description: Natural gas exports.

structure:Codelist.common:Name: Index type
structure:Codelist.common:Description: This codelist represents different types of price indices and related measures.

structure:Code.common:Name: Bank stock index
structure:Code.common:Description: A financial index that tracks the performance of a basket of stocks issued by banking institutions. This index provides insights into the health and performance of the banking sector, reflecting changes in stock prices of banks in response to economic, regulatory, and market conditions.

structure:Code.common:Name: Core consumer price index (CPI)
structure:Code.common:Description: A measure of the price level of consumer goods and services, excluding volatile items such as food and energy.

structure:Code.common:Name: Commodity price index, energy, crude oil (petroleum)
structure:Code.common:Description: The Commodity Price Index for energy, crude oil (petroleum) is a measure that tracks the average price changes of crude oil over time.

structure:Code.common:Name: Commodity net export price index
structure:Code.common:Description: Represents the difference in the trends of export and import price indices for commodities. It is calculated by subtracting the Commodity Import Price Index from the Commodity Export Price Index. A positive value indicates that the prices of exports are increasing at a faster rate than the prices of imports, potentially leading to a favorable trade balance and contributing to economic growth.

structure:Code.common:Name: Commodity export price index
structure:Code.common:Description: A measure that tracks the changes over time in the prices of a basket of goods exported by a country. This index provides insight into the trends of export prices for commodities such as oil, metals, and agricultural products. An increase in the index suggests that the prices of exported commodities are rising, potentially leading to higher revenues for exporters.

structure:Code.common:Name: Core HICP inflation forecast
structure:Code.common:Description: The Core Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) Inflation Forecast predicts the future rate of inflation, excluding volatile items such as energy, food, alcohol, and tobacco. This forecast helps in assessing underlying inflation trends and is crucial for monetary policy decisions and economic planning.

structure:Code.common:Name: Commodity import price index
structure:Code.common:Description: This index measures the changes in the prices of a basket of goods imported into a country over time. It reflects the cost trends of imported commodities, including energy sources, raw materials, and food products. A higher index indicates increasing import prices, which may affect domestic inflation rates and the purchasing power of consumers, as well as impact the costs for businesses relying on imported goods.

structure:Code.common:Name: Core PCE Price Index
structure:Code.common:Description: The Core Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Price Index is a measure of inflation that tracks changes in the prices of goods and services purchased by consumers, excluding food and energy prices.

structure:Code.common:Name: Consumer price index (CPI)
structure:Code.common:Description: The Consumer Price Index (CPI) is an index of the prices of consumption goods and services, as compared to a certain reference period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Relative consumer price index (CPI)
structure:Code.common:Description: The CPI of the country compared to the trade-weighted CPI of the country’s trade partners

structure:Code.common:Name: Consumer price index (Urban)
structure:Code.common:Description: The Consumer Price Index (Urban), often abbreviated as CPI-U, is a key economic indicator that measures the average change over time in the prices paid by urban consumers for a fixed basket of goods and services.

structure:Code.common:Name: Commodity price index
structure:Code.common:Description: A commodity price index is a measurement tool that tracks the average price changes of a basket of commodities over time. These commodities can include various raw materials or primary agricultural products

structure:Code.common:Name: Deflator
structure:Code.common:Description: A measure used to adjust nominal values for inflation, reflecting the real value.

structure:Code.common:Name: Flexible exchange market pressure index
structure:Code.common:Description: Measures the pressure on a country's exchange rate in a flexible exchange rate system, taking into account factors such as changes in exchange rates, interest rates, and international reserves. It helps in identifying periods of excessive upward or downward pressure on the currency, indicating potential stability or vulnerability in the foreign exchange market. Calculated as one unit equivalent to one standard deviation of standarized variable.

structure:Code.common:Name: Export price index (XPI)
structure:Code.common:Description: An index that measures the price changes of goods and services sold to foreign buyers.

structure:Code.common:Name: Financial stress indicators
structure:Code.common:Description: Quantitative measures that signal the level of stress in the financial system. These indicators can include volatility in stock and bond markets, widening credit spreads, and increased interbank lending rates. They are used to identify periods of financial turbulence that could impact economic stability and inform policy responses. Calculated as the sum of standardized subcomponents.

structure:Code.common:Name: Herfindahl index
structure:Code.common:Description: A measure of market concentration and competition, calculated as the sum of the squares of the market shares of all firms in the market.

structure:Code.common:Name: Harmonised index of consumer prices (HICP)
structure:Code.common:Description: The Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) gives comparable measures of inflations for the countries and country groups for which it is produced. It is an economic indicator that measures the change over time of the prices of consumer goods and services acquired by households. In other words, it is a set of consumer price indexes (CPIs) calculated according to a harmonized approach and a set of definitions as laid down in Regulations and Recommendations. For example, the European Union's HICP provides the official measure of consumer price inflation in the euro area for the purposes of monetary policy and the assessment of inflation convergence as required under the Maastricht criteria for accession to the euro.

structure:Code.common:Name: Industrial production index (IPI)
structure:Code.common:Description: Industrial Production Index (IPI) is a monthly economic indicator that measures changes in the volume of output in the industrial sector, typically comprising manufacturing, mining, and utilities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Chain linked volume
structure:Code.common:Description: A volume measure that adjusts for changes in price levels over time by chaining together successive periods' volume measures.

structure:Code.common:Name: Chain linked volume (rebased)
structure:Code.common:Description: A chain linked volume measure that has been recalibrated to a new base period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Import price index
structure:Code.common:Description: An index that measures the price changes of goods and services purchased from foreign sellers.

structure:Code.common:Name: Nominal effective exchange rate (NEER)
structure:Code.common:Description: A nominal effective exchange rate (NEER) is a measure of the value of a currency against a weighted average of several foreign currencies. The weights are derived by taking a three-year average of the trade partners' combined value of imports and exports with the focal country as a share of the focal countries' total combined value of imports and exports.

structure:Code.common:Name: Price deflator
structure:Code.common:Description: An economic indicator used to adjust nominal economic data series for changes in relevant price levels. Price deflators can be explicit, such as producer or consumer price indices, or implicit, such as the GDP deflator derived by dividing nominal GDP by GDP in volume terms.

structure:Code.common:Name: Producer price index (PPI)
structure:Code.common:Description: The Producer Price Index (PPI) is a key economic indicator that measures the average change over time in the selling prices received by domestic producers for their output.

structure:Code.common:Name: Real effective exchange rate (REER)
structure:Code.common:Description: A real effective exchange rate (REER) is a measure of the value of a currency against a weighted average of several foreign currencies divided by a price deflator or index of costs. The weights are derived by taking a three-year average of the trade partners' combined value of imports and exports with the focal country as a share of the focal countries' total combined value of imports and exports. An increase in REER implies that exports become more expensive and imports become cheaper; therefore, an increase indicates a loss in trade competitiveness.

structure:Code.common:Name: Retail sales index
structure:Code.common:Description: The Retail Sales Index (RSI) measures the monthly performance of the retail sector by tracking changes in the value of sales at retail establishments. It is an important economic indicator that reflects consumer spending and retail sector health, providing insights into economic trends and consumer behavior.

structure:Code.common:Name: Financial price index
structure:Code.common:Description: A composite index that tracks the movement of financial asset prices, such as stocks, bonds, and other securities. It provides insights into the overall performance of financial markets and can signal shifts in investor sentiment, economic expectations, and market conditions. Calculated as one unit equivalent to one standard deviation of standarized variable.

structure:Code.common:Name: Stock returns
structure:Code.common:Description: Measures the profit or loss generated on an investment in a stock over a specific period. Stock returns can be calculated based on price appreciation (capital gains) and any dividends received, offering investors a comprehensive view of the performance and profitability of their stock investments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Theil index
structure:Code.common:Description: A Theil index can be interpreted as a measure of redundancy, lack of diversity, isolation, segregation, inequality, non-randomness, and compressibility. In the context of diversification, the higher the index the less diversification.

structure:Code.common:Name: Terms of trade (TOT)
structure:Code.common:Description: The ratio of export prices to import prices, indicating the relative value of imports in terms of exports.

structure:Code.common:Name: Volume index
structure:Code.common:Description: Index showing the average of the proportionate changes in quantities of a specified set of goods or services between two periods.

structure:Code.common:Name: Wholesale price index (WPI)
structure:Code.common:Description: The Wholesale Price Index (WPI) measures changes in the purchaser prices paid by non-household institutional units

structure:Code.common:Name: Price deflator (Eurostat)
structure:Code.common:Description: An economic indicator used to adjust nominal economic data series for changes in relevant price levels. Price deflators can be explicit, such as producer or consumer price indices, or implicit, such as the GDP deflator derived by dividing nominal GDP by GDP in volume terms.

structure:Code.common:Name: Unit value deflator
structure:Code.common:Description: A price index constructed by comparing the average price of a unit of goods or services in a given period to the average price of that same unit in a base period. UVDs are often used in international trade to analyze changes in export and import prices.

structure:Code.common:Name: Core producer price index (Core PPI)
structure:Code.common:Description: The Producer price index (PPI) is a key economic indicator that measures the average change over time in the selling prices received by domestic producers for their output.

structure:Code.common:Name: Purchasing managers index (PMI)
structure:Code.common:Description: The Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) is a monthly survey-based economic indicator measuring changes in key business conditions—such as production, new orders, and employment—across manufacturing and services, with readings above 50 indicating expansion and below 50 signaling contraction.

structure:Code.common:Name: Harmonised index of producer prices (HIPP)
structure:Code.common:Description: The Harmonised Index of Producer Prices (HICP) gives comparable measures of inflations for the countries and country groups for which it is produced. It is an economic indicator that measures the change over time of the prices of producer goods and services acquired by producers. In other words, it is a set of producer price indexes (CPIs) calculated according to a harmonized approach and a set of definitions as laid down in Regulations and Recommendations.

structure:Code.common:Name: Morgan Stanley MSCI stock price index
Terms of trade (TOT) Goods
structure:Code.common:Description: The ratio of export of goods prices to import of goods prices, indicating the relative value of imports of goods in terms of exports of goods.

structure:Code.common:Name: Price deflator (EUR)
structure:Code.common:Description: An economic indicator used to adjust nominal economic data series for changes in relevant price levels. Price deflators can be explicit, such as producer or consumer price indices, or implicit, such as the GDP deflator derived by dividing nominal GDP by GDP in volume terms. Derived by taking the current price series denominated in EUR divided by the constant price series denominated in EUR.

structure:Code.common:Name: Price deflator (USD)
structure:Code.common:Description: An economic indicator used to adjust nominal economic data series for changes in relevant price levels. Price deflators can be explicit, such as producer or consumer price indices, or implicit, such as the GDP deflator derived by dividing nominal GDP by GDP in volume terms. Derived by taking the current price series denominated in USD divided by the constant price series denominated in USD.

structure:Code.common:Name: Price deflator (SDR)
structure:Code.common:Description: An economic indicator used to adjust nominal economic data series for changes in relevant price levels. Price deflators can be explicit, such as producer or consumer price indices, or implicit, such as the GDP deflator derived by dividing nominal GDP by GDP in volume terms. Derived by taking the current price series denominated in SDR divided by the constant price series denominated in SDR.

structure:Code.common:Name: Production index
structure:Code.common:Description: Production Index is a indicator that measures changes in the volume of output in a sector, typically comprising manufacturing, mining, and utilities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Core inflation excluding food and energy
structure:Code.common:Description: Core inflation excluding food and energy.

structure:Code.common:Name: Core inflation including housing
structure:Code.common:Description: Core inflation including housing.

structure:Code.common:Name: Consumer price index (CPI) common reference period
structure:Code.common:Description: The Consumer Price Index (CPI) is an index of the prices of consumption goods and services, as compared to a certain reference period.

structure:Codelist.common:Name: Social Concepts
structure:Codelist.common:Description: This codelist represents a broad category encompassing various social indicators, such as tourism and labor concepts.

structure:Code.common:Name: Employed persons
structure:Code.common:Description: Persons above the age of 15 who were in paid employment or self-employment during a specified reference period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Employed persons index
structure:Code.common:Description: An index that measures the level of employed persons relative to a base period, providing a quantitative measure of employment trends.

structure:Code.common:Name: Labor force
structure:Code.common:Description: The sum of employed and unemployed persons in an economy, actively participating in the labor market.

structure:Code.common:Name: Tourist
structure:Code.common:Description: Persons traveling to and staying in places outside their usual environment for not more than one consecutive year for leisure, business, and other purposes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Tourist visitors index
structure:Code.common:Description: A numerical representation that measures the relative changes in the number of tourist visitors over time compared to a base period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Tourist visitors
structure:Code.common:Description: Individuals who engage in tourism activities, including travel and stay outside their usual environment for leisure, business, and other purposes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Unemployment rate
structure:Code.common:Description: The percentage of the labor force that is unemployed and actively seeking employment. It is calculated as the number of unemployed persons divided by the total labor force.

structure:Code.common:Name: Unemployed persons
structure:Code.common:Description: Persons of working age who are without work, are currently available for work, and are actively seeking employment.

structure:Code.common:Name: Wage rate
structure:Code.common:Description: A measure of the monetary compensation for labor services, typically expressed in terms of a fixed amount per hour, day, month, or other unit of time.

structure:Code.common:Name: Number of tourist visitors
structure:Code.common:Description: The total count of individuals participating in tourism activities within a specified period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Population
structure:Code.common:Description: The total number of people living in a specific area or country.

structure:Code.common:Name: Labor compensation
structure:Code.common:Description: The total remuneration, in cash or in kind, payable by employers to employees in return for work done.

structure:Code.common:Name: Employee compensation
structure:Code.common:Description: All payments made to employees, including wages, salaries, and benefits.

structure:Code.common:Name: Employed persons, based on natural rate of unemployment
structure:Code.common:Description: The number of people employed, adjusted to account for the natural rate of unemployment, which is the rate of unemployment expected in a healthy economy.

structure:Code.common:Name: Hourly compensation
structure:Code.common:Description: The amount of money paid to an employee for one hour of work.

structure:Code.common:Name: Labor share of national income
structure:Code.common:Description: The proportion of national income paid to labor, usually expressed as a percentage.

structure:Code.common:Name: Population ages 16 to 64
structure:Code.common:Description: The total number of people within the age range of 16 to 64, often considered the working-age population.

structure:Code.common:Name: Population aggregation
structure:Code.common:Description: The process of compiling data on the population from various sources to create a comprehensive dataset.

structure:Code.common:Name: Labor productivity
structure:Code.common:Description: A measure of economic performance that compares the amount of goods and services produced with the number of hours worked.

structure:Code.common:Name: Unit labor cost
structure:Code.common:Description: The average cost of labor per unit of output, calculated by dividing total labor costs by the number of units produced.

structure:Code.common:Name: Unemployment rate
structure:Code.common:Description: The percentage of the labor force that is unemployed and actively seeking employment.

structure:Code.common:Name: Natural rate of unemployment
structure:Code.common:Description: The rate of unemployment that is expected in a healthy economy due to normal labor market turnover.

structure:Code.common:Name: Health-related personal travel services
structure:Code.common:Description: Services related to travel for health purposes, including medical tourism and travel for medical treatment.

structure:Code.common:Name: Labor share of national income
structure:Code.common:Description: The portion of national income that is allocated to labor compensation.

structure:Code.common:Name: Average monthly earnings
structure:Code.common:Description: The average amount of money earned by workers per month.

structure:Code.common:Name: Average weekly earnings
structure:Code.common:Description: The average amount of money earned by workers per week.

structure:Code.common:Name: Wages
structure:Code.common:Description: Payments made to workers for their labor or services, typically on an hourly, daily, or piecework basis.

structure:Code.common:Name: Harmonized unemployment rate
structure:Code.common:Description: A standardized measure of unemployment that allows for comparison across different countries or regions.

structure:Code.common:Name: Hours worked per employee
structure:Code.common:Description: The total number of hours worked by an employee within a specific period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Poverty rate
structure:Code.common:Description: The percentage of the population living below the poverty line, often defined by income thresholds.

structure:Code.common:Name: Unit labor cost in US Dollars
structure:Code.common:Description: The average cost of labor per unit of output, calculated by dividing total labor costs by the number of units produced in US Dollars.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign Currency
structure:Code.common:Description: Currency used in a country other than one's own.

structure:Codelist.common:Name: Frequency
structure:Codelist.common:Description: This code list provides a set of values indicating the "frequency" of the data (e.g. weekly, monthly, quarterly). The concept “frequency” may refer to various stages in the production process, e.g. data collection or data dissemination. For example, a time series could be disseminated at annual frequency but the underlying data are compiled monthly. The code list is applicable for all different uses of "frequency". This code list was formally adopted on 4 December 2013. More information about and supporting material for this code list and SDMX code lists in general (e.g. list of generic codes for expressing general concepts like "Total", "Unknown", etc.; syntaxes for the creation of further codes; general guidelines for the creation of SDMX code lists) can be found at this address: https://sdmx.org/?page_id=4345.

structure:Code.common:Name: Trihourly
structure:Code.common:Description: To be used for data collected or disseminated every three hours.

structure:Code.common:Name: Daily – business week
structure:Code.common:Description: Similar to "daily", however there are no observations for Saturdays and Sundays (so, neither “missing values” nor “numeric values” should be provided for Saturday and Sunday)

structure:Code.common:Name: Minutely
structure:Code.common:Description: While N denotes "minutely", usually, there may be no observations every minute (for several series the frequency is usually "irregular" within a day/days). And though observations may be sparse (not collected or disseminated every minute), missing values do not need to be given for the minutes when no observations exist: in any case the time stamp determines when an observation is observed.

structure:Code.common:Name: Irregular
structure:Code.common:Description: To be used with irregular time series that stores data for a sequence of arbitrary timepoints. Irregular time series are appropriate when the data arrives unpredictably, such as when the application records every stock trade or when random events are recorded (the interval between each element can be a different length)

structure:Code.common:Name: Occasional annual
structure:Code.common:Description: The event occurs occasionally with an infrequent update that could span from 1 year to several years between events. It implies a survey that experiences a gap for several years prior to the next survey update (this is commonly linked to funding available to run a specific survey (i.e. health surveys), whereas a regular annual survey refers typically to ‘programs’ that are funded regularly and fall under the Statistics Act, and therefore never experience a gap)

structure:Code.common:Name: Occasional monthly
structure:Code.common:Description: The event occurs occasionally with an infrequent update that could span from 1 month to several months between events. It implies a survey that experiences a gap for several months prior to the next survey update.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other
structure:Code.common:Description: To be used when the qualitative or quantitative values that a variable takes in a data set is associated to multiple occurrences with frequency other than the already defined ones (for example every 5 hours and 32 minutes etc.)

structure:Code.common:Name: Unspecified
structure:Code.common:Description: To be used when a set of values are reported within a time range but not associated to sub ranges. Often this could happen in case of missing or sparse information. (Let’s say we have two observations for 2020 but we do not know if they are part of a monthly reporting or quarterly reporting)

structure:Code.common:Name: Not applicable
structure:Code.common:Description: To be used when the qualitative or quantitative values that a variable takes in a data set is not associated to multiple occurrences (only single occurrence exists) one can use the _Z as frequency.

structure:Codelist.common:Name: Access and Sharing Level
structure:Codelist.common:Description: This codelist defines the allowable levels of access and sharing for a particular data resource, specifying who can view, use, or distribute the data and under what conditions.

structure:Codelist.common:Name: Gender
structure:Codelist.common:Description: This codelist represents the spectrum of an individual's internal and individual experience of gender, which can be the same or different from their sex assigned at birth.

structure:Code.common:Name: Men
structure:Code.common:Description: An individual who defines themselves and lives as a male.

structure:Code.common:Name: Women
structure:Code.common:Description: An individual who defines themselves and lives as a female.

structure:Code.common:Name: Transgender men
structure:Code.common:Description: An individual who defines themselves and lives as a male, who was assigned female at birth.

structure:Code.common:Name: Transgender women
structure:Code.common:Description: An individual who defines themselves and lives as a female, who was assigned as male at birth.

structure:Code.common:Name: Cis men
structure:Code.common:Description: An individual who defines themselves and lives as a male, who was assigned male at birth.

structure:Code.common:Name: Cis women
structure:Code.common:Description: An individual who defines themselves and lives as a female, who was assigned female at birth.

structure:Code.common:Name: Non-binary
structure:Code.common:Description: An individual who defines themselves outside the binary of man or woman, and which may include various identities located at any point on the gender spectrum.

structure:Code.common:Name: Gender fluid
structure:Code.common:Description: An individual who does not have a fixed gender, and whose gender moves between different points on the gender spectrum. 3

structure:Code.common:Name: Gender non-conforming
structure:Code.common:Description: An individual who does not conform with the gender roles/norms/behaviours/expression expected from a given gender in a given society

structure:Code.common:Name: Agender / Gender neutral
structure:Code.common:Description: An individual who does not identify with any gender.

structure:Code.common:Name: Gender queer
structure:Code.common:Description: Genderqueer individuals typically reject notions of static categories of gender and embrace a fluidity of gender identity and often, though not always, sexual orientation. People who identify as "genderqueer" may see themselves as being both male and female, neither male nor female or as falling completely outside these categories.”

structure:Code.common:Name: Indigenous gender-variant identities
structure:Code.common:Description: Individuals from indigenous communities who define themselves in a range of identities on the gender continuum outside the western binary approach to gender. They often define their gender from a spiritual perspective and are seen/see themselves as being able to cross freely between male and female, or to exist in a state that is in between, or neither.

structure:Code.common:Name: Two-spirit
structure:Code.common:Description: Two-spirit spirit is also used to refer to the 2SLGBTQ+ community, as indigenous peoples reclaim their ancestral ways of respecting individuals who do not define themselves within the gender social construct of man and woman.

structure:Code.common:Name: Not applicable
structure:Code.common:Description: For cases where the concept of gender is not applicable.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other
structure:Code.common:Description: For individuals who do not define themselves as any of the available options.

structure:Codelist.common:Name: COICOP 2018
structure:Codelist.common:Description: This codelist represents an updated and expanded version of the COICOP classification system, designed to better reflect the evolving consumption patterns of the 21st century. It includes 14 divisions, 50 groups, 153 classes, and 449 subclasses.

structure:Code.common:Name: Food and non-alcoholic beverages
structure:Code.common:Description: Expenditures on food items intended for human consumption, excluding alcoholic beverages.

structure:Code.common:Name: Alcoholic beverages, tobacco and narcotics
structure:Code.common:Description: Expenditures on alcoholic beverages, tobacco products, and narcotic substances.

structure:Code.common:Name: Clothing and footwear
structure:Code.common:Description: Expenditures on garments, footwear, and accessories for personal use.

structure:Code.common:Name: Housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels
structure:Code.common:Description: Expenses related to housing, including rent, mortgage payments, utilities (water, electricity, gas), and fuels for heating.

structure:Code.common:Name: Furnishings, household equipment and routine household maintenance
structure:Code.common:Description: Expenditures on furniture, appliances, household tools, and routine maintenance and repair services for the home.

structure:Code.common:Name: Health
structure:Code.common:Description: Expenses related to medical and paramedical services, therapeutic appliances, and pharmaceutical products.

structure:Code.common:Name: Transport
structure:Code.common:Description: Expenditures on transportation services, including public transport fares, vehicle purchases, and fuel costs.

structure:Code.common:Name: Information and communication
structure:Code.common:Description: Spending on communication devices, internet access, postal services, and other information and communication technologies.

structure:Code.common:Name: Recreation, sport and culture
structure:Code.common:Description: Expenses on recreational activities, sports events, cultural events, hobbies, and leisure equipment.

structure:Code.common:Name: Education services
structure:Code.common:Description: Payments for educational services at all levels, including tuition fees.

structure:Code.common:Name: Restaurants and accomodation services
structure:Code.common:Description: Spending on meals and drinks at restaurants, cafes, and other food service establishments, as well as accommodation.

structure:Code.common:Name: Insurance and financial services
structure:Code.common:Description: Expenses related to insurance premiums and financial services, such as bank charges and investment fees.

structure:Code.common:Name: Personal care, social protection and miscellaneous goods and services
structure:Code.common:Description: A wide range of expenditures, including personal care products, social services, and other miscellaneous items.

structure:Code.common:Name: Individual consumption expenditure of non-profit institutions serving households (NPISHS)
structure:Code.common:Description: Expenditures by non-profit institutions on behalf of households.

structure:Code.common:Name: Individual consumption expenditure of general government
structure:Code.common:Description: Expenditures by the government on goods and services for individual consumption.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total
structure:Code.common:Description: The total sum of all individual consumption expenditures across all categories.

structure:Code.common:Description: This is a country grouping established by the World Bank's classification of countries in fragile and conflict-affected situations. The list consists of (i) countries with high levels of institutional and social fragility and (ii) countries affected by violent conflict, using indicators and thresholds assessed by the World Bank. It is updated annually and available publicly. Under the new IMF strategy for Fragile and Conflicted States (FCS), the Fund has adopted the methodology, thresholds, and criteria of the World Bank's Fragility and Conflict Situations for the IMF Fragile and Conflicted States. This is explained in the FCS Strategy Board paper: The IMF Strategy for Fragile and Conflict-Affected States (March 14, 2022, p. 21-22).
